segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Abraham, the Prophet, peace be upon him, never lied except three times: twice for the sake of Allah, [namely] his saying, 'Indeed, I am sick,'

and his saying, 'Rather, it was their chief, this one, who did it.' And once concerning Sarah. He arrived in the land of a tyrant, and Sarah was with him, and she was the most beautiful of people. So he said to her, 'If this tyrant learns that you are my wife, he will take you from me by force. So if he asks you, tell him that you are my sister, for you are my sister in Islam, since I know of no Muslim on earth besides me and you.' When he entered the tyrant's land, some of the tyrant's people saw her and came to him and said, 'A woman has come to your land who should belong only to you.'

So he sent for her, and she was brought. Abraham, peace be upon him, stood to pray. When she came in to the tyrant, he could not restrain himself from stretching out his hand to her, but his hand was seized with a severe seizure. He said to her, 'Pray to Allah to release my hand, and I will not harm you.'

She did so, but he went back to it, and his hand was seized more tightly than the first time. He said the same to her, and she did so, but he went back to it, and he was seized more tightly than the previous two times. He said, 'Pray to Allah to release my hand, and I swear by Allah that I will not harm you.'

She did so, and his hand was released. Then he called the one who had brought her and said to him, 'You have only brought me a devil, and you have not brought me a human being. Take her out of my land and give her Hagar.'

[Abū Hurayrah] said: So she came walking back. When Abraham, peace be upon him, saw her, he turned away [from his prayer] and said to her, 'What happened?' She said, 'Good. Allah restrained the hand of the wicked one and gave me a servant.'
Abū Hurayrah said: "That is your mother, O sons of the water of the sky."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on Lot; he used to take refuge in a strong support."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people camped with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the land of Thamūd, al-Ḥijr.
They drew water from its well and kneaded dough with it.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them to pour out what they had drawn from its well,
and to feed the dough to the camels.
And he commanded them to draw water from the well that the she-camel used to come to.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who mentioned several hadith, among them; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Were it not for the Children of Israel, food would not have spoiled and meat would not have rotted. And were it not for Eve, no woman would ever have betrayed her husband."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was named al-Khiḍr only because he sat on a white barren patch of ground, and it suddenly stirred with green behind him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ at Marr al-Ẓahrān, picking the fruit of the arāk tree, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Take the black ones from it."
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is as if you have tended sheep." He said:
"Yes. Was there any prophet who did not tend them?"
Or words to that effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"There is no child of Adam born but that Satan touches him when he is born,
and he cries out loudly from the touch of Satan,
except Mary and her son."
Then Abū Hurayrah would say: "'And indeed, I seek refuge for her in You, and for her descendants, from Satan, the accursed.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ proposed marriage to Umm Hāniʾ, daughter of Abū Ṭālib, and she said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have grown old and I have children."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of women who have ridden camels..."
Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Yūnus, except that he said:
"...the most tender toward a child in his early years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that Jesus is the servant of Allah, the son of His maidservant, and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is true and the Fire is true,' Allah will admit him through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise he wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you are three, two should not converse privately to the exclusion of their companion."
And Sufyān said in his narration:
"Two should not converse privately to the exclusion of the third, for that would grieve him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In one narration, and once he said, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ:
"Do not leave a fire burning in your houses when you go to sleep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every prophet has a supplication that he makes, and I wish, if Allah wills, to keep my supplication in reserve as intercession for my nation on the Day of Resurrection."
Kaʿb said to Abū Hurayrah, "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Abū Hurayrah said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to his bed, he would lie on his right side, then say:
"O Allah, I have submitted myself to You,
and turned my face to You,
and entrusted my affair to You,
and rested my back upon You,
out of longing and fear of You.
There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You.
I believe in Your Book which You have revealed,
and in Your Prophet whom You have sent."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever says these words and then dies during that night, dies upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah)."
{They struck them with awe} is from rahbah (fear).
Malakūt means kingship, like rahbūt and raḥmūt: rahbūt is better than raḥmūt;
you say: to be feared is better than to be shown mercy.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bashshār and ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd (the wording is Ibn Saʿīd's) said: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatādah,
from Abū al-ʿĀliyah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say in times of distress:

"There is no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; Glory be to Allah, the Almighty."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"The heart of an old man remains young in the love of two things: love of life and wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The son of Ādam grows old, while two things remain young in him: the craving for wealth and the craving for long life."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wealth is not in having abundant possessions,
but true wealth is the wealth of the soul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The bedding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on which he slept was made of tanned leather stuffed with palm fibre.
label: machine translation

segments_en: People are like a hundred camels, among which you can hardly find a single one fit for riding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn al-Qāsim, Mālik narrated to me,
and a transition: Qutaybah informed us,
he said: al-Mughīrah narrated to us,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah the Exalted said: When My servant loves to meet Me, I love to meet him; and when he dislikes meeting Me, I dislike meeting him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Three things follow the dead person;
two return and one remains with him.
His family, his wealth and his deeds follow him;
his family and his wealth return, and his deeds remain."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will people be gathered on the Day of Resurrection?" He said, "Barefoot and naked."
I said, "And the women?" He said, "And the women."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will they not be ashamed?" He said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, the matter will be too severe for them to look at one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ in a tent, and he said:
"Would you be pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?" We said, "Yes." He said:
"Would you be pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise?" We said, "Yes." He said:
"Would you be pleased to be half of the people of Paradise?" We said, "Yes." He said:
"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise,
for none will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul,
and you, among the people of polytheism, are only like a white hair on the skin of a black ox, or like a black hair on the skin of a red ox."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the ʿAṣr prayer one day while it was still daytime. Then he stood up to deliver a sermon, and he left nothing that would occur until the Hour is established except that he told us of it; whoever remembered it remembered it, and whoever forgot it forgot it. And among what he said was:
"Indeed, the world is sweet and green, and Allah is appointing you as successors in it, so He will see how you act. Beware, then, of the world, and beware of women."
And among what he said was:
"Beware! Let no man's fear of people prevent him from speaking the truth when he knows it."
He said: Then Abū Saʿīd wept and said, "By Allah, we have seen things and we held back out of fear."
And among what he said was:

"Beware! A banner will be set up for every treacherous person on the Day of Resurrection in proportion to his treachery, and there is no treachery greater than the treachery of a leader of the common people, whose banner will be planted at his backside."
And among what we memorized that day was:

"Beware! The children of Adam were created in various classes. Among them are those who are born believers, live as believers, and die as believers; and among them are those who are born disbelievers, live as disbelievers, and die as disbelievers; and among them are those who are born believers, live as believers, and die as disbelievers; and among them are those who are born disbelievers, live as disbelievers, and die as believers. Beware! Among them are those who are slow to anger and quick to calm down, and among them are those who are quick to anger and quick to calm down, so the one offsets the other. Beware! Among them are those who are quick to anger and slow to calm down. Beware! The best of them is the one slow to anger and quick to calm down. Beware! The worst of them is the one quick to anger and slow to calm down. Beware! Among them are those who are good in repaying and good in demanding, and among them are those who are bad in repaying but good in demanding, and among them are those who are good in repaying but bad in demanding, so the one offsets the other. Beware! Among them are those who are bad in repaying and bad in demanding. Beware! The best of them is the one good in repaying and good in demanding. Beware! The worst of them is the one bad in repaying and bad in demanding. Beware! Anger is an ember in the heart of the son of Adam. Have you not seen the redness of his eyes and the swelling of his veins? So whoever feels any of that, let him cling to the ground."
He said: And we began looking toward the sun to see whether any of it remained, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beware! What remains of the world compared to what has passed of it is only like what remains of this day of yours compared to what has passed of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Egypt said: I asked Abū al-Dardāʾ about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

"For them are good tidings in the life of this world." He said: No one has asked me about it except one man, since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"No one has asked me about it other than you since it was revealed. It is the good dream, which the Muslim sees or which is seen for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The testimony of a treacherous man or woman is not permissible, nor that of one who has been flogged for a prescribed punishment, man or woman, nor that of one who harbors rancor against his brother, nor that of one known for false testimony, nor that of a dependent of a household [testifying] for them, nor that of one suspected regarding allegiance or kinship."
Al-Fazārī said: The dependent is the follower.
This is a gharīb ḥadīth; we do not know it except from the narration of Yazīd ibn Ziyād al-Dimashqī.
Yazīd is considered weak in ḥadīth, and this ḥadīth is not known from al-Zuhrī except through his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him."
He said: This is a gharīb ḥadīth; we do not know it from the narration of Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of standing passed by him, and ʿAlqamah said to him: You have kinship with me and a right over me, and I have seen you enter upon these rulers and speak before them whatever Allah wills you to speak. And I heard Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, one of you may speak a word pleasing to Allah, not thinking that it will reach as far as it does, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will record His pleasure for him because of it until the Day he meets Him. And indeed, one of you may speak a word displeasing to Allah, not thinking that it will reach as far as it does, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will record His displeasure against him because of it until the Day he meets Him."
ʿAlqamah said: So look, woe to you, at what you say and what you speak, for many a word I was prevented from speaking because of what I heard from Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is not one of us who imitates others. Do not imitate the Jews or the Christians, for the Jews' greeting is a gesture with the fingers, and the Christians' greeting is a gesture with the palms."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed through the mosque one day while a group of women were sitting, and he waved his hand in greeting. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd gestured with his hand [to demonstrate].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Greeting comes before speech."
And with this chain of transmission, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"Do not invite anyone to eat until he has given the greeting of peace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a gathering that included a mixture of Muslims and Jews, and he greeted them with peace.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever lifts a curtain and puts his gaze into a house before being given permission, and sees the private parts of its people, has committed an act that is not lawful for him to commit. If a man had met him just as he put his gaze in and poked out his eyes, I would not have objected to it. And if a man passes by a door that has no curtain and is not closed, and he looks, there is no sin on him; the sin is only on the people of the house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was in his house when a man peered in at him, so he went toward him with a broad arrowhead, and the man drew back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade them from coming to their womenfolk at night [on returning from a journey].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you writes a letter, let him dust it with earth, for that is more effective for the need."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a scribe in front of him, and I heard him say:
"Put the pen on your ear, for that helps the one dictating to remember."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "ʿAlayka as-salām." He said:
"Do not say 'ʿalayka as-salām,' but say 'as-salāmu ʿalayka.'"
And he mentioned a long story. This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He did not hear it from him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by some people of the Anṣār who were sitting in the road, and he said:
"If you must do so, then return the greeting, help the wronged, and guide people to the way."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us meets his brother or friend, should he bow to him?" He said, "No."
He said, "Should he embrace him and kiss him?" He said, "No."
He said, "Should he take his hand and shake it?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the completion of the greeting is taking the hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The completion of visiting the sick is that one of you places his hand on his forehead, or he said on his hand, and asks him how he is. And the completion of your greetings among yourselves is shaking hands."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Ḥārithah came to Medina while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house. He came and knocked on the door, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up and went to him, uncovered, dragging his garment. By Allah, I never saw him uncovered before or after that. He embraced him and kissed him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day I came to him:
"Welcome to the rider who has made hijrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
sneezed beside Ibn ʿUmar and said, "Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah."

Ibn ʿUmar said, "I too say, 'Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah,' but this is not how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught us. He taught us to say, 'Praise be to Allah in every circumstance.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: This hadith is similar to the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd. Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥakam al-Baṣrī narrated it to us:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us,
from ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār, with this [chain].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Sneezing is from Allah and yawning is from Satan. So when one of you yawns, let him put his hand over his mouth, and when he says 'ah, ah,' Satan laughs at him from inside. Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning. So when a man says 'ah, ah' when he yawns, Satan laughs inside him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sneezing, drowsiness, and yawning during prayer, menstruation, vomiting, and nosebleed are from Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man has more right to his seat, and if he leaves for some need and then returns, he is still more entitled to his seat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was no person dearer to them than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Yet when they saw him they would not stand, because they knew he disliked that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah came out, and ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn Ṣafwān stood up when they saw him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no man who forsakes a Muslim in a place where his sanctity is violated and his honor is diminished, except that Allah will forsake him in a situation where he would love for Him to help him. And there is no man who helps a Muslim in a place where his honor is diminished and his sanctity is violated, except that Allah will help him in a situation where he would love for Him to help him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came and made his camel kneel, then tied it, then entered the mosque and prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he went to his camel, untied it, then mounted and called out: "O Allah, have mercy on me and Muḥammad, and do not include anyone else in our mercy."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you say he is more astray, or his camel? Did you not hear what he said?" They said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Is any of you unable to be
like Abū Ḍayghm — or Ḍamḍam, Ibn ʿUbayd was unsure — who, when he woke in the morning, would say: "O Allah, I have given my honor in charity to Your servants."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you pursue the faults of the people, you will corrupt them, or you will almost corrupt them."
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: A word that Muʿāwiyah heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, by which Allah the Exalted benefited him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a ruler seeks suspicion among the people, he corrupts them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Masʿūd was brought a man, and it was said, "This is so-and-so, his beard is dripping with wine." ʿAbd Allāh said, "We have been forbidden to spy, but if something becomes apparent to us, we will take him to account for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever sees a fault and conceals it is like one who revives a girl buried alive."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The scribe of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir said: We had neighbors who drank wine. I forbade them but they did not stop, so I said to ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, "These neighbors of ours drink wine, and I forbade them but they did not stop, so I am going to call the police on them." He said, "Leave them."
Then I returned to ʿUqbah another time and said, "Our neighbors have refused to stop drinking wine, and I am going to call the police on them."
He said, "Woe to you, leave them, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say..." and he mentioned a meaning similar to the hadith of Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting with his Companions, a man began to abuse Abū Bakr and harmed him, but Abū Bakr remained silent. Then he harmed him a second time, and Abū Bakr remained silent. Then he harmed him a third time, and Abū Bakr defended himself against him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up when Abū Bakr defended himself. Abū Bakr said, "Were you angry with me, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"An angel came down from heaven, denying what he said to you. But when you defended yourself, Satan came in, and I would not sit when Satan came in."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to ask about defending oneself,

{And whoever defends himself after having been wronged, those have no blame upon them}. ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān narrated to me from Umm Muḥammad, the wife of his father. Ibn ʿAwn said: They claimed that she used to visit the Mother of the Believers. She said: The Mother of the Believers said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while Zaynab bint Jaḥsh was with us. He began to do something with his hand, so I gestured with my hand until I made her aware of it, and he held back. Zaynab began to rush at ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and he forbade her, but she refused to stop. So he said to ʿĀʾishah, "Insult her."
So she insulted her and got the better of her. Zaynab went to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and said, "ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, has attacked you and did such and such."
Then Fāṭimah came, and he said to her:
"She is the beloved of your father, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah."
So she left and told them, "I said such and such to him, and he said such and such to me."
He said: And ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke to him about that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When your companion dies, leave him; do not speak ill of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, may Allah be pleased with him, who was one of those who wrote down the revelation, said: Abū Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of Yamāmah, and ʿUmar was with him.
Abū Bakr said: ʿUmar has come to me and said, "The killing has become intense among the people on the day of Yamāmah,
and I fear that the killing will become intense among the reciters [of the Qur'an] in other places, and much of the Qur'an will be lost,
unless you collect it.
And I think you should collect the Qur'an."
Abū Bakr said: I said to ʿUmar, "How can I do something that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do?" ʿUmar said, "By Allah, it is good."
ʿUmar kept going back to me about it until Allah opened my heart to it,
and I came to see what ʿUmar saw.
Zayd ibn Thābit said: And ʿUmar was sitting with him, not speaking.
Abū Bakr said: You are a young and intelligent man, and we do not suspect you.
You used to write down the revelation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so seek out the Qur'an and collect it.

By Allah, if he had burdened me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me regarding the collection of the Qur'an. I said, "How can you two do something that the Prophet ﷺ did not do?" Abū Bakr said, "By Allah, it is good."
I kept going back to him until Allah opened my heart to that for which Allah had opened the hearts of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
So I set out and sought the Qur'an, collecting it from scraps of parchment, shoulder blades, palm stalks, and the memories of men,
until I found two verses of Sūrat at-Tawbah with Khuzaymah al-Anṣārī,

which I did not find with anyone else: "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer, [he is] concerned over you..." to the end of the two verses.
The sheets on which the Qur'an was collected remained with Abū Bakr until Allah took him,
then with ʿUmar until Allah took him,
then with Ḥafṣah, daughter of ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord" – he said: A group of humans used to worship a group of jinn, and the group of jinn accepted Islam.
But the humans held on to their worship, so it was revealed: "Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord." Bishr ibn Khālid also narrated it to me: Muḥammad informed us,
meaning Ibn Jaʿfar, from Shuʿbah, from Sulaymān, with this chain of transmission.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding the saying of the Almighty: "And do not recite your prayer aloud or silently," she said: This was revealed concerning supplication.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A huge, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection who will not weigh with Allah as much as the wing of a mosquito." And he said: Recite: "And We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight."
And from Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from Abū az-Zinād, the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white-and-black ram – Abū Kurayb added: and it will be made to stand between Paradise and the Fire – and they agreed on the rest of the hadith – and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will stretch their necks, look, and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' He said: And it will be said: 'O people of the Fire, do you recognize this?' He said: They will stretch their necks, look, and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' He said: Then it will be ordered, and it will be slaughtered. He said: Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity, no death! And O people of the Fire, eternity, no death!'"

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: "And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe," and he pointed with his hand toward the world.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah have mercy on the early emigrant women. When Allah revealed "and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests," they tore their thicker garments – Ibn Ṣāliḥ said: their heavier garments – and covered themselves with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said: O Messenger of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "
Is the One who made him walk on his feet in the world not able to make him walk on his face on the Day of Resurrection?"
Qatādah said: Yes, by the might of our Lord!
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: Five matters have already passed: the smoke, the moon, the Romans, the seizure, and the inevitable punishment: "So it is going to be inevitable."
label: machine translation

segments_en: This verse was revealed:

"And you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people" concerning Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. Zayd came complaining, and he intended to divorce her, so he consulted the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Keep your wife for yourself and fear Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: {And spend in the cause of Allah, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction}. He said: It was revealed concerning spending.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man may circumambulate the House, remaining in a lawful state, until he enters ihrām for Hajj.
Then when he sets out for ʿArafah, whoever can afford a sacrificial animal of camels, cattle or sheep,
whatever he can afford of these, whichever he wishes,
but if he cannot afford it, then he must fast three days during Hajj,
and that is before the Day of ʿArafah.
If the last of the three days is the Day of ʿArafah, there is no blame on him.
Then let him proceed until he stands at ʿArafāt from the ʿAṣr prayer until darkness comes.
Then let them depart from ʿArafāt, when they pour forth from it, until they reach Jamʿ, where they spend the night,
and then let them remember Allah often,
or say takbīr and tahlīl abundantly before you enter the morning; then pour forth,
for the people used to pour forth,
and Allah the Exalted said: {Then pour forth from where the people pour forth, and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful}, until you throw the pebbles at the Jamrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, [read]: {Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied} with the lighter pronunciation,
and he took it in that sense,

and he recited: {Until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When will the help of Allah come?" Indeed, the help of Allah is near}. Then I met ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and mentioned that to him. He said, "ʿĀʾishah said: Allah forbid!
By Allah, Allah never promised His Messenger anything except that he knew it would come to pass before he died,
but trials continued to afflict the messengers until they feared that those with them would deny them,"
so she used to read it: {and thought that they had been denied} with the heavier pronunciation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a sister who was being proposed to.
And Ibrāhīm said, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan:
Maʿqil ibn Yasār narrated to me
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn al-Zubayr said: I said to ʿUthmān, "This verse in Sūrat al-Baqarah, {And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind} up to His saying {without expulsion}, has been abrogated by the other,
so why do you write it?" He said, "Leave it,
O son of my brother. I will not change anything of it from its place."
Ḥumayd said: or something like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is reported, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"When Allah decrees a matter in the heavens, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, like a chain [striking] upon a smooth rock. ʿAlī said: and others said: [a smooth rock] — it penetrates them. Then, when fear is removed from their hearts, they say: 'What did your Lord say?'
They say to the one who asked: 'The truth. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.'
Then those who steal a hearing hear it,
and those who steal a hearing are like this, one above another"—and Sufyān described it with his hand,
spreading apart the fingers of his right hand,
and setting them upright, one above another—"Sometimes a flaming meteor strikes the listener
before he can pass it on to his companion,

and burns him; and sometimes it does not reach him until he has passed it on to the one beneath him, and then to the one beneath him, until they cast it down to the earth"—and Sufyān may have said: "until it reaches the earth—and it is cast into the mouth of the sorcerer.
He then adds a hundred lies to it, and [what he said] turns out true.
Then people say: 'Did he not tell us that on such and such a day, such and such would happen,
and we found it to be true, because of the word that was heard from the heavens?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl used to say to a slave girl of his, "Go and earn something for us." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, in order to seek the goods of worldly life. And whoever compels them, then indeed, after their compulsion, Allah is [to them] Forgiving and Merciful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer. He recited {Qāf. By the Glorious Qur'an}, until he recited {and the tall palm trees}. He said: I kept repeating it, and I did not understand what he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite {Qāf. By the Glorious Qur'an} in the dawn prayer, and his prayer after that was shorter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir ibn Samurah about the prayer of the Prophet
ﷺ. He said: He used to keep the prayer short, and he did not pray the prayer of these people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High} in the noon prayer, and in the morning prayer a longer [passage] than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would hear the crying of a child with its mother while he was in prayer, and he would recite a short sūrah or a brief sūrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man, whom he named, gained control of Kufa in the time of Ibn al-Ashʿath, and he ordered Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh to lead the people in prayer. He would pray, and when he raised his head from bowing he would stand for about the time it takes me to say: O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth and filling whatever You will beyond that, O Possessor of praise and glory. None can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and the might of the mighty cannot benefit him against You.

Al-Ḥakam said: I mentioned that to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, and he said: I heard al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib say: The prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his bowing, his rising from bowing, his prostration, and the time between the two prostrations were nearly equal.
Shuʿbah said: I mentioned it to ʿAmr ibn Murrah, and he said: I saw Ibn Abī Laylā, and his prayer was not like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maṭar ibn Nājiyah,
when he gained control of Kufa, ordered Abū ʿUbaydah to lead the people in prayer. And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed the dawn prayer behind the Prophet ﷺ and heard him recite {So I swear by the retreating stars, that run and hide}. And none of us would bend his back until he had fully reached prostration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he did not mention [it] regarding prostration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say often:
"Glory be to Allah and with His praise; I seek forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him."
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I see you saying often: Glory be to Allah and with His praise; I seek forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him." He said:
"My Lord informed me that I would see a sign in my nation, and when I saw it I should say often: Glory be to Allah and with His praise; I seek forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him.

And I have seen it: {When the help of Allah and the conquest comes}, the conquest of Mecca, {and you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify the praises of your Lord and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you prostrate, place your palms down and raise your elbows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhrī,
with this chain of transmission. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ was praying at ʿArafah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I and a companion
of mine were discussing a hadith, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān said: I will tell you
what I heard from Abū Saʿīd and what I saw
of him. He said: While I was with Abū Saʿīd,

praying on Friday toward something that screened him from the people, a young man from the Banū Abī Muʿayṭ came and wanted to pass in front of him. Abū Saʿīd pushed him in the chest. The man looked and found no way except in front of Abū Saʿīd, so he returned, and Abū Saʿīd pushed him in the chest harder than the first push. He stood up, spoke ill of Abū Saʿīd, then pushed through the people and went out and entered upon Marwān and complained to him of what he had met. He said: Abū Saʿīd then entered upon Marwān, and Marwān said to him: What is the matter between you and your nephew? He has come complaining about you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He sent to Abū Juhaym al-Anṣārī [asking]: What did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say? Then he mentioned [a report] with the meaning of the hadith of Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he used to seek out the spot where the Qur'an copy was placed and would pray voluntary prayer there.
And he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek out that place, and it was between the pulpit and the qiblah, about the width of a sheep's passage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: What interrupts the prayer? He said: We said: A woman and a donkey.
She said: Indeed, woman is an evil beast! I remember myself lying across in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ like a funeral bier while he was praying.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he entered upon the Prophet ﷺ. He said: I saw him praying on a mat on which he prostrated. He said: And I saw him praying in a single garment, wrapped around himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last sūrah to be revealed in full was Barāʾah (at-Tawbah),
and the last verse to be revealed was the closing verse of Sūrat an-Nisāʾ: {They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning one who leaves no direct heirs (kalālah)}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Yemen have come to you.
They are softer in heart and gentler in spirit.
Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni.
Boastfulness and arrogance are among the owners of camels,
while tranquility and dignity are among the people of sheep and goats."
Ghundar said, from Shuʿbah, from Sulaymān: I heard Dhakwān,
from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ [the same].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: No one who performs ṭawāf around the House, whether a pilgrim or not, [does so] except that he is released from the state of iḥrām.

I said to ʿAṭāʾ: From where did he derive that? He said: From the saying of Allah, the Most High: {Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.} He said: I said: But that is after standing at ʿArafah.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: It is after ʿArafah and before it.
And he took that from the command of the Prophet ﷺ when he ordered them to come out of iḥrām during the Farewell Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ fought in nineteen military campaigns,
and after he migrated he performed only one Hajj, the Farewell Hajj; he performed no other Hajj after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"Time has come round to its original form, as on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive ones, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, Dhū al-Ḥijjah and Muḥarram, and Rajab of Muḍar, which is between Jumādā and Shaʿbān." Then he said: "Which month is this?"
We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He remained silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its own. Then he said:
"Is it not Dhū al-Ḥijjah?" We said: "Yes." He said:
"And which city is this?"
We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He remained silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its own. He said: "Is it not the [sacred] city?" We said: "Yes." He said:
"And which day is this?"
We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He remained silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its own. Then he said:
"Is it not the Day of Sacrifice?"
We said: "Yes, Messenger of Allah." He said:

"Indeed, your blood and your wealth—Muḥammad said: and I think he said—and your honour are sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this city of yours, in this month of yours. You will meet your Lord, and He will ask you about your deeds. So do not return after me as disbelievers—or astray—striking one another's necks. Let the one who is present convey [this] to the one who is absent, for perhaps some of those to whom it is conveyed will retain it better than some of those who heard it." Then he said:
"Have I not conveyed [the message]?"
Ibn Ḥabīb said in his narration: "and Rajab of Muḍar."
And in the narration of Abū Bakr:
"So do not return after me..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My companions sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ask him for mounts for them, when they were with him in the Army of Hardship—which is the expedition of Tabūk. I said: "O Prophet of Allah, my companions sent me to you so that you would provide them with mounts." He said:
"By Allah, I will not provide you with anything to ride."

I met him when he was angry, without realizing it. So I returned, saddened by the refusal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and fearing that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had become displeased with me. I went back to my companions and told them what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. I had waited only a short while when I heard Bilāl calling: "Where is ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays?"
I answered him, and he said: "Respond to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he is calling you."
When I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said:

"Take these two paired camels, and these two, and these two"—six camels that he had just bought from Saʿd—"and go with them to your companions and say: Allah—or he said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—provides you with these to ride, so ride them."

Abū Mūsā said: So I went to my companions with them and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ provides you with these to ride. But by Allah, I will not leave you until some of you go with me to someone who heard the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when I asked him for you, and his refusal the first time, and then his giving them to me afterward. Do not think that I have told you something he did not say."
They said to me: "By Allah, you are truthful in our eyes, and we will do whatever you wish."

So Abū Mūsā went with a group of them until they came to those who had heard the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his refusal of them and then his giving to them afterward. They told them exactly what Abū Mūsā had told them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due on it, but that on the Day of Resurrection plates of fire will be beaten out for him and heated in the fire of Hell, and his side, his forehead, and his back will be branded with them. Whenever they cool, they will be restored for him, during a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the servants and he sees his way, either to Paradise or to the Fire."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about camels?" He said:

"Nor is there an owner of camels who does not pay what is due on them—and part of what is due on them is milking them on the day they come to water—but that on the Day of Resurrection he will be laid out for them on a wide, level plain, and they will be at their fullest; not one of their young will be missing. They will trample him with their hooves and bite him with their mouths. Whenever the first of them has passed over him, the last of them will be sent back to him, during a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the servants and he sees his way, either to Paradise or to the Fire."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about cattle and sheep?" He said:

"Nor is there an owner of cattle or sheep who does not pay what is due on them, but that on the Day of Resurrection he will be laid out for them on a wide, level plain; not one of them will be missing, and none among them will be with twisted horns, or hornless, or with broken horns. They will gore him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. Whenever the first of them has passed over him, the last of them will be sent back to him, during a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the servants and he sees his way, either to Paradise or to the Fire."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about horses?" He said:

"Horses are of three kinds: for one man they are a burden, for another a covering, and for another a reward. As for the one for whom they are a burden, he is a man who keeps them for show, boasting, and hostility toward the people of Islam; so for him they are a burden. As for the one for whom they are a covering, he is a man who keeps them for the cause of Allah and then does not forget Allah's right in their backs and their necks; so for him they are a covering. As for the one for whom they are a reward, he is a man who keeps them for the cause of Allah, for the people of Islam, in a meadow or garden. Whatever they eat from that meadow or garden, there will be written for him good deeds equal to the number of what they ate, and good deeds equal to the number of their dung and urine. And whenever they break their tether and run one or two stretches, Allah will write for him good deeds equal to the number of their footprints and their dung. And whenever their owner passes with them by a river and they drink from it, even though he did not intend to water them, Allah will write for him good deeds equal to the number of what they drank."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about donkeys?" He said:

"Nothing has been revealed to me concerning donkeys except this unique, comprehensive verse: {So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was sitting
with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a woman came to him and said: "I gave a slave girl in charity to my mother, and she has died." He said:
"Your reward is secured, and the inheritance has returned her to you."
She said: "O Messenger of Allah, she owed a month of fasting. Should I fast on her behalf?" He said: "Fast on her behalf."
She said: "She never performed Hajj. Should I perform Hajj on her behalf?" He said: "Perform Hajj on her behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
both from Ibn ʿUyaynah
—ʿAmr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us—from ʿAmr,
that he heard Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim
narrating from his father,

Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who said: I lost a camel of mine, so I went out looking for it on the Day of ʿArafah. Then I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing with the people at ʿArafah. I said: "By Allah, this man is one of the Ḥums; what is he doing here?" And Quraysh were counted among the Ḥums.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn sent for me during the illness in which he died and said: "I was going to narrate to you some hadith, that perhaps Allah may benefit you through them after me. If I live, keep them hidden from me, and if I die, narrate them if you wish. I have been given greetings of peace. And know that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ combined Hajj and ʿUmrah, then no verse of the Book of Allah was revealed concerning it, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ did not forbid it.
A man said about it, by his own opinion, whatever he wished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ declared ihrām for ʿUmrah, and his Companions declared it for Hajj. The Prophet ﷺ did not come out of ihrām, nor did those of his Companions who had brought sacrificial animals, while the rest came out of it. Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh was among those who had brought sacrificial animals, so he did not come out of ihrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The wife] of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a girl in the house of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, with a dark mark on her face, and he said:
"She is under the effect of the evil eye, so seek ruqyah for her."
Meaning, there was a yellowish pallor on her face.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The evil eye is real."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ruqyah with this supplication:
"Remove the affliction, O Lord of the people. In Your hand is the cure; there is none who can remove it but You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to see dreams that made me ill. He said: Then I met Abū Qatādah, and he said: I too used to see dreams that made me ill, until I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"A good dream is from Allah. So if one of you sees what he likes, let him not tell it except to someone he loves. And if he sees what he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of Satan and the evil of the dream, and not tell it to anyone, for it will not harm him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no bad omen, and the best of it is the good omen."
He said: What is the good omen, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"The good word that one of you hears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about fortune-tellers, and he said: "They are nothing."
They said: O Messenger of Allah, sometimes they tell us something and it turns out to be true.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"That word is from the truth;
a jinn snatches it,
and drops it into the ear of his ally,
and they mix with it a hundred lies."
ʿAlī said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said it was mursal,
"the word from the truth."
Then it reached me that he later narrated it with a connected chain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no contagion, no bad omen, no ṣafar, and no hāmah."
A Bedouin said: What about camels that are in the sand as if they were gazelles, then a mangy camel mixes with them and gives them mange? He said:
"Then who gave the first one the mange?"
Maʿmar said: Al-Zuhrī said: A man narrated to me from Abū Hurayrah that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Let one with sick animals not bring them to those that are healthy."
He said: The man questioned him again, saying: Did you not narrate to us that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no contagion, no ṣafar, and no hāmah"?
He said: I did not narrate it to you.
Al-Zuhrī said: Abū Salamah said: He had narrated it, and I never heard that Abū Hurayrah forgot any hadith except this one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ, or he said Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ, said:
"While a man was walking in a fine garment,
pleased with himself, his hair combed,
Allah caused the earth to swallow him,
and he will keep sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of my nation will enter, seventy thousand of them, their faces shining like the moon on the night of the full moon."
Abū Hurayrah said: ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan al-Asadī stood up, lifting a striped cloak he was wearing, and said: O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, make him one of them."
Then a man from the Anṣār stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"ʿUkkāshah has beaten you to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wrapped in a Yemeni ḥibarah cloth, then it was taken off him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some garments were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among them a black khamīṣah, and he said:
"Whom do you think we should clothe with this khamīṣah?" The people were silent. He said:
"Bring me Umm Khālid."
So I was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he clothed me with it with his own hand and said: "Wear it out and wear it thin."
[He said it] twice. Then he began to look at the markings of the khamīṣah,
and pointing to me with his hand, he said:
"O Umm Khālid, this is sanā."
And sanā in the language of the Abyssinians means beautiful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Umm Sulaym gave birth, she said to me: O Anas, watch this boy, and let him not receive anything until you take him in the morning to the Prophet ﷺ so that he may perform taḥnīk for him. So I took him in the morning,
and he was in an orchard, wearing a Ḥurayth-style khamīṣah,
and he was branding the camels that had been brought to him at the Conquest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said concerning the captives of Badr:
"If al-Muṭʿim ibn ʿAdī were alive and then spoke to me about these filthy ones, I would release them to him."
Al-Layth said, from Yaḥyā,
from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab:
The first trial occurred—meaning the killing of ʿUthmān—and it left none of the people of Badr.

Then the second trial occurred—meaning [the battle of] al-Ḥarrah—and it left none of the people of al-Ḥudaybiyah. Then the third occurred, and it did not lift while the people still had any strength [or: any benefit].
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when some people from Banū Tamīm came to him, and he said:
"Receive the good news, O Banū Tamīm."
They said, "You have given us good news, so give us [something]."
Then some people from the people of Yemen entered, and he said:
"Receive the good news, O people of Yemen, since Banū Tamīm did not accept it." They said, "We accept.
We have come to you to gain understanding in the religion and to ask you about the beginning of this matter, how it was." He said:
"Allah existed and there was nothing before Him,
and His Throne was upon the water.
Then He created the heavens and the earth,
and wrote everything in the Remembrance."
Then a man came to me and said, "ʿImrān, go after your she-camel, for it has gone off." So I set out to look for it,
and the mirage was cutting off [my view] of it.
By Allah, I wish that it had gone and that I had not gotten up [to leave].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Jibrīl, peace be upon him, taught me to recite in one mode. I kept going back to him and asking for more, and he kept increasing it for me until it reached seven modes."
Ibn Shihāb said: It has reached me that these seven modes concern matters that are one and the same, in which there is no difference regarding what is lawful or unlawful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Nūḥ will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him, 'Did you convey [the message]?' He will say, 'Yes, my Lord.'
Then his nation will be asked, 'Did he convey it to you?' They will say, 'No warner came to us.'
He will say, 'Who are your witnesses?' He will say, 'Muḥammad and his nation.'
So you will be brought and you will testify."

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: {And thus We have made you a middle nation}—he said, "just"—{that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you.} And from Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn, who said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The noble son of the noble son of the noble son of the noble, Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, said: 'Had I stayed in prison as long as he stayed, and then the messenger had come to me, I would have responded.' Then he recited:
{So when the messenger came to him, he said, 'Return to your lord and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands'}." He said:
"And may Allah have mercy on Lūṭ. He used to take refuge in a strong support when he said:
{If only I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support}. After him Allah did not send a prophet except among the nobility of his people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade, on the day of Khaybar, the meat of every predator with a fang and every bird with a talon, the meat of domestic donkeys, the muthaththamah, and the khalīsah, and that pregnant women be had relations with until they give birth to what is in their wombs.
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: Abū ʿĀṣim was asked about the muthaththamah. He said: It is when a bird or some other animal is set up and then shot at.

And he was asked about the khalīsah, and he said: It is [an animal] that a wolf or a predator has seized, and a man catches up with it and takes it from the predator, and it dies in his hand before he can slaughter it properly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Laylā said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If a snake appears in a dwelling, say to it: 'We ask you by the covenant of Nūḥ and the covenant of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd that you not harm us.' If it returns, then kill it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to sacrifice two rams, one on behalf of the Prophet ﷺ and the other on behalf of himself.
He was asked about it, and he said: He—meaning the Prophet ﷺ—commanded me to do it, so I will never abandon it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I brought young sheep (jadhaʿ) to Madinah and they did not sell for me. I met Abū Hurayrah and asked him, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"What an excellent sacrificial animal is the jadhaʿ of sheep."
He said: Then the people rushed to buy them up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Madinah for ten years, offering the sacrifice [each year].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the ʿaqīqah for al-Ḥasan with a sheep and said:
"O Fāṭimah, shave his head and give in charity the weight of his hair in silver."
He said: So I weighed it, and it weighed one dirham or part of a dirham.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon, then came down and called for two rams and slaughtered them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A servant has no vow concerning what he does not own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: An army,

of the armies of the Muslims, whose commander was Salmān al-Fārisī, besieged one of the castles of Persia. They said: O Abū ʿAbdillāh, shall we not attack them? He said: Leave me to invite them as I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invite them.

So Salmān came to them and said to them: I am only a man from among you, a Persian. You see the Arabs obey me. If you accept Islam, you will have the same as we have and the same obligations as we have. If you refuse and insist on your religion, we will leave you upon it, and you will give us the jizyah out of hand while you are humbled.
He said: And he spoke to them in Persian: And you are not praised.
And if you refuse, we will declare an end to the treaty with you on equal terms.
They said: We are not the ones to pay the jizyah, rather we will fight you.
So they said: O Abū ʿAbdillāh, shall we not attack them? He said: No.
So he invited them for three days to the like of this, then he said: Attack them.
He said: So we attacked them and conquered that castle.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Khaybar with a group of the Ashʿarīs, and he gave us a share along with those who had conquered it.
This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb.
Some of the people of knowledge act upon this. Al-Awzāʿī said: Whoever joins the Muslims before shares are allotted for the horses is given a share.
And Burayd is given the kunyah Abū Burdah, and he is trustworthy; Sufyān al-Thawrī, Ibn ʿUyaynah and others narrated from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And his name is Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Hamdānī, and Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān; they both said: Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī narrated to us,
Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us,
from Sufyān ibn Saʿīd, from Hishām,
from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAlī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Jibrīl came down to him and said to him: Give them—meaning your Companions—a choice regarding the captives of Badr: execution, or ransom on condition that the same number of them be killed next year.
They said: Ransom, and some of us will be killed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ransomed two Muslim men in exchange for one man of the polytheists.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, our horsemen have trampled upon the women of the polytheists and their children. He said:
"They are from their fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that Khosrow sent him a gift and he accepted it from him, and that kings sent him gifts and he accepted them from them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh was struck by an arrow on the day of al-Aḥzāb, and they severed his vein (the akḥal or abjal). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cauterized it with fire, and his hand swelled, so he left it, and the blood flowed from him. He cauterized it again and his hand swelled. When he saw that, he said: O Allah, do not take my soul until my eyes are gratified regarding Banū Qurayẓah.

So his vein held, and not a drop dripped until they surrendered to the judgment of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh. He sent for him, and he judged that their men be killed and their women be spared, so that the Muslims could make use of them.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You have hit upon the judgment of Allah concerning them."
They were four hundred. When he had finished killing them, his vein burst open and he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For one of you to sit on a burning coal that burns his clothes until it reaches his skin is better for him than to sit on a grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not sit on graves, and do not pray facing them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the grave of his mother and wept, and made those around him weep. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I asked my Lord, the Exalted, for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but I was not given permission. Then I asked permission to visit her grave, and I was given permission. So visit graves, for they remind [you] of death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was in a gathering in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was present, and he said:
"I had forbidden you to eat the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days,
but now eat, feed others, and store [it] as you wish.
I had also told you not to prepare nabīdh in the gourds, the varnished jars, the hollowed palm trunks, and the green jars,
prepare nabīdh in whatever [containers] you see fit, and avoid every intoxicant.
I had also forbidden you to visit graves, but whoever wishes to visit, let him visit,
and do not speak falsehood [or improper words]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah mentioned: I heard al-Mundhir ibn Jarīr
narrating from his father, who said:

We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the early part of the day, when some people came, bare-footed and unclothed, wearing their swords, most of them from Muḍar, indeed all of them from Muḍar. The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed when he saw their poverty. He went in, then came out, and ordered Bilāl, who called the adhān and then the iqāmah for prayer. He prayed, then delivered a sermon and said:

"{O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed Allah is ever, over you, an Observer} and {Fear Allah, and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow.} Let a man give charity from his dinar, from his dirham, from his clothing, from his ṣāʿ of wheat, from his ṣāʿ of dates," until he said, "even if it is [only] half a date."

Then a man from the Anṣār came with a purse that his hand could barely carry, indeed it was too heavy for it. Then the people followed one after another until I saw two heaps of food and clothing, and I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shining as though it were gilded. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it, without any decrease in their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, without any decrease in their burdens."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: "He informed us," and the others said: "Ismāʿīl narrated to us,"
who is Ibn Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad,
who is Ibn Abī Ḥarmalah, from Kurayb,
that Umm al-Faḍl bint al-Ḥārith

sent him to Muʿāwiyah in Syria. He said: I came to Syria and completed her need. The month of Ramadan began while I was in Syria, and I saw the crescent on the night of Friday. Then I came to Medina at the end of the month, and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, asked me, then mentioned the crescent, and said: "When did you see the crescent?" I said: "We saw it on the night of Friday."
He said: "You saw it yourself?" I said: "Yes, and the people saw it, and they fasted, and Muʿāwiyah fasted."
He said: "But we saw it on the night of Saturday, so we will continue to fast until we complete thirty days or see it."
I said: "Is the sighting of Muʿāwiyah and his fasting not sufficient for you?" He said: "No. This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us."
Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā was unsure whether it was "nakhtafī" or "taktafī" [we are satisfied or you are satisfied].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"The two months of ʿĪd do not fall short."
In the narration of Khālid:
"The two months of ʿĪd: Ramadan and Dhū al-Ḥijjah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not let the adhān of Bilāl deceive you regarding your suḥūr, nor the whiteness of the horizon extending upward like this, until it spreads out like this."
Ḥammād illustrated it with his hands, saying, meaning spreading horizontally.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The difference between our fasting and the fasting of the People of the Book is the meal of suḥūr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended a funeral with Ibn ʿUmar, and when he placed the deceased in the niche of the grave, he said: "In the name of Allah, and in the cause of Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah."

Then, as he began setting the bricks over the niche, he said: "O Allah, protect it from Satan and from the punishment of the grave. O Allah, make the earth spacious on both its sides, raise its soul up, and grant it Your good pleasure."

I said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, is this something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or something you said from your own opinion?" He said: "Then I would indeed be capable of saying it myself! Rather, it is something I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ died, there was in Madinah a man who dug graves with a side niche and another who dug graves with a central trench. They said:
"Let us seek the guidance of our Lord and send for both of them; whichever of them comes first, we will leave the other."
So they sent for both, and the one who dug the side niche came first. So they dug a side niche for the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, they disagreed about the side niche and the central trench, until they spoke about it and their voices rose. Then
ʿUmar said: "Do not raise your voices near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whether alive or dead," or words to that effect.
So they sent for both the one who dug central trenches and the one who dug side niches, and the one who dug side niches came and dug a side niche for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he ﷺ was buried.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One night I came to guard the Prophet ﷺ, and there was a man reciting loudly. The Prophet ﷺ came out, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, this man is showing off."
He said: Then the man died in Madinah, and when they had finished preparing him, they carried his bier. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Be gentle with him; may Allah be gentle with him. He loved Allah and His Messenger."
He said: And his grave was dug, and he said:
"Make it spacious for him; may Allah make it spacious for him."
Some of his Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, you were grieved for him." He said:
"Yes, for he loved Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Dig, make it wide, and do it well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked the grave of ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn with a rock.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over a funeral, then came to the grave of the deceased and threw dust on it three times from the side of the head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"To walk on a burning coal or a sword, or to stitch my sandal on my foot, is more beloved to me than to walk on the grave of a Muslim. And it makes no difference to me whether I relieve myself in the middle of the graves or in the middle of the marketplace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was walking
with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said:
"O son of al-Khaṣāṣiyyah, what grievance do you have against Allah, that you have become one who walks with the Messenger of Allah?"
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have no grievance against Allah at all. Every good thing Allah has given me."
Then he passed by the graveyards of the Muslims and said:
"These have attained much good."
Then he passed by the graveyards of the polytheists and said:
"These have missed out on much good."
He said: Then he turned and saw a man walking between the graves in his sandals, and he said:
"O wearer of the two leather sandals, throw them off!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted permission to visit graves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father used to maintain family ties, and he used to do this and that.
Where is he?" He said: "In the Fire."
He said: It was as if the man was upset by that, so he said: "O Messenger of Allah, then where is your father?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Wherever you pass by the grave of a disbeliever, give him the glad tidings of the Fire."

He said: Afterwards the Bedouin accepted Islam and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ burdened me with hardship; I never pass by the grave of a disbeliever except that I give him the glad tidings of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: But it was not made obligatory upon us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and found some women sitting. He said: "What makes you sit here?"
They said: "We are waiting for the funeral." He said: "Will you wash the body?" They said: "No." He said: "Will you carry it?" They said: "No." He said:
"Will you lower it into the grave with those who lower it?" They said: "No." He said:
"Then go back, burdened with sin and not rewarded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, regarding {and they will not disobey you in what is right}, he said: "[It means] wailing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said, "
Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun and the moon when the sky is clear?" We said, "No." He said, "
Then you will have no difficulty in seeing your Lord on that Day,
except as you have in seeing the two of them." Then he said, "A caller will call out: Let every people go to what they used to worship.
So the people of the cross will go with their cross,
and the people of idols with their idols,
and the people of every deity with their deity, until there remain only those who used to worship Allah, whether righteous or sinful,
and the last remnants of the People of the Book.
Then Hell will be brought forward, appearing like a mirage, and the Jews will be asked, 'What did you used to worship?' They will say, 'We used to worship ʿUzayr, the son of Allah.'
It will be said, 'You have lied; Allah never took a consort or a son. What do you want?' They will say, 'We want You to give us something to drink.'
It will be said, 'Drink,' and they will fall into Hell. Then the Christians will be asked, 'What did you used to worship?' They will say, 'We used to worship the Messiah, the son of Allah.'
It will be said, 'You have lied; Allah never took a consort or a son.
What do you want?' They will say, 'We want You to give us something to drink.' It will be said, 'Drink.'

They will fall [into Hell] until there remain only those who used to worship Allah, whether righteous or sinful. It will be said to them, 'What keeps you here when the people have gone?' They will say, 'We parted from them when we were in greater need of them than today, and we heard a caller calling out: Let every people join what they used to worship.
We are only waiting for our Lord.'" He said, "Then the Almighty will come to them.
He will say, 'I am your Lord.'
They will say, 'You are our Lord.'
None will speak to Him except the prophets. He will say, 'Is there a sign between you and Him by which you know Him?' They will say, 'The shin.'
Then He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate to Him,
and there will remain those who used to prostrate to Allah for show and reputation.
They will go to prostrate, but their backs will become a single rigid plank.
Then the bridge will be brought and placed over the back of Hell."
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the bridge?" He said, "It is a slippery place where feet slide,
with hooks, clamps, and broad thorns,
having a curved thorn like those that grow in Najd, called as-Saʿdān.
The believer will cross it like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like the finest horses and riding camels.
Some will be saved unharmed, some will be saved but scratched, and some will be piled into the Fire of Hell,
until the last of them passes, dragged along.
You do not plead with me more earnestly for a right
that has become clear to you than the believers will plead with the Almighty on that Day
for their brothers, when they see that they themselves have been saved. They will say, 'Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us, and act with us.'
Allah the Exalted will say, 'Go, and bring out whoever you find with an atom's weight of faith equal to a dinar in his heart.'
Allah will have forbidden the Fire to consume their forms,
so they will come to them, and some will have sunk into the Fire up to their feet and up to the middle of their shins,
and they will bring out those whom they recognize.
Then they will return, and He will say, 'Go, and bring out whoever you find with faith equal to half a dinar in his heart.'
They will bring out those whom they recognize.
Then they will return, and He will say, 'Go, and bring out whoever you find with faith equal to the weight of an atom in his heart.'
They will bring out those whom they recognize."
Abū Saʿīd said, "If you do not believe me, then recite: {Indeed, Allah does not wrong even by the weight of an atom, and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it.}" [The Prophet ﷺ said:] "
Then the prophets, the angels, and the believers will intercede, and the Almighty will say, 'My intercession remains.'
He will take a handful from the Fire and bring out people who have been burned,
and they will be thrown into a river at the entrances of Paradise called the Water of Life,
and they will sprout along its banks as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood,
which you have seen beside a rock or beside a tree.
The part that faces the sun is green,
and the part that faces the shade is white,
and they will come out as if they were pearls.

Seals will be placed on their necks, and they will enter Paradise. The people of Paradise will say, 'These are the freed ones of the Most Merciful; He admitted them to Paradise without any deed they did or any good they sent ahead.'
It will be said to them, 'You have what you have seen, and the like of it with it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dūmat al-Jandal;
as for Suwāʿ, it belonged to Hudhayl;
as for Yaghūth, it belonged to Murād and then to Banū Ghuṭayf at al-Jurf, near Saba;
as for Yaʿūq, it belonged to Hamdān;
as for Nasr, it belonged to Ḥimyar,
the family of Dhū al-Kalāʿ.
These were names of righteous men of the people of Noah.
When they died, Satan inspired their people to set up statues in the places where they used to sit,
and to name them after them. They did so, but the statues were not worshipped until those people had died and the knowledge was forgotten; then they were worshipped.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I stayed in seclusion at Ḥirāʾ."
Like the hadith of ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "It throws sparks like a palace." He said, "We used to store wood, three cubits long or less, called a palace,
and we would store it for the winter and call it a palace."
label: machine translation
