segments_en: We would store it for the winter and call it a palace.
{As if they were yellow camels}: the ropes of ships, gathered together until they are like the waists of men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, for one of you to persist in an oath concerning his family is more sinful before Allah than for him to give the expiation that Allah has made obligatory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
"If one of you persists in an oath, that is more sinful before Allah than the expiation He has commanded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed—Ibrāhīm said: he either added or reduced—and when he had given the salām, it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, has something new occurred in the prayer?" He said: "What is that?"
They said: "You prayed such and such." He said: So he folded his legs, faced the qiblah, performed two prostrations, then gave the salām. Then he turned to us with his face and said:

"Had anything new occurred in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human being; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me. And when one of you is in doubt about his prayer, let him seek what is correct and complete his prayer on that basis, then let him perform two prostrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: A sheep of ours died, so we tanned its skin, and we continued to prepare nabīdh in it until it became a worn-out waterskin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Prophet ﷺ the ṣāʿ was one and a third mudd by your mudd today; then it was increased in the time of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not turn away from your fathers,
for whoever turns away from his father has committed disbelief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A drunken man was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered that he be beaten.
Some of us struck him with his hand,
some of us struck him with his sandal,
and some of us struck him with his garment.
When he left, a man said: "What is wrong with him? May Allah disgrace him!"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not be helpers of Satan against your brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I would not carry out a prescribed punishment on anyone and have him die from it and feel something about it in myself, except in the case of the one who drinks wine, for if he dies I would pay his blood money, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not establish a fixed punishment for it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan, so he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling on that, and he said:
"Can you find a slave to free?" He said: "No." He said:
"Are you able to fast two months?" He said: "No." He said:
"Then feed sixty poor people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said: "If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword, with its sharp edge."
That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Are you amazed at Saʿd's jealousy?
By Allah, I am more jealous than he,
and Allah is more jealous than I,
and because of Allah's jealousy He has forbidden indecencies, both what is apparent of them and what is hidden.
And no one loves the offering of excuses more than Allah,
and for that reason He sent the bearers of good news and the warners. And no one loves praise more than Allah, and for that reason Allah has promised Paradise."
ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAmr reported from ʿAbd al-Malik:
"No person is more jealous than Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: A Jew
killed a girl for the sake of some silver ornaments she had, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had him executed in retaliation for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Sahl ibn Ḥunayf: "Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say anything about the Khawārij?" He said: I heard him say—and he pointed with his hand toward Iraq—
"From it will emerge a people who recite the Qurʾān but it does not go beyond their throats,
they pass out of Islam as the arrow passes through the game."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"This pain or sickness is a punishment with which some nations before you were punished; then it remained afterward in the land, going away one time and coming another. So whoever hears of it in a land, let him not go to it, and whoever is in a land where it breaks out, let him not leave in flight from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If one of you sees a dream that he likes, it is from Allah, so let him praise Allah for it and relate what he saw. But if he sees other than that, something he dislikes, it is from Satan, so let him seek refuge in Allah from its evil and not mention it to anyone, for it will not harm him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A good dream is from Allah and a bad dream is from Satan. So if one of you sees something he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge in Allah from its evil, for it will not harm him."
He said: "I used to see a dream that was heavier on me than a mountain, but as soon as I heard this hadith, I no longer cared about them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: My uncle, after whom I was named, did not take part with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Badr. He said: This weighed heavily on him, and he said, "The first battle that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought, I was absent from it. If Allah shows me a battle with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after this, Allah will see what I do." He said: He feared to say anything more than that. He said: So he took part with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uḥud. He said: He met Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, and Anas said to him, "O Abū ʿAmr, where [are you going]?" He said, "Ah, the fragrance of Paradise! I find it coming from beyond Uḥud." He said: Then he fought them until he was killed. He said: More than eighty wounds were found on his body, from strikes, stabs, and arrows. He said: His sister, my paternal aunt al-Rubayyiʿ bint al-Naḍr, said, "I only recognized my brother by his fingertips."

And this verse was revealed: "Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah; among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who is still waiting, and they have not changed [their commitment] in the least." He said: They used to think that it was revealed about him and his companions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughing so fully that I could see his uvula; he would only smile. And when he saw clouds or wind, it could be seen on his face. So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, when people see clouds they are glad, hoping that rain is in them, but when you see them, I see dislike on your face." He said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, what assures me that there is no punishment in it? A people was punished with wind, and a people saw the punishment and said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Paradise and the Fire disputed, and the Fire said, 'I have been given the arrogant and the tyrannical.'

And Paradise said, 'What is the matter with me that only the weak and lowly people, and their simple-minded, enter me?' Allah said to Paradise, 'You are only My mercy; through you I show mercy to whom I will of My servants.'
And He said to the Fire, 'You are only My punishment; through you I punish whom I will of My servants.
And each of you shall have its fill. As for the Fire, it will not be filled until Allah, Blessed and Exalted, places His foot in it, and it says, "Enough, enough, enough."
Then it will be filled, and its parts will be drawn together. And Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah will bring into being a creation for it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And I think that I also heard it myself from Abū Salamah,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Recite the Qurʾān once every month."
He said: I said, "I find that I have strength." He said:
"Then recite it in twenty nights."
He said: I said, "I find that I have strength." He said:
"Then recite it in seven, and do not go beyond that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Respond to this invitation when you are invited to it."
He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar used to attend invitations, whether to a wedding or otherwise, and he would attend them while fasting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās. I said, "I have a small jar in which I prepare nabīdh, until it ferments and settles, and then I drink it."
He said, "For how long has this been your drink?" I said, "For twenty years," or he said, "for forty years."
He said, "For a long time your veins have been watered with filth."
Among what they cited as a pretext is the hadith of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Nāfiʿ from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar:
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar said: I saw a man come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a cup containing nabīdh while he was by the corner [of the Kaʿbah]. He handed him the cup, and he raised it to his mouth and found it strong, so he returned it to its owner. A man among the people said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, is it forbidden?" He said, "Bring the man to me."
He was brought, and he took the cup from him, then called for water and poured it into it, then raised it to his mouth and frowned. Then he called for water again and poured it into it. Then he said:
"When these containers become too strong for you, break their strength with water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked about drinks,
and he said, "Avoid everything that bubbles and ferments."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the care of Ibn ʿUmar. Raisins would be soaked for him and he would drink it the next day. Then the raisins would be dried, other raisins would be added to them, and water put in it, and he would drink it the next day. When the day after that came, he would throw it away.
They also argued from the hadith of Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ became thirsty around the Kaʿbah and asked for a drink. He was brought nabīdh from the water-station. He smelled it and frowned, and said:
"Bring me a bucket of Zamzam."
He poured it over it and then drank. A man said, "Is it forbidden, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "No."

This report is weak, because Yaḥyā ibn Yamān was alone in transmitting it, apart from the companions of Sufyān, and Yaḥyā ibn Yamān's hadith is not used as evidence because of his poor memory and his many mistakes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you fear the strength of nabīdh, break it with water. ʿAbdullāh said: Before it becomes strong.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Thaqīf met ʿUmar with a drink. He asked for it, and when he brought it close to his mouth he disliked it. So he called for it and broke it with water, and said, "Do it like this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The nabīdh that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb drank had been turned into vinegar.
Among what indicates the soundness of this is the hadith of al-Sāʾib:
label: machine translation

segments_en: I found on so-and-so the smell of a drink, and he claimed it was the drink of ṭilāʾ. I am asking about what he drank, and if it was intoxicating I will flog him. So ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, flogged him the full prescribed punishment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He disliked selling raisins
to someone who would make them into nabīdh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd had vineyards and many grapes, and he had a trustee over them. They yielded a great many grapes, so he wrote to him, "I fear the grapes will be lost. If you think fit, I will press them." Saʿd wrote back to him, "When this letter of mine reaches you, withdraw from my estate. By Allah, I will never entrust you with anything after this."
So he dismissed him from his estate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sell it as juice to someone who will make it into ṭilāʾ and will not make it into wine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That I provide
the Muslims with ṭilāʾ from which two thirds has gone and one third remains.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read the letter of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to Abū Mūsā: "To proceed: a caravan has come to me from Syria carrying a thick, black drink like the tar applied to camels. I asked them how long they cook it, and they told me they cook it down to two thirds, so that the two worse thirds are gone: one third through its excess and one third through its smell. So order those where you are to drink it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: For it has two [shares] and you have one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, used to provide people with ṭilāʾ into which flies would fall and be unable to get out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Saʿīd, "What is the drink that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, made lawful?" He said, "That which is cooked until two thirds are gone and one third remains."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Is it cooked down to half?" He said, "No, until two thirds are gone and one third remains."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ṭilāʾ is cooked down to a third, there is no harm in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Ḥasan about ṭilāʾ cooked down to half,
and he said, "Do not drink it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked al-Ḥasan about juice that is cooked. He said, "Cook it until two thirds are gone and one third remains."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Satan disputed with Noah, peace be upon him, over the grapevine. He said, "This is mine," and Noah said, "This is mine." They settled on this: that Noah would have a third of it and Satan two thirds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every intoxicant is forbidden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās when a man came and asked him about juice,
and he said, "Drink it as long as it is fresh."
He said, "I cooked a drink and I have some doubt about it."
He said, "Were you drinking it before you cooked it?" He said, "No."
He said, "Fire does not make lawful what has been made forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, fire neither makes anything lawful nor makes it forbidden.
He said: Then he explained to me his saying "it does not make anything lawful," because of what they said about ṭilāʾ, "and it does not make it forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Drink the juice as long as it does not foam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibrāhīm about juice,
and he said, "Drink it, even when it bubbles, as long as it has not changed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Maʿqil, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ḥujr,
from Zayd ibn Thābit,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever grants something to another for life, it belongs to the one to whom it was granted, in his life and after his death. Do not practice ruqbā; whoever grants something as ruqbā, it follows its own course."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had a ferocious she-camel which entered a garden and did damage in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was spoken to about it, and he ruled that guarding gardens by day is the responsibility of their owners, and guarding livestock by night is the responsibility of their owners, and that the owners of the livestock are liable for whatever their livestock damage at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Were it not for the hadith of Ibn Buraydah, from his father,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"Judges are of three kinds: two in the Fire and one in Paradise. A man who knew the truth and judged by it is in Paradise; a man who judged between people out of ignorance is in the Fire; and a man who was unjust in judgment is in the Fire."
we would have said that a judge who exercises his own reasoning is in Paradise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The verses

in Sūrat al-Māʾidah in which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {So judge between them or turn away from them} up to {those who act justly}, were revealed only concerning blood money between Banū al-Naḍīr and Banū Qurayẓah. The slain of Banū al-Naḍīr had greater honor and their blood money was paid in full, whereas Banū Qurayẓah paid only half the blood money. They took the matter for judgment to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed that concerning them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held them to the truth in that matter and made the blood money equal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people of Ḥimṣ, from the Companions of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, [reported] that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to send Muʿādh to Yemen, he said:
"How will you judge when a case is brought before you?"
He said: I will judge by the Book of Allah. He said:
"And if you do not find it in the Book of Allah?"
He said: Then by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said:
"And if you do not find it in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor in the Book of Allah?"
He said: I will exercise my own judgment and spare no effort.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck his chest and said:
"Praise be to Allah, Who has granted success to the messenger of the Messenger of Allah in what pleases the Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The testimony of a Bedouin against a person of a town is not permissible."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ bought a horse from a Bedouin and asked him to follow him so he could pay him the price of his horse. The Prophet ﷺ walked ahead quickly while the Bedouin lagged behind. Men began to approach the Bedouin and bargain with him over the horse, not knowing that the Prophet ﷺ had bought it, until some of them offered more than the price at which the Prophet ﷺ had bought it from him. Then the Bedouin called out to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Either you buy this horse, or I will sell it.
The Prophet ﷺ stopped when he heard his call and said:
"Have I not already bought it from you?"
He said: No, by Allah, I have not sold it to you. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I have indeed bought it from you."
People began to gather around the Prophet ﷺ and the Bedouin as the two went back and forth, and the Bedouin kept saying: Bring a witness who will testify that I sold it to you.
Khuzaymah ibn Thābit said: I testify that you sold it to him.
He said: The Prophet ﷺ turned to Khuzaymah and said: "On what basis do you testify?"
He said: On the basis of your truthfulness, O Messenger of Allah.
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the testimony of Khuzaymah equal to the testimony of two men.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men
brought a dispute over some goods to the Prophet ﷺ, and neither of them had proof. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Draw lots for the oath, whether you both like it or dislike it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, meaning to the Jews:
"I adjure you by Allah, Who revealed the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah concerning one who commits adultery?"
And he related the rest of the hadith, in the account of the stoning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They mention that a man

from Quraysh had a share in Banū Qurayẓah and brought a dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about Mahzūr, meaning the torrent whose water they divide. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled between them that the water is to be held up to the ankles, and the upper [landowner] is not to hold back the water from the lower.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to his bed, he would blow into his hands and recite the Muʿawwidhāt,
and then wipe his body with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people
asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ until they pressed him with their questions. So one day he came out, ascended the pulpit, and said:
"Ask me. You will not ask me about anything except that I will make it clear to you."
When the people heard that, they fell silent and were fearful that some matter had come upon them.

Anas said: I began to look right and left, and every man had wrapped his head in his garment, weeping. Then a man from the mosque, who used to be accused of being a quarreler and was called by a name other than his father's, stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Ḥudhāfah."

Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up and said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Messenger. We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of trials."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have never seen a day like today in terms of good and evil. Paradise and the Fire were shown to me, and I saw them just beyond this wall."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to supplicate with this supplication:
"My Lord, forgive me my error, my ignorance, and my excess in all my affairs,
and what You know better than I.
O Allah, forgive me my mistakes, my deliberate acts, my ignorance, and my jesting,
and all of that is in me.
O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have done after, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back,
and You have power over all things."
ʿUbaydullāh ibn Muʿādh said: My father narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us,
from Abū Isḥāq,
from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We memorized it from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah, as a narration, who said:
"Allah has ninety-nine names,
one hundred less one.
No one memorizes them except that he enters Paradise,
and He is One and loves the odd number."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ drew a square line,
and drew a line in the middle extending out of it,
and drew small lines toward this one in the middle,
from its side that was in the middle, and said: "This is the human being,
and this is his appointed term encompassing him, or it has already encompassed him, and this one which is outside is his hope,
and these small lines are the afflictions.
If this one misses him, that one bites him,
and if that one misses him, this one bites him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I brought ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān water for ablution, and he performed ablution. Then he said: Some people narrate hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I do not know, except that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution like this ablution of mine, and then he said:
"Whoever performs ablution like this, his previous sins will be forgiven, and his prayer and his walking to the mosque will be supererogatory."
In the narration of Ibn ʿAbdah: I came to ʿUthmān and he performed ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Which of you is there whose heir's wealth is dearer to him than his own wealth?"
They said: O Messenger of Allah, there is none of us except that his own wealth is dearer to him than the wealth of his heir.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Know that there is none among you except that his heir's wealth is dearer to him than his own wealth. Your wealth is what you send ahead, and the wealth of your heir is what you leave behind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on the day Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, died. The people said, "It was eclipsed only because of the death of Ibrāhīm."

So the Prophet ﷺ stood and led the people in prayer of six rakʿahs with four prostrations. He began by saying the takbīr, then recited and made the recitation long. Then he bowed for about as long as he had stood, then raised his head from the bowing and recited a recitation shorter than the first recitation. Then he bowed for about as long as he had stood, then raised his head from the bowing and recited a recitation shorter than the second recitation. Then he bowed for about as long as he had stood, then raised his head from the bowing, then went down into prostration and performed two prostrations. Then he stood and bowed likewise three times, each one longer than the one after it, and his bowing was about as long as his prostration. Then he stepped back and the rows stepped back behind him until we reached—and Abū Bakr said: until he reached the women—then he moved forward and the people moved forward with him until he stood in his place. He finished when he finished, and the sun had become bright. Then he said:

"O people, the sun and the moon are only two signs among the signs of Allah, and they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone among the people—and Abū Bakr said: for the death of a human being. So when you see something of that, pray until it clears. There is nothing that you have been promised except that I have seen it in this prayer of mine. The Fire was brought forward, and that was when you saw me step back, fearing that some of its blast would reach me. I even saw in it the man with the curved staff dragging his intestines in the Fire. He used to steal from the pilgrims with his curved staff; if he was noticed, he would say, 'It only got caught on my staff.'

But if they were unaware of him, he would go off with it. And I saw in it the woman with the cat, which she had tied up, neither feeding it nor letting it eat from the vermin of the earth, until it died of hunger. Then Paradise was brought forward, and that was when you saw me move forward until I stood in my place. I stretched out my hand wanting to take some of its fruit so that you might see it, then it occurred to me not to do so. There is nothing that you have been promised except that I have seen it in this prayer of mine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed eight rakʿahs with four prostrations when the sun was eclipsed.
And from ʿAlī, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no Muslim who is afflicted by a calamity and turns to what Allah commanded by saying:

'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, with You I seek reward for my calamity, so reward me for it and give me something better in exchange for it'—except that Allah rewards him for it and gives him something better in exchange." She said:
When Abū Salamah died, I remembered what he had narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I said:
"Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, with You I seek reward for this calamity of mine, so reward me for it."
When I wanted to say, "and give me something better in exchange," I said to myself:
"Could I be given something better than Abū Salamah?"
Then I said it, and Allah gave me Muhammad ﷺ in exchange.
And He rewarded me for my calamity.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm ʿAṭiyyah said: We were forbidden to follow funeral processions, but it was not made binding upon us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar when Khabbāb, the owner of the maqṣūrah, appeared and said, "O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, do you not hear what Abū Hurayrah is saying? He heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Whoever goes out with a funeral from its house and prays over it, then follows it until it is buried, will have two qīrāṭs of reward, each qīrāṭ like Uḥud; and whoever prays over it and then returns will have a reward like Uḥud.'"

So Ibn ʿUmar sent Khabbāb to ʿĀʾishah to ask her about what Abū Hurayrah had said, and then to return to him and inform him of what she said. Ibn ʿUmar took a handful of pebbles from the mosque and turned them over in his hand until the messenger returned to him and said, "ʿĀʾishah said: Abū Hurayrah has spoken the truth."
Ibn ʿUmar threw the pebbles that were in his hand to the ground and then said, "We have neglected many qīrāṭs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever it was her night with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would go out in the last part of the night to al-Baqīʿ and say:

"Peace be upon you, abode of believing people. What you were promised has come to you; tomorrow you will be given more time. And we, Allah willing, will be joining you. O Allah, forgive the people of Baqīʿ al-Gharqad."
Qutaybah did not give the wording "and it has come to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar met Ibn Ṣāʾid on one of the roads of Madīnah and said something to him that angered him, so he swelled up until he filled the road. Ibn ʿUmar then went in to Ḥafṣah, who had already heard of it. She said to him, "May Allah have mercy on you! What did you want from Ibn Ṣāʾid? Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'He will only emerge out of anger with which he becomes angry.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ used to say "Ibn Ṣayyād."

He said: Ibn ʿUmar said: I met him twice. I met him and said to some of them, "Do you say that he is the one?" He said, "No, by Allah." I said, "By Allah, you are lying to me! Some of you told me that he would not die until he had the most wealth and children among you, and so he is today, they claim." We talked and then I left him. Then I met him another time, and his eye had swollen up. I said, "When did your eye become as I see it?" He said, "I do not know." I said, "You do not know, while it is in your head?" He said, "If Allah willed, He could create it in this staff of yours."

He snorted like the loudest braying of a donkey I have ever heard. Some of my companions claimed that I struck him with a staff I had with me until it broke, but as for me, by Allah, I was not aware of it. Then he came and entered upon the Mother of the Believers and told her. She said, "What do you want with him? Do you not know that he ﷺ said:
'The first thing that will send him out against the people is anger with which he becomes angry.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I know better than he what the Dajjāl has with him. He has two rivers flowing: one appears to the eye as white water, and the other appears to the eye as blazing fire. So whoever of you lives to see it, let him go to the river that he sees as fire, and let him close his eyes, then lower his head and drink from it, for it is cold water. And the Dajjāl is blind in one eye, with a thick film over it, and between his eyes is written 'Kāfir' (disbeliever), which every believer will read, whether literate or not."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to him and said, "What is this hadith that you narrate, saying that the Hour will come at such and such a time?"

He said, "Glory be to Allah!" — or "There is no god but Allah," or a similar phrase — "I had almost resolved not to tell anyone anything ever again. I only said that you will soon see a momentous event: the House will be burned, and such and such will happen." Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Dajjāl will emerge among my Ummah and remain forty — I do not know whether forty days, forty months, or forty years. Then Allah will send ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, who resembles ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd, and he will pursue him and destroy him. Then people will live for seven years with no enmity between any two. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of Syria, and no one will remain on the face of the earth who has in his heart an atom's weight of good or faith except that it will take his soul, even if one of you were to enter the heart of a mountain, it would enter upon him until it takes him."
He said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"Then the worst of people will remain, light as birds and with the minds of predatory beasts, neither recognizing any good nor denouncing any evil. Satan will appear to them in human form and say, 'Will you not respond?' They will say, 'What do you command us?' He will command them to worship idols, and in that state their provision will be plentiful and their life comfortable. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will tilt his neck to one side and raise the other. The first to hear it will be a man plastering the trough of his camels. He will fall unconscious, and the people will fall unconscious. Then Allah will send — or he said, Allah will send down — rain like dew or shade — Nuʿmān was unsure — from which the bodies of people will grow. Then the Trumpet will be blown a second time, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said, 'O people, come to your Lord!'

'Stop them, for they are to be questioned.' Then it will be said, 'Bring out the party of the Fire.' It will be asked, 'How many?' It will be said, 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.' That is the Day that makes children turn gray-haired, and that is the Day when the shin will be uncovered."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever sends ahead three [children] who have not reached puberty, they will be for him a strong fortress against the Fire."
Abū Dharr said, "I have sent ahead two." He said, "And two."
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, the master of the reciters, said, "I have sent ahead one." He said:
"And one. But that [reward] applies only at the first shock [of the loss]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad and Khālid ibn ʿUrfuṭah, and they mentioned that a man had died
of a disease of the stomach, and both of them wished to be present at his funeral. One said to the other, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say:
'Whoever is killed by his stomach will not be punished in his grave'?"
The other said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever consoles one who has suffered a loss will have a reward like his."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The soul of the believer is held in suspension by his debt until it is settled on his behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat the tambourines for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
of Banū Fazārah married for [a dowry of] two sandals, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Are you pleased, with regard to yourself and your property, with two sandals?" She said, "Yes." He said: So he permitted it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ghaylān ibn Salamah al-Thaqafī
accepted Islam while he had ten wives from the time of ignorance, and they accepted Islam with him. So the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to choose four of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned his daughter Zaynab to Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ with a new dowry and a new marriage contract.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She freed Barīrah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her the choice [to stay with or leave her husband]; she had a free husband.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any woman who dies while her husband is pleased with her will enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No woman harms her husband in this world but his wife among the wide-eyed Ḥūr says, 'Do not harm him, may Allah fight you! He is only a guest with you, and he is about to leave you and come to us.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās and Abū
Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān disagreed about a woman who gives birth a few nights after her husband's death. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "[Her waiting period is] the later of the two terms."
Abū Salamah said, "If she has given birth, she has become lawful [to remarry]."
Then Abū Hurayrah came and said, "I am with my nephew,"
meaning Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

So they sent Kurayb, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, to Umm Salamah to ask her about that. He came back and informed them that she said: Subayʿah gave birth a few nights after her husband's death, and she mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "You have become lawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, concerning a man who has made ẓihār from his wife and has relations with her before making expiation, he said: "One expiation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ having made ẓihār from his wife and then had relations with her. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I made ẓihār from my wife and had relations with her before making expiation." He said:
"What made you do that, may Allah have mercy on you?"
He said, "I saw her anklet in the moonlight." He said:
"Then do not approach her until you do what Allah has commanded you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from his wives, and he declared [something] forbidden; so he made the forbidden lawful and made expiation for the oath.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from praying in the mosque."
So a son of his said, "We will certainly prevent them."
He became extremely angry and said, "I am telling you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you say, 'We will certainly prevent them'?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī, the chieftain,

a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fought alongside Muʿāwiyah in the land of the Romans. He saw the people selling pieces of gold for dinars and pieces of silver for dirhams, and he said, "O people, you are consuming usury! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Do not sell gold for gold except like for like, with no excess between them and no delay.'"
Muʿāwiyah said to him, "O Abū al-Walīd, I do not see usury in this except in the case of delay."
ʿUbādah said, "I tell you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you tell me your own opinion! If Allah brings me out of this, I will not live with you in a land where you have authority over me."

When he returned, he went to Madinah. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to him, "What brought you, O Abū al-Walīd?" He related the matter to him, and what he had said about not living with Muʿāwiyah. ʿUmar said, "Return to your land, O Abū al-Walīd. May Allah make ugly a land in which you and the likes of you are not present."
And he wrote to Muʿāwiyah, "You have no authority over him. Make the people act according to what he said, for that is the correct ruling."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So think of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what is most pleasant, most rightly guided, and most God-fearing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Let me not find any of you, when a hadith is related from me, reclining on his couch and saying, 'Recite a Qurʾān to us.'
Whatever good has been said, I have said it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: to a man, "O son of my brother, when I narrate to you a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, do not coin analogies for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never missed Ibn Masʿūd on a Thursday evening without coming to him. He said: I never heard him say about anything, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said," until one evening he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said," and then he bowed his head.

He said: I looked at him, and he was standing with the buttons of his shirt undone, his eyes brimming with tears and his neck veins swollen. He said, "Or less than that, or more than that, or close to that, or similar to that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Anas ibn Mālik narrated a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and finished it, he would say, "Or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to Zayd ibn Arqam, "Narrate to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said, "We have grown old and have forgotten, and narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a serious matter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ anything.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to memorize hadith, and hadith was [carefully] memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. But now that you have ridden the hard and the docile camel alike, how far off that is!
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sent us to Kufa and saw us off, walking with us to a place called Ṣirār.
He said, "Do you know why I walked with you?" We said, "Because of the right of the Companionship of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the right of the Anṣār."

He said, "But I walked with you for a hadith I wanted to tell you, so that you would remember it because of my walking with you: you are going to a people in whose chests the Qurʾān hums like the boiling of a cauldron. When they see you, they will stretch their necks toward you and say, 'The Companions of Muḥammad!'
So narrate little from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I will be your partner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied Saʿd ibn Mālik from Madinah to Makkah, and I did not hear him narrate a single hadith from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: on this pulpit:
"Beware of narrating too much from me. Whoever speaks on my authority, let him say what is true or correct, and whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer, then turned his face to us and gave us an eloquent admonition. Then he mentioned something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "There is no contagion."
Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I heard Abū Hurayrah,
narrating from the Prophet ﷺ, who said,
"Do not bring the sick [camels] to the healthy ones." And from al-Zuhrī, who said:
Sinān ibn Abī Sinān al-Duʾalī informed me
that Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "There is no contagion."
Then a Bedouin stood up and said, "What about camels that are in the sands, like gazelles, and then a mangy camel comes among them and they become mangy?" The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Then who infected the first one?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Bilāl come with a short spear and plant it in the ground,
then he called the iqāmah for the prayer,
and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ come out in a cloak, with his garment tucked up,
and he prayed two rakʿahs facing the spear,
and I saw people and animals passing in front of him, beyond the spear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Then the Prophet ﷺ called for his cloak,
then he set off walking,
and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and I followed him,
until he came to the house in which Ḥamzah was,
and he asked permission to enter, and they gave them permission.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Anas wearing a yellow hooded cloak made of khazz silk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of the Muslims migrated to Abyssinia,
and Abū Bakr prepared to migrate. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Wait a while,
for I hope that I will be given permission."
Abū Bakr said, "Do you hope for that? May my father be your ransom." He said, "Yes."
So Abū Bakr held himself back for the sake of accompanying the Prophet ﷺ,
and he fed two riding camels that he had with acacia leaves for four months.
ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah said: One day we were sitting in our house at the height of midday when someone said to Abū Bakr, "Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, coming with his head covered,
at an hour when he did not usually come to us."
Abū Bakr said, "May my father and mother be his ransom!
By Allah, he has come at this hour only because of some matter."
The Prophet ﷺ came and asked permission to enter,
and he was given permission, so he entered,
and when he entered he said to Abū Bakr,
"Send away those who are with you."
He said, "They are only your family, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"I have been given permission to depart."
He said, "Then [may I have] your companionship, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Then take one of these two riding camels of mine, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said, "For the price."
She said: So we prepared them both as quickly as possible,
and we made a food bag for them in a leather satchel,
and Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr cut a piece from her waist-band
and tied the satchel with it,
and for that reason she was called Dhāt al-Niṭāq (She of the Waist-band).
Then the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr reached a cave in a mountain called Thawr,
and he stayed there three nights. ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr would spend the night with them,
and he was a young man, sharp and quick to understand,
and he would leave them before dawn,
and by morning he would be with Quraysh in Makkah as though he had spent the night there,
and he would not hear of any plot against them without retaining it,
until he came to them with news of it when darkness fell,
and ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah, the freed slave of Abū Bakr, would graze a milch flock of sheep for them,
and he would bring it to them when a portion of the evening had passed,
and they would spend the night with its fresh milk until ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah drove it off at the darkness before dawn,
doing that on each of those three nights.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rifāʿah divorced his wife,
and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Zubayr al-Quraẓī married her.
ʿĀʾishah said: She was wearing a green veil. She complained to her
and showed her the greenness [bruising] on her skin.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and the women were supporting one another, ʿĀʾishah said, "I have not seen anything like what the believing women suffer;
her skin is greener than her garment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in a red leather tent,
and I saw Bilāl take the water left from the Prophet's ﷺ ablution, and the people were rushing to get it,
so whoever got some of it rubbed himself with it,
and whoever did not get any took from the moisture on his companion's hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for the Anṣār and gathered them in a tent and said to them,
"Be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger,
for I will be at the Pool."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ al-Anṣārī came to us from Madīnah, and the Anṣār used to regard him as a man of understanding. He narrated to us, saying: Abū Qatādah al-Anṣārī, the horseman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out the army of the commanders, with this account.
He said: Nothing woke us except the sun having risen, so we got up hastily for our prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Slowly, slowly."
Until, when the sun had risen high, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever among you prays the two units of the Fajr prayer, let him pray them."

So those who used to pray them stood up, and those who did not used to pray them also prayed them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the call to prayer be made, and it was made. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and led us in prayer, and when he finished he said,

"Indeed, we praise Allah that we were not occupied with any worldly matter that distracted us from our prayer. Rather, our souls were in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He sent them back whenever He willed. So whoever among you reaches the morning prayer on the next day in a good state, let him pray along with it the like of it [as a make-up prayer]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a journey, and they slept through the Fajr prayer. They woke up in the heat of the sun, and they moved on a little until the sun had risen high. Then he commanded a muʾadhdhin, who gave the call to prayer. He prayed two units before the Fajr, then the iqāmah was called, and then he prayed the Fajr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mikhbar al-Ḥabashī, who used to serve the Prophet ﷺ, said in this report: He performed ablution, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, an ablution that did not soil him with dust. Then he commanded Bilāl, who gave the call to prayer. Then the Prophet ﷺ stood and prayed two units without haste. Then he said to Bilāl, "Call the iqāmah for the prayer."
Then he prayed the obligatory prayer, without haste.
He said, from Ḥajjāj, from Yazīd ibn Ṣulayḥ: Dhū Mikhbar, a man from Abyssinia, narrated to me. And ʿUbayd said: Yazīd ibn Ṣāliḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: So he gave the call to prayer, and he was not hasty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We returned with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the time of Ḥudaybiyah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Who will keep watch over us?"
Bilāl said, "I will."
So they slept until the sun rose. Then the Prophet ﷺ woke up and said,
"Do as you used to do." He said: So we did so. He said,
"So do likewise for whoever sleeps through [a prayer] or forgets it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I was not commanded to build mosques lofty and ornate."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: You will surely decorate them as the Jews and the Christians decorated [theirs].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The mosque of the Prophet

ﷺ: in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ its pillars were of palm trunks, and its top was shaded with palm fronds. Then they decayed in the caliphate of Abū Bakr, so he rebuilt it with palm trunks and palm fronds. Then they decayed in the caliphate of ʿUthmān, so he rebuilt it with baked brick, and it has remained firm until now.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Samurah wrote to his son: To proceed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to build mosques in our neighborhoods, to take care in their construction, and to keep them clean.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The freed woman] of the Prophet ﷺ said: O Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling about Bayt al-Maqdis. He said,
"Go to it and pray in it."
— and the land at that time was at war — "But if you cannot go to it and pray in it, then send oil to be burned in its lamps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the mosque, he said: It rained one night, and in the morning the ground was wet. A man began to come with pebbles in his garment and spread them beneath him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said,
"How good this is."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It used to be said that when a man takes pebbles out of the mosque, they plead with him [to return them].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, the pebble pleads with the one who takes it out of the mosque."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"If only we had left this door for the women."
Nāfiʿ said: Ibn ʿUmar never entered through it until he died.
Someone other than ʿAbd al-Wārith said: ʿUmar said [it], and that is more correct.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
used to forbid entering
through the women's door.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met ʿUqbah ibn Muslim and said to him: It has reached me that you narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that when he entered the mosque he would say,
"I seek refuge in Allah the Magnificent, in His Noble Face, and in His eternal authority, from the accursed Satan."
He said, "Is that all?" I said, "Yes."
He said: When he says that, Satan says, "He is protected from me for the rest of the day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I and Abū Hurayrah were with Ibn ʿAbbās, a woman came to him and said, "Her husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth less than four months after the day he died."
Ibn ʿAbbās said, "The later of the two terms."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to Subayʿah al-Aslamiyyah, "You are not permitted to remarry until four months and ten days have passed over you, the longer of the two terms."

So she went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about that. She claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her a ruling that she could marry once she had delivered her child. She had been nine months pregnant when her husband died. She was married to Saʿd ibn Khawlah, who died during the Farewell Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then she married a young man of her people when she had delivered what was in her womb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse with him: the verse {And for those who are pregnant, their term is that they give birth} was revealed only after the verse about a woman whose husband has died. When a woman whose husband has died gives birth, she has become permitted [to remarry]. The wording is that of Maymūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, the shorter Sūrat al-Nisāʾ,
was revealed after al-Baqarah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Juraij, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Saʿd ibn Isḥāq,
from Zaynab bint Kaʿb,
from al-Fāriʿah bint Mālik, that her husband

went out in search of some slaves and they killed him. Shuʿbah and Ibn Juraij said: She was living in a remote house, so she came with her brother to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They mentioned it to him and he gave her permission. Then, when she turned back, he called her and said:
"Stay in your house until the prescribed period reaches its end."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab bint Kaʿb, from al-Furayʿah bint Mālik, that her husband

had hired some laborers to work for him, and they killed him. She mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I am not in a house that he owned, and no provision is coming to me from him. May I move to my family and my orphans and take care of them?" He said, "Do so." Then he said, "How did you say it?"
So she repeated her words to him. He said:
"Observe your waiting period wherever the news reached you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That her husband

went out in search of some slaves of his and was killed at the edge of al-Qadūm. She said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned to him moving to my family, and I mentioned to him something of my situation. She said: He gave me permission. Then, as I was leaving, he called me and said:
"Stay with your family until the prescribed period reaches its end."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he allowed a woman whose husband has died, at the time of her purification [from menstruation], to use qusṭ and aẓfār [types of incense].
label: machine translation

segments_en: [She was] with a man of Banū Makhzūm, who divorced her three times and went out on one of the military expeditions, and instructed his agent to give her some maintenance. She considered it too little, so she went to one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in while she was with her, and she said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Fāṭimah bint Qays. So-and-so divorced her and sent her some maintenance, but she returned it, and he claims it is something he is giving as a favor." He said, "He has spoken truly." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Move to Umm Kulthūm and observe your waiting period with her." Then he said:
"Umm Kulthūm is a woman who is visited by many visitors, so move to ʿAbdullāh ibn Umm Maktūm, for he is blind."

So she moved to ʿAbdullāh and observed her waiting period with him until it ended. Then Abū al-Jahm and Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān proposed to her. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to seek his advice about the two of them, and he said:
"As for Abū al-Jahm, he is a man for whom I fear, on your behalf, his readiness to use the staff; and as for Muʿāwiyah, he is a man who is poor and has no wealth."
Afterwards she married Usāmah ibn Zayd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her maternal aunt was divorced and wished to go out to her date palms. She met a man who forbade her, so she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Go out and harvest your dates; perhaps you may give charity and do some good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man said, "O Messenger of Allah, the people have let their horses go and laid down their weapons, and they say there is no more jihad, the war has put down its burdens." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned his face toward him and said:

"They have lied! Now, now the fighting has come. There will not cease to be a group of my community fighting for the truth, and Allah will turn the hearts of some people astray for them and provide for them from those people, until the Hour is established and until the promise of Allah comes. Goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection. It has been revealed to me that I will be taken without delay, and you will follow me in groups, some of you striking the necks of others. And the secure home of the believers is ash-Shām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, after women, than horses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not fight those of my people who turn away, together with those who accept [Islam]?" So he permitted me to fight them and commanded me. When I left him, he asked about me: "What did the Ghuṭayfī do?" He was told that I had set out. He said: So he sent someone after me and had me brought back. I came to him while he was among a group of his Companions, and he said:
"Call the people; whoever among them accepts Islam, accept it from him, and whoever does not accept Islam, do not hurry until I give you [further instruction]."
He said: And what was revealed about Sabaʾ was revealed. A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is Sabaʾ? A land or a woman?" He said:

"It is neither a land nor a woman, but a man who had ten [sons] among the Arabs. Six of them went to the right [Yaman] and four of them went to the left [Shaʾm]. As for those who went to the left, they are Lakhm, Judhām, Ghassān and ʿĀmilah. As for those who went to the right, they are al-Azd, the Ashʿarīs, Ḥimyar, Madhḥij, Anmār and Kindah."
A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, and what is Anmār?" He said:
"Those from whom come Khathʿam and Bajīlah."
This was also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said concerning this verse:

"Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those We chose from Our servants; among them are those who wrong themselves, among them are those who are moderate, and among them are those who are foremost in good deeds." He said:
"All of these are of one rank, and all of them will be in Paradise."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith; we know it only through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
"And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more." He said, "Twenty thousand [more]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah:
"And We made his descendants the survivors." He said:
"Ḥām, Sām and Yāfith." Thus [it is narrated].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sām is the father of the Arabs, Ḥām is the father of the Abyssinians, and Yāfith is the father of the Romans."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd, who is Ibn ʿAbbād, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,

who said: Abū Ṭālib fell ill, so Quraysh came to him, and the Prophet ﷺ came too. Beside Abū Ṭālib there was room for one man [to sit]. Abū Jahl stood up to prevent him [from sitting there], and they complained about him to Abū Ṭālib, saying, "O son of my brother, what do you want from your people?" He said:
"I want from them one word by which the Arabs will submit to them, and the non-Arabs will pay them the jizyah."
He said, "One word?" He said, "One word." He said:
"O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah." They said, "A single god?
We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is nothing but a fabrication." He said: Then the Qurʾān was revealed about them:
"Ṣād. By the Qurʾān containing the reminder. Rather, those who disbelieve are in pride and opposition," up to His saying:
"We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is nothing but a fabrication."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"My Lord, Blessed and Exalted, came to me tonight in the best form." [The narrator] said: I think he said, "in a dream." "He said, 'O Muhammad, do you know what the Highest Assembly dispute about?' I said, 'No.'

He said: Then He placed His hand between my shoulders until I felt its coolness in my chest," or he said, "in my throat, "and I came to know what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. He said, 'O Muhammad, do you know what the Highest Assembly dispute about?' I said, 'Yes.
They dispute about the expiations.

The expiations are staying in the mosques after the prayers, walking on foot to the congregations, and performing ablution thoroughly despite difficulties. Whoever does that will live in goodness and die in goodness, and will be free of his sins as on the day his mother bore him.' And He said, 'O Muhammad, when you pray, say: O Allah, I ask You to enable me to do good deeds, to abandon evil deeds, and to love the poor. And when You intend a trial for Your servants, take me to You without being put to trial.' He said: And the [raised] ranks are spreading the greeting of peace, feeding people, and praying at night while people sleep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My Lord came to me in the best form and said, 'O Muhammad.' I said, 'Here I am, my Lord, at Your service.' He said, 'What do the Highest Assembly dispute about?' I said, 'My Lord, I do not know.' So He placed His hand between my shoulders and I felt its coolness in my chest, and I came to know what is between the east and the west. He said, 'O Muhammad.'

I said, 'Here I am, Lord, at Your service.' He said, 'What do the Highest Assembly dispute about?' I said, 'About the [raised] ranks and the expiations, about taking steps to the congregations, performing ablution thoroughly despite disliked circumstances, and waiting for one prayer after another. Whoever maintains them will live in goodness and die in goodness, and will be free of his sins as on the day his mother bore him.'"
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith by this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to Medina with Abū Bakr riding behind him,
and Abū Bakr was an elderly man who was well known,
while the Prophet ﷺ was a young man who was not known.
He said: A man would meet Abū Bakr and say, "O Abū Bakr,
who is this man in front of you?" He would say, "This man guides me along the way."
The one who heard it would think he meant only the road,
but he really meant the way of goodness.
Then Abū Bakr turned around,
and there was a horseman who had caught up with them,
so he said, "O Messenger of Allah,
this is a horseman who has caught up with us."
The Prophet ﷺ turned and said, "O Allah, throw him down." The horse threw him down,
then it got up neighing, and the man said, "O Prophet of Allah, command me as you wish." He said, "Stay where you are,
and do not let anyone catch up with us."
He said: At the beginning of the day he was struggling hard against the Prophet ﷺ,
and at the end of the day he was a guard for him.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at the side of the lava field,
and sent word to the Ansar,
and they came to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted the two of them,
and said, "Ride, both of you, secure and obeyed."
So the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr rode,
and they surrounded them with weapons,
and it was said in Medina, "The Prophet of Allah has come,
the Prophet of Allah ﷺ has come."
They climbed up to look and kept saying, "The Prophet of Allah has come,
the Prophet of Allah has come."
He went on until he stopped beside the house of Abū Ayyūb.
While he was speaking with his family,
ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām heard of him, as he was in a date-palm grove of his family picking fruit for them,
so he hurried to put down what he was picking for them there,
and came with it still with him,
and he listened to the Prophet ﷺ, then returned to his family.
Then the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Which of our family's houses is nearest?"
Abū Ayyūb said, "I am, O Prophet of Allah. This is my house, and this is my door." He said,
"Go and prepare a resting place for us."
He said, "Both of you, rise, with the blessing of Allah."
When the Prophet ﷺ had come, ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām came and said, "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah,
and that you have come with the truth,
and the Jews know that I am their master and the son of their master,
and the most knowledgeable of them and the son of their most knowledgeable,
so call them and ask them about me before they know that I have become Muslim,
for if they know that I have become Muslim, they will say about me what is not true."
So the Prophet ﷺ sent for them, and they came and entered upon him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
"O company of Jews,
woe to you, fear Allah,
for by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, you know that I am truly the Messenger of Allah,
and that I have come to you with the truth, so become Muslim."
They said, "We do not know that."
They said this to the Prophet ﷺ; he said it three times. He said,
"What kind of man is ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām among you?"
They said, "He is our master and the son of our master,
and the most knowledgeable of us and the son of our most knowledgeable." He said,
"What if he became Muslim?"
They said, "Allah forbid,
he would never become Muslim." He said,
"What if he became Muslim?"
They said, "Allah forbid,
he would never become Muslim." He said,
"O Ibn Salām, come out to them."
So he came out and said, "O company of Jews, fear Allah,
for by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, you know that he is the Messenger of Allah,
and that he has come with the truth." They said, "You are lying."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. He said: The stipend fixed for the earliest Emigrants was four thousand, in four installments,
and for Ibn ʿUmar it was fixed at three thousand five hundred. It was said to him, "He is one of the Emigrants,
so why did you reduce him from four thousand?" He said, "Only his parents emigrated with him."
He meant that he was not like one who emigrated on his own.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said to me, "Do you know what my father said to your father?" I said, "No."
He said: "My father said to your father, 'O Abū Mūsā,
would it please you that our Islam with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, our emigration with him, our striving with him,
and all our deeds with him were credited to us, and that every deed we did after him we would escape from
only evenly, with nothing for us and nothing against us?' My father said, 'No, by Allah,
we strove after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we prayed, and we fasted,
and we did much good,
and many people became Muslim at our hands,
and we hope for reward for that.'
Then my father said, 'But as for me, by the One in whose hand is the soul of ʿUmar, I wish that that would be credited to us,
and that everything we did afterward we would escape from only evenly, with nothing for us and nothing against us.'"
I said, "By Allah, your father was better than my father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh was struck in his median arm vein. The Prophet ﷺ cauterized it with his own hand using a broad arrowhead; then it swelled again, and he cauterized it a second time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I am the master of the children of Ādam, and this is no boast. I am the first for whom the earth will be split open on the Day of Resurrection, and this is no boast. I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and this is no boast. And the banner of praise will be in my hand on the Day of Resurrection, and this is no boast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No one has done us a favor except that we have repaid him, apart from Abū Bakr, for he has done us a favor for which Allah will repay him on the Day of Resurrection. No one's wealth has ever benefited me as much as the wealth of Abū Bakr. And if I were to take a close friend (khalīl), I would take Abū Bakr as a close friend. Indeed, your companion is the close friend of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr and Abū Usāmah, from Zakariyyā,
from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father,
from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no pact of alliance in Islam, and any pact of alliance that existed in the Jāhiliyyah, Islam only strengthens it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good," or: "He who is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever stops at a place and then says: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' nothing will harm him until he departs from that place."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
Mālik ibn Anas narrated this hadith, that it reached him from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ashajj, and he mentioned something similar to this hadith.
This hadith was also narrated from Ibn ʿAjlān, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ashajj, and he says: from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Khawlah.
He said: The hadith of al-Layth is more authentic than the narration of Ibn ʿAjlān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fāṭimah came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him for a servant, and he said to her:

"Say: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of everything, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Qurʾān, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold. You are the First, so there is nothing before You; You are the Last, so there is nothing after You; You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Settle my debt for me and enrich me against poverty."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb, and some of the students of al-Aʿmash narrated something like this from al-Aʿmash.
Some of them narrated it from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, as a mursal report, and did not mention Abū Hurayrah in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Umm al-Dardāʾ was his wife. He said: I came to Syria and went to Abū al-Dardāʾ at his house but did not find him; I found Umm al-Dardāʾ, who said: Do you intend to perform Hajj this year? I said: Yes.
She said: Then pray to Allah for good for us, for the Prophet ﷺ used to say:

"The supplication of a Muslim for his brother in his absence is answered. At his head is an appointed angel; whenever he prays for good for his brother, the appointed angel says: Āmīn, and the same for you."
He said: Then I went out to the market and met Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he said the same to me, narrating it from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ... (transition to another chain:) and Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us: Ḥammād narrated to us,
from al-Muʿallā ibn Ziyād,
tracing it back to Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah, tracing it back to Maʿqil ibn Yasār, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Worship during times of turmoil (harj) is like emigrating to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to relieve himself, and when he wanted to answer the call of nature he would go far away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met a man who had accompanied the Prophet ﷺ for four years, just as Abū Hurayrah accompanied him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade any of us to comb his hair every day, or to urinate in the place where he bathes, or for a man to perform ablution with the water left over by a woman, or a woman with the water left over by a man; rather, they should scoop water together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Were it not that it would be hard on my Ummah, I would command them to use the siwāk at every prayer, and I would delay the ʿIshāʾ prayer until a third of the night."

He said: Zayd ibn Khālid used to attend the prayers in the mosque with his siwāk behind his ear, like the place of the pen on the ear of a scribe. He would not stand for prayer without using the siwāk, and then he would return it to its place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Abū Kurayb—the wording is Yaḥyā's—Yaḥyā said: He informed us; and the other two said:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash,
from Abū Sufyān, from Jābir, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a physician to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb; he cut a vein from him and then cauterized it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion."
And he also related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let not one with sick camels be brought to one with healthy camels."
Abū Salamah said: Abū Hurayrah used to narrate both of them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Abū Hurayrah fell silent afterward about his saying "There is no contagion," and he held to:
"Let not one with sick camels be brought to one with healthy camels."

He said: Then al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Dhubāb, who was Abū Hurayrah's cousin, said: O Abū Hurayrah, I used to hear you narrate to us, along with this hadith, another hadith about which you have now become silent. You used to say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion."
But Abū Hurayrah refused to acknowledge that, and said:
"Let not one with sick camels be brought to one with healthy camels."
Al-Ḥārith did not let the matter go, until Abū Hurayrah became angry and spoke in Abyssinian. He said to al-Ḥārith: Do you know what I said? He said: No.
Abū Hurayrah said: I said, "I refuse."
Abū Salamah said: By my life, Abū Hurayrah used to narrate to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no contagion."
So I do not know whether Abū Hurayrah forgot, or whether one of the two statements abrogated the other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer with us, he would turn his face to the people and say:
"Did any of you see a dream last night?"
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
This hadith is also narrated from ʿAwf and Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū Rajāʾ, from Samurah, from the Prophet ﷺ, in a long account.
He said: And in this way Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated this hadith from Wahb ibn Jarīr, in abridged form.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtbah when they mentioned the age of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some of the people said: Abū Bakr was older than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿAbdullāh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken [in death] at the age of sixty-three; Abū Bakr died at sixty-three; and ʿUmar was killed at sixty-three.

He said: Then a man from the group, called ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd, said: Jarīr narrated to us, saying: We were sitting with Muʿāwiyah when they mentioned the age of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Muʿāwiyah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken at the age of sixty-three years; Abū Bakr died at sixty-three; and ʿUmar was killed at sixty-three.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was taken [in death] at the age of sixty-five. This is how he, meaning Ibn Bashshār, narrated it to us, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated the same from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I passed by with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among some date palms, and he saw people pollinating the palms. He said:
"What are these people doing?"
They said: They take from the male and put it into the female. He said:
"I do not think that this is of any use."
That reached them, so they abandoned it and came down from the palms. Then it reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

"It was only a conjecture. If it is of any benefit, then do it. I am only a human being like you, and conjecture may be mistaken or correct. But when I tell you, 'Allah said,' I will never lie about Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAlī
mentioned the daughter of Abū Jahl. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Fāṭimah is only a part of me. What harms her harms me, and what troubles her troubles me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said this about a month before his death, or around that time: "
There is no living soul today that will reach one hundred years while still alive at that time."
And from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
the keeper of the water supply, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh,
from the Prophet ﷺ, the same. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān explained it, saying: [It means] the shortening of lifespan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was my grandfather, Munqidh ibn ʿAmr. He was a man who had been struck on the head by a stab wound, which damaged his speech. Despite that he did not give up trading, and he was constantly being cheated. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said to him:
"When you make a sale, say: 'No deception.'
Then for every item you buy you have the option for three nights. If you are satisfied, keep it, and if you are displeased, return it to its owner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ relieved Muʿādh ibn Jabal of his creditors, then appointed him over Yemen. Muʿādh said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took my property for himself [to settle my debts], then appointed me [as governor].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any man who dies while he has with him the exact property of another man, whether that man had collected some of his due from him or had not, he [the owner] is equal to the other creditors."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He recited this verse: {O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term} until he reached {But if one of you trusts another} and said: This abrogated what came before it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the people of Egypt, from Suraq:
The Prophet ﷺ permitted the testimony of one man together with the oath of the claimant.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: {The feet of a false witness will not move until Allah makes the Fire obligatory for him.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the testimony of the People of the Book against one another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ruled that a lifetime gift (ʿumrā) belongs to the heir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no ruqbā. Whoever is given something as a ruqbā, it is his in life and in death."
