He said: Ruqbā is when one says to the other: It is for the one of us who outlives the other.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man has more right to his gift as long as he has not been compensated for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: His grandmother,
Khayrah, the wife of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with some jewelry of hers and said: I have given this in charity. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"It is not permissible for a woman to dispose of her wealth except with her husband's permission. Did you ask Kaʿb's permission?" She said: Yes.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Kaʿb ibn Mālik, her husband, and said:
"Did you permit Khayrah to give her jewelry in charity?" He said: Yes.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted it from her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar gave a horse in charity during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he saw its owner selling it cheaply. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about that, and he said:
"Do not buy back your charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had mounted a man on a horse called Ghamr or Ghamrah, then he saw a colt or filly from its offspring being sold, attributed to his horse, so he forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I gave my mother a garden of mine, and she has died and left no heir other than me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Your charity is secured, and your garden has returned to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A loaned item must be returned, and a loaned milch animal must be given back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is entrusted with a deposit is not liable for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah is with the debtor until he settles his debt, as long as it is not for something Allah dislikes."
He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar used to say to his treasurer: Go and take a loan for me, for I dislike spending a night without Allah being with me, after what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Any man who takes on a debt while intending not to repay it will meet Allah as a thief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever dies owing a dinar or a dirham, it will be paid from his good deeds, for there will be no dinar or dirham [there]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever eases the burden of one in hardship, Allah will ease his affairs in this world and the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever gives respite to one in hardship will have charity for every day, and whoever gives him respite after the debt has fallen due will have the like of it as charity every day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever loves that Allah shade him in His shade, let him give respite to one in hardship or forgive him [part of the debt]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar on a journey, as he was heading to some land of his. Then someone came to him and said, "Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd is gravely ill, so see if you can reach her."

So he set out hurriedly, and with him was a man from Quraysh travelling alongside him. The sun set and he did not pray, though I knew him to be someone who was careful about the prayer. When he delayed, I said, "The prayer, may Allah have mercy on you!"

He turned to me and went on until, at the end of the twilight, he dismounted and prayed Maghrib. Then he called the iqāmah for ʿIshāʾ, when the twilight had already disappeared, and he prayed with us. Then he turned to us and said, "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a hurry on a journey, he did it this way."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun set while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Makkah, so he combined the two prayers at Sarif.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on eighteen journeys, and I never saw him omit the two rakʿahs when the sun passed its zenith, before Ẓuhr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on an errand. He said: I came back and he was praying on his mount, facing toward the east, with his prostration lower than his bowing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah in the year of the Conquest for fifteen days, shortening the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at ʿUsfān, and the polytheists were led by Khālid ibn al-Walīd. We prayed Ẓuhr, and the polytheists said, "We have caught them off guard; we have caught them unaware. If only we had attacked them while they were praying!" Then the verse of shortening the prayer was revealed between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr. When ʿAṣr came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood facing the qiblah, with the polytheists in front of him. One row formed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and after that row another row formed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed and they all bowed; then he prostrated and the row nearest him prostrated, while the others stood guarding them. When these had prayed the two prostrations and stood up, the others who were behind them prostrated. Then the row nearest him moved back to the place of the others, and the last row advanced to the place of the first row. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed and they all bowed; then he prostrated and the row nearest him prostrated, while the others stood guarding them. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the row nearest him sat, the others prostrated; then they all sat, and he gave the salām to all of them. He prayed it at ʿUsfān, and he prayed it on the day of Banū Sulaym.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked Abū Hurayrah, "Did you pray the prayer of fear with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Abū Hurayrah said, "Yes."

Marwān said, "When?" Abū Hurayrah said, "In the year of the expedition of Najd. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for the ʿAṣr prayer, and one group stood with him, while another group stood facing the enemy, with their backs to the qiblah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr, and they all said the takbīr, those with him and those facing the enemy. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed one rakʿah, and the group with him bowed. Then he prostrated and the group next to him prostrated, while the others stood facing the enemy. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and the group with him stood, and they went off to face the enemy, and the group that had been facing the enemy came forward. They bowed and prostrated while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood as he was. Then they stood, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed another rakʿah and they bowed with him, and he prostrated and they prostrated with him. Then the group that had been facing the enemy came forward and bowed and prostrated while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him sat. Then came the salām; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salām and they all gave the salām. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had two rakʿahs, and each man of the two groups had one rakʿah each."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed Ẓuhr in a state of fear. Some of them formed rows behind him and some faced the enemy. He prayed two rakʿahs with them, then gave the salām. Those who had prayed with him went off and took the position of their companions, and those others came and prayed behind him. He prayed two rakʿahs with them, then gave the salām. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had four rakʿahs, and his Companions had two rakʿahs each.
And Ḥasan used to give a ruling accordingly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man praying two rakʿahs after the dawn prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The dawn prayer is two rakʿahs."
The man said, "I had not prayed the two rakʿahs before it, so I prayed them now."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Blessing is in chestnut horses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade inciting animals to fight one another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿAlī] may Allah be pleased with him, said: A mule was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he rode it. ʿAlī said: If we were to breed donkeys with horses, we would have [mules] like this one.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Only those who do not know do that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was walking, a man came with a donkey and said: O Messenger of Allah, ride. And the man stepped back.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
No, you have more right to the front of your mount than I do, unless you give it to me."
The man said: Then I have given it to you. So he rode.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever brings a horse in between two horses."
meaning, while he is not certain that it will win,
"then it is not gambling. But whoever brings a horse in between two horses when he is certain that it will win, then it is gambling."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade handing over a sword while it is drawn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He named him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wore two coats of mail, one over the other, on the day of Uḥud, or he put on two coats of mail.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim sent me to al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib to ask him about the banner
of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what it was like. He said: It was black and square, made of a striped woollen cloth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, when a riding animal was brought to him to ride. When he placed his foot in the stirrup he said: In the name of Allah. When he settled on its back he said: Praise be to Allah. Then he said: {Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it ourselves. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.} Then he said: Praise be to Allah, three times,
then he said: Allah is the Greatest,
three times. Then he said: Glory be to You, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.

Then he laughed. It was said: O Commander of the Faithful, why did you laugh? He said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ do as I have done and then laugh, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you laugh? He said: "
Your Lord is pleased with His servant when he says: Forgive me my sins, knowing that none forgives sins but Me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
A single rider is a devil, two riders are two devils, and three are a company of riders."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to a village called Ubnā and said: "
Go to Ubnā in the morning, then burn it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

When one of you comes upon livestock, if its owner is there, let him ask his permission; if he permits him, let him milk and drink, but not carry any away. If there is no one there, let him call out three times; if anyone answers him, let him ask permission; and if no one answers him, let him milk and drink, but not carry any away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [From] his father, Rāfiʿ ibn ʿAmr al-Ghifārī, who said: I was a boy,
throwing stones at our date palms, or he said the date palms of the Anṣār, and I was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
O boy, and Ibn Kāsib said: he said, O my son, why do you throw stones at the palms?"
He said: I said: To eat. He said: "
Do not throw stones at the palms, and eat what falls at their base."
He said: Then he wiped my head and said: "
O Allah, fill his stomach."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went out on a military expedition, he would say: "
O Allah, You are my support and You are my helper, and with You I fight."
He said: This is a good, gharīb hadith. The meaning of his saying ʿaḍudī is: my aid.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

sent al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin to al-Hurmuzān, and he mentioned the hadith at length. Al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin said: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when he did not fight at the beginning of the day, he would wait until the sun had passed its zenith, the winds blew, and victory descended.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Kill the elders of the polytheists and spare their youths."
The sharkh are the boys who have not yet grown [pubic hair].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mutual imprecation (liʿān) was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī said something about it, then left.
Then a man from his people came to him complaining that he had found a man with his wife.
ʿĀṣim said, "I have been tried with this only because of what I said."
So he took the man to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about what he had found his wife doing. That man was pale, thin-fleshed, with straight hair.
And the one whom he accused of being with his wife was heavily built, with thick calves, tawny, and fleshy. The Prophet ﷺ said, "O Allah, make it clear."
Then she gave birth to a child resembling the man whom her husband had said he had found with her.
So the Prophet ﷺ had them carry out the mutual imprecation between them.
A man said to Ibn ʿAbbās in the gathering, "Is she the one about whom the Prophet ﷺ said,
'If I were to stone anyone without proof, I would stone this woman'?"
He said, "No, that was a woman who openly displayed evil in Islam." Abū Ṣāliḥ and ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf said: "khadlan" [meaning heavily built with thick calves].
label: machine translation

segments_en: He divorced a wife of his while she was menstruating, with one pronouncement of divorce. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to take her back, then keep her until she became pure, then until she menstruated another menstrual period with him, then to let her be until she became pure from her menstruation. Then if he wished to divorce her, he should divorce her when she is pure, before having intercourse with her. That is the waiting period that Allah commanded for divorcing women.

Ibn Rumḥ added in his narration: Whenever ʿAbdullāh was asked about that, he would say to the person, "If you divorced your wife once or twice, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to do this. But if you divorced her three times, then she has become unlawful for you until she marries a husband other than you, and you have disobeyed Allah regarding what He commanded you concerning the divorce of your wife."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
whose husband had died, and they feared for her eye, so they came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked his permission to use kohl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"One of you used to stay in the worst part of her house, in her worst clothes, for a whole year; then when a dog passed by she would throw a piece of dung and come out. So why not [wait] four months and ten days?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿĀʾishah, "Did the Prophet ﷺ forbid eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days?" She said, "He did that only in a year when people were starving,
so he wanted the wealthy to feed the poor.
And we used to set aside the trotters and eat them after fifteen days."
It was said, "What forced you to that?" She laughed and said, "The family of Muhammad ﷺ never ate their fill of wheat bread with a seasoning for three consecutive days until he met Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, who is al-Iskāf, from Qatādah, from Anas,
may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I do not know that the Prophet ﷺ ever ate from a small bowl,
nor was fine bread ever made for him,
nor did he eat at a table."
Qatādah was asked, "Then on what did they eat?" He said, "On a leather mat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A disbelieving guest stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a sheep for him; it was milked and he drank its milk, then another, and he drank it, then another, and he drank it, until he had drunk the milk of seven sheep. Then the next morning he accepted Islam, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a sheep for him; it was milked and he drank its milk, then he ordered another for him but he could not finish it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The believer drinks in one intestine, and the disbeliever drinks in seven intestines."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The Muslim eats in one intestine,
and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A roasted mastigure lizard (ḍabb) was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and placed near him. He stretched out his hand to eat from it, but those present said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, it is the meat of a ḍabb."
So he withdrew his hand from it. Khālid ibn al-Walīd said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, is the ḍabb forbidden?" He said,
"No, but it was not found in the land of my people, so I find myself disliking it."
Then Khālid reached for the ḍabb and ate from it while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked on.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah granted Khaybar to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as spoils, he divided it into thirty-six shares in total. He set aside half for the Muslims, eighteen shares, each share consisting of one hundred, and the Prophet ﷺ was among them, having a share like that of any one of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set aside the other eighteen shares, which was the half, for his needs and for whatever affairs of the Muslims might befall him. That was al-Waṭīḥ, al-Katībah, al-Sulālim and their dependencies. When the properties came into the hands of the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims, they had no workers to spare them the labor of working them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the Jews and made an arrangement with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah granted Khaybar to His Prophet ﷺ as spoils, he divided it into thirty-six shares, each share consisting of one hundred shares. He set aside half of it for his needs and whatever might befall him: al-Waṭīḥah, al-Katībah and what was joined with them. He set aside the other half and divided it among the Muslims: al-Shaqq, al-Naṭāh and what was joined with them. The share of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among what was joined with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And some,

of the descendants of Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, said: A remnant of the people of Khaybar remained, having fortified themselves. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to spare their blood and to send them into exile, and he did so. The people of Fadak heard of that and surrendered on the same terms. So Fadak belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ exclusively, because no horses or riding camels had been driven against it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Khaybar by force after fighting, and that those of its people who surrendered did so on condition of exile after the fighting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a fifth of Khaybar, then divided the rest among those who were present at it and those of the people of al-Ḥudaybiyah who were absent from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ camped at Marr al-Ẓahrān, al-ʿAbbās said: I said, "By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ enters Makkah by force before they come to him and ask for his protection, it will be the destruction of Quraysh." So I sat on the mule of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Perhaps I will find someone in need who will go to the people of Makkah and tell them where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is, so that they may come out to him and ask for his protection." While I was riding, I heard the voices of Abū Sufyān and Budayl ibn Warqāʾ. I said, "O Abū Ḥanẓalah!" He recognized my voice and said, "Abū al-Faḍl?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "What is the matter? May my father and mother be your ransom!" I said, "This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the people with him."

He said, "Then what is the way out?" He mounted behind me and his companion went back. In the morning I took him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he accepted Islam. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Sufyān is a man who loves this honor, so give him something." He said,
"Yes. Whoever enters the house of Abū Sufyān is safe, whoever shuts his door upon himself is safe, and whoever enters the Mosque is safe."
So the people dispersed to their houses and to the Mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir whether they had taken any spoils on the day of the Conquest. He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah, he sent al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ and Khālid ibn al-Walīd with the cavalry, and he said,
"O Abū Hurayrah, call the Anṣār."
He said, "Take this road, and let no one show himself to you except that you put him down."
Then a caller cried out, "There is no Quraysh after today."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever enters a house is safe, and whoever lays down his weapon is safe."

The nobles of Quraysh made for the Kaʿbah and entered it, and it was crowded with them. The Prophet ﷺ circled the House and prayed behind the Station, then took hold of the two sides of the door, and they came out and pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ upon Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir about the matter of
Thaqīf when they pledged allegiance. He said: They stipulated to the Prophet ﷺ that there would be no charity (ṣadaqah) upon them and no jihad, and he heard the Prophet ﷺ say afterwards,
"They will give charity and fight in jihad when they have accepted Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the delegation of

Thaqīf came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he lodged them in the Mosque so that it would soften their hearts. They stipulated to him that they would not be conscripted, would not pay the tithe, and would not be taxed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"You shall not be conscripted and you shall not pay the tithe, but there is no good in a religion that has no bowing (rukūʿ)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no claiming of children born of fornication in Islam. Whoever engaged in it in the Jāhiliyyah has joined his paternal kin; and whoever claims a child from other than a lawful marriage will neither inherit nor be inherited from."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, was brought a case of a woman who gave birth after three [months]—similar to it—without mentioning Yemen, nor the Prophet ﷺ, nor his statement about making [the man] content with the child.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so is my son; I committed adultery with his mother in the Jāhiliyyah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no such claim in Islam. The matter of the Jāhiliyyah has gone. The child belongs to the marriage bed, and for the adulterer is the stone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My family married me to a Roman slave woman of theirs, and I had relations with her. She gave birth to a black boy like me, and I named him ʿAbdullāh. Then I had relations with her again, and she gave birth to a black boy like me, and I named him ʿUbaydullāh. Then a Roman slave boy of my family called Yūḥannah was tempted by her, and he spoke to her in his foreign tongue, and she gave birth to a boy like a gecko. I said to her, "What is this?" She said, "This is Yūḥannah's."

We brought the matter to ʿUthmān. He asked the two of them and they confessed. He said to them, "Will you be satisfied if I judge between you with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the child belongs to the marriage bed."
I think he said that he flogged her and flogged him, and they were both slaves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman

said, "O Messenger of Allah, this son of mine—my womb was a container for him, my breast a water-skin for him, and my lap a shelter for him. His father has divorced me and wants to take him away from me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"You have more right to him as long as you do not remarry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Quraysh
used to fast on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ during the pre-Islamic period of ignorance.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded fasting it, until fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever wishes, let him fast it,
and whoever wishes, let him not fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ was fasting and the time to break the fast came, and he then slept before breaking it, he would not eat that night or that day until evening. Qays ibn Ṣirmah al-Anṣārī was fasting, and when the time to break the fast came, he went to his wife and said, "Do you have any food?" She said, "No, but I will go and look for some for you."
He had been working that day, and sleep overcame him. His wife came, and when she saw him she said, "What a disappointment for you!"
When midday came, he fainted. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed:
"It has been made lawful for you, on the night of fasting, to go in to your wives." So they rejoiced greatly over it.
"And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed, "And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread," he said: When a man wanted to fast, he would tie a black thread and a white thread to his feet, and he would keep eating and drinking until he could tell the two apart by sight. Then Allah afterwards revealed "of the dawn," and so they knew that what was meant by that was the night and the day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my mother has died,
and she owed a month of fasting.
Should I make it up on her behalf?" He said:
"Yes. The debt owed to Allah is more deserving of being paid."
Sulaymān said: Al-Ḥakam and Salamah said,
while we were all sitting when Muslim narrated this hadith: We heard Mujāhid mention this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
And it is mentioned from Abū Khālid: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam and Muslim al-Baṭīn,
and Salamah ibn Kuhayl,
from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
that a woman said to the Prophet ﷺ, "My sister has died."
Yaḥyā and Abū Muʿāwiyah said: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Saʿīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that a woman said to the Prophet ﷺ, "My mother has died."
ʿUbaydullāh said, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah, from al-Ḥakam, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: A woman said to the Prophet ﷺ, "My mother has died, and she owed fasting that she had vowed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade continuous fasting without breaking the fast at night, and a man among the Muslims said to him, "But you practice continuous fasting, O Messenger of Allah!" He said:
"And which of you is like me? I spend the night while my Lord feeds me and gives me drink."
When they refused to stop continuous fasting, he fasted continuously with them for a day, and then another day,
then they saw the new moon, and he said:
"If it had been delayed, I would have made you continue longer," as a rebuke to them,
when they refused to stop.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a bond of brotherhood between Salmān and Abū ad-Dardāʾ. Salmān visited Abū ad-Dardāʾ and saw Umm ad-Dardāʾ in shabby clothes. He said, "What is the matter with you?" She said, "Your brother Abū ad-Dardāʾ has no need of this world."
He said: When Abū ad-Dardāʾ came, he brought food to Salmān and said, "Eat, for I am fasting."
Salmān said, "I will not eat until you eat."
So he ate. When night came, Abū ad-Dardāʾ went to get up to pray, and Salmān said to him, "Sleep."
So he slept, then went to get up again, and Salmān said to him, "Sleep."

He slept, and when it was near dawn, Salmān said to him, "Get up now." So they both rose and prayed. Then he said, "Your self has a right over you, your Lord has a right over you, your guest has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give everyone with a right his due."
Then they came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said to him, "Salmān spoke the truth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ did not fast more in any month than in Shaʿbān,
for he used to fast all of Shaʿbān, and he would say:
"Take on only as many deeds as you can bear,
for Allah does not grow weary until you grow weary."
The prayer most beloved to the Prophet ﷺ was the one done regularly, even if it was little.
And whenever he prayed a prayer, he would keep to it regularly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he would take him and al-Ḥasan and say,
"O Allah, I love them both, so love them."
Or as he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While he was with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Ayman entered and did not complete his bowing or his prostration, so [Ibn ʿUmar] said, "Repeat it."
When he left, Ibn ʿUmar said to me, "Who is this?" I said, "Al-Ḥajjāj ibn Ayman, the son of Umm Ayman."
Ibn ʿUmar said, "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen this man, he would have loved him,"
and he mentioned his love for him and for what Umm Ayman had borne.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥafṣah [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ said to her,
"Indeed ʿAbdullāh is a righteous man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: So he began to poke [it] with a stick,
and he said something about its beauty.
Anas said, "He was the one who most resembled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among them,"
and he had dyed [his hair] with wasmah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī: Anas informed me,
He said: No one resembled the Prophet ﷺ more than al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar used to say, "Abū Bakr is our master, and he freed our master," meaning Bilāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Bilāl said] to Abū Bakr, "If you bought me for yourself, then keep me,
but if you bought me for Allah, then leave me to the work of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Teach him the Book."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah prayed one rakʿah of Witr after the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and a freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās was with him.
He went to Ibn ʿAbbās, who said, "Leave him,
for he was a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah fell ill,
so Ibn ʿAbbās came and said, "O Mother of the Believers,
you are going to meet your forerunners of truth: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and ʿĀʾishah set out for Basrah, ʿAlī sent ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī,
and they came to us at Kufa and ascended the pulpit.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī was at the top of the pulpit,
and ʿAmmār stood below al-Ḥasan.
We gathered around him, and I heard ʿAmmār say, "ʿĀʾishah has set out for Basrah,
and by Allah, she is the wife of your Prophet ﷺ in this world and the Hereafter,
but Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is testing you
to know whether you obey Him or her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Anas, "Tell me, was the name 'the Anṣār' one you called yourselves,
or did Allah name you with it?" He said, "Rather, Allah named us."
We used to visit Anas, and he would narrate to us the merits of the Anṣār and their battles,
and he would turn to me, or to a man from al-Azd, and say, "Your people did such and such on such and such a day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The day of Buʿāth was a day Allah brought forward for His Messenger ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived [in Madinah] when their assembly had split apart, their nobles had been killed, and they had been wounded,
so Allah brought it forward for His Messenger ﷺ, leading to their entering Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Anṣār [said] that every people have followers,
and that we have followed you,
so supplicate to Allah that He make our followers part of us. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"O Allah, make their followers part of them."
ʿAmr said: I mentioned it to Ibn Abī Laylā.
He said: Zayd claimed that.
Shuʿbah said: I think he was Zayd ibn Arqam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed the best of the households of the Anṣār is the household of Banū al-Najjār,
then ʿAbd al-Ashhal,
then the household of Banū al-Ḥārith,
then Banū Sāʿidah,
and in all the households of the Anṣār there is good."

Then Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah caught up with us and said, "Abū Usayd, did you not see that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ ranked the Anṣār and put us last?" Saʿd reached the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
you ranked the households of the Anṣār and put us last." He said,
"Is it not enough for you to be among the best?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah and met ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, may Allah be pleased with him, who said, "Won't you come so I can feed you barley meal and dates,
and you can enter a house?" Then he said, "You are in a land where usury is widespread.
If you are owed a right by a man and he gives you a gift of a load of straw,
or a load of barley, or a load of fodder, do not take it, for it is usury."
Al-Naḍr, Abū Dāwūd and Wahb did not mention "the house" from Shuʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Mirbaʿ al-Anṣārī came to us while we were at ʿArafah, in a place that ʿAmr described as being far from the Imam. He said: "I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to you. He says to you:
'Stay at your sacred sites, for you are on an inheritance from the inheritance of your father Ibrāhīm.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at ʿArafah. Some people, or a group, from the people of Najd came and told a man to call out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How is Hajj performed?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed a man to call out:

"Hajj is ʿArafah day. Whoever arrives before the dawn prayer on the night of Jamʿ has completed his Hajj. The days of Minā are three; whoever hastens on in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him."
He said: Then he had a man ride behind him, who began calling out that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Muzdalifah when he went out to the prayer. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have come from the two mountains of Ṭayyiʾ. I have exhausted my mount and tired myself out. By Allah, I did not leave a single sand-hill without standing upon it. Do I have a Hajj?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever attends this prayer of ours and stays with us until we depart, and had already stood at ʿArafah before that, by night or by day, has completed his Hajj and fulfilled his rites."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave permission to the camel herders to stay away from spending the night [at Minā], to stone on the Day of Sacrifice, then to combine the stoning of two days after the Day of Sacrifice, stoning for both on one of them.
Mālik said: I think he said: on the first of the two. Then they stone on the day of departure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Any woman whom two guardians marry off belongs to the first of them, and any man who sells a sale to two men, it belongs to the first of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given the comprehensive words of goodness and its conclusions, or he said, the openings of goodness. He taught us the sermon of prayer and the sermon of need. The sermon of prayer: "All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger."

The sermon of need: "Indeed, all praise is for Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and seek His forgiveness. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide, and whomever He misguides, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger."

Then you connect your sermon with three verses from the Book of Allah: {O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared} to the end of the verse; {And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs} to the end of the verse; {Fear Allah and speak a word that is right. He will rectify your deeds for you and forgive you your sins} to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has two wives and inclines to one of them over the other will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of his body hanging down."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to divide his time among his wives, and he was just. Then he would say:
"O Allah, this is my doing in what I have control over, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not."
Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated it as a mursal report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when a roasted sheep was brought. He said: "Eat."
Some of the people moved aside, and one said: "I am fasting."
ʿAmmār said: "Whoever fasts the day about which people are in doubt has disobeyed Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: meaning al-Juʿfī, from Zāʾidah,
al-Maʿnā, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have seen the new moon." Al-Ḥasan said in his narration, meaning of Ramaḍān. He said:
"Do you bear witness that there is no god but Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said:
"Do you bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said:
"O Bilāl, announce to the people that they should fast tomorrow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The dead person is brought to the grave, and the righteous man sits up in his grave, neither frightened nor disturbed. Then it is said to him:
"What were you upholding?" He says:
"I was upholding Islam." Then it is said to him:
"Who is this man?" He says:
"Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He came to us with clear proofs from Allah, and we believed him." Then it is said to him:
"Have you seen Allah?" He says:
"It is not fitting for anyone to see Allah."
Then an opening is made for him toward the Fire, and he looks at it, its parts crashing against one another. It is said to him:
"Look at what Allah has protected you from."
Then an opening is made for him toward Paradise, and he looks at its bloom and what is in it. It is said to him: "This is your seat." And it is said to him:
"You lived upon certainty, you died upon it, and you will be raised upon it, if Allah wills."
The evil man sits in his grave, frightened and disturbed, and it is said to him:
"What were you upholding?" He says: "I do not know." Then it is said to him:
"Who is this man?" He says:
"I heard people saying something, so I said it."
Then an opening is made for him toward Paradise, and he looks at its bloom and what is in it. It is said to him:
"Look at what Allah has turned away from you."
Then an opening is made for him toward the Fire, and he looks at it, its parts crashing against one another. It is said to him:
"This is your seat. You lived upon doubt, you died upon it, and you will be raised upon it, if Allah the Exalted wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the dead person is placed in the grave, the sun is made to appear to him as it is setting. He sits up wiping his eyes and says: 'Leave me alone, let me pray.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The two who hold the Trumpet have in their hands—or: in their hands are—two horns, and they keep watching, waiting for when they will be commanded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Banū Layth—he said: and he was raised in the care of Abū Saʿīd—said: I heard him, meaning Abū Saʿīd,
saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Bridge (Ṣirāṭ) will be set up over the midst of Hell, upon thorns like the thorns of the saʿdān plant. Then the people will pass over: some will be saved and safe; some will be scratched yet pass through; then some will be saved; some will be held back on it; and some will be overturned into it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You will come to me at the Basin with bright faces and bright limbs from ablution. This is the mark of my community; no one else has it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"On the Day of Resurrection a prophet will come with one man, another prophet will come with two men, another prophet will come with three, and more than that and fewer. It will be said to him: 'Did you convey the message to your people?' He will say: 'Yes.'
Then his people will be called and it will be said: 'Did he convey it to you?' They will say: 'No.'
It will be said: 'Who testifies for you?' He will say: 'Muhammad and his community.'
So the community of Muhammad will be called and it will be said: 'Did this one convey the message?' They will say: 'Yes.'
He will say: 'How do you know that?' They will say: 'Our Prophet informed us that the messengers had indeed conveyed the message, and we believed him.'
He said: That is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {And thus We have made you a middle community, so that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We returned with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:

"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is no servant who believes and then stays upright except that he will be led along the path to Paradise. I hope that they will not enter it until you and those of your offspring who are righteous have settled into dwellings in Paradise. And my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my community into Paradise without reckoning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection, seventy communities will be completed, and we are the last of them and the best of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "We are the last of the nations and the first to be judged. It will be said: 'Where is the unlettered community and its prophet?' So we are the last and the first."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When Allah gathers the creation on the Day of Resurrection, He will permit the community of Muhammad to prostrate, and they will prostrate to Him for a long time. Then it will be said: 'Raise your heads. We have made your number a ransom for you from the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"This community is a community shown mercy; its punishment is in its own hands. When the Day of Resurrection comes, a man from the polytheists will be handed over to each Muslim, and it will be said: 'This is your ransom from the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made supplication, he would begin with himself, and he said:

"May the mercy of Allah be upon us and upon Moses. Had he been patient, he would have seen wonders from his companion. But he said: 'If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion; you have already received an excuse from me.'" Ḥamzah narrated it at greater length.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A man from the people of ʿIlliyyīn will look down upon the people of Paradise, and Paradise will light up because of his face, as though it were a shining star."
He said: This is how the hadith came: "shining" (durrī).
The letter dāl has a ḍammah and is not pronounced with a hamzah.
"And indeed Abū Bakr and ʿUmar are among them, and they are well deserving of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned the hadith. A man from the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us about Sabaʾ: is it a land or a woman?" He said:
"It is neither a land nor a woman, but a man who had ten children among the Arabs. Six of them settled toward the right (Yemen) and four toward the left (Syria)."
ʿUthmān al-Ghaṭafānī said "al-Ghaṭafānī" in place of "al-Ghuṭayfī," and he said: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥakam al-Nakhaʿī narrated to us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ — Ismāʿīl said, from Abū Hurayrah, as a narration — he mentioned the hadith about revelation. He said: That is the meaning of His statement, the Exalted: "Until, when fear is removed from their hearts..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: The recitation of the Prophet ﷺ was: "Yes, My signs did come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers." Abū Dāwūd said: This is a mursal narration; al-Rabīʿ did not meet Umm Salamah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ recite it: "Then [there will be] rest (rawḥ) and fragrance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ recite: "He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From one to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught the recitation: "On that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated a hadith in which he mentioned "Jibrīl and Mīkāl."
Then he recited it: "Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: How the recitation "Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl" is read was mentioned in the presence of al-Aʿmash. Al-Aʿmash narrated to us from Saʿd al-Ṭāʾī, from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the one who blows the Trumpet, and he said:
"On his right is Jibrāʾīl and on his left is Mīkāʾīl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She mentioned, or said something similar, the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment." He would pause his recitation verse by verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Maysarah,
— the meaning is the same — both said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us,
from Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn,
from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah,
from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father,
from Abū Dharr,
who said: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a donkey while the sun was setting, and he said:
"Do you know where this sets?"
I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"It sets in a spring of hot, murky water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to them in the porch of the Muhājirūn, and a person asked him: "Which verse in the Qur'an is the greatest?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"'Allah! There is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He recited: "Hayta lak." Shaqīq said: "We recite it 'Hiʾtu lak.'" Ibn Masʿūd said: "I prefer to recite it as I was taught."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to ʿAbdullāh: "Some people recite this verse: 'And she said, Hayta lak.'" He said: "I recite as I was taught, and that is dearer to me: 'And she said, Hayta lak.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he recited to us: "[This is] a sūrah which We have sent down and made obligatory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some women from the people of Syria entered upon ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she said: "Where are you from?" They said: "From the people of Syria."
She said: "Perhaps you are from the district whose women enter the public baths?" They said: "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was carrying a heavy stone, and as I was walking, my garment fell off me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Take your garment and put it on, and do not walk about naked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man must not lie with a man in one garment, nor a woman with a woman, except a child with a parent."
He said: And he mentioned a third, but I forgot it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave a horse in charity for the cause of Allah, then he found it being sold,
and he wanted to buy it.
So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked his advice, and he said:
"Do not take back your charity."
For this reason Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, would never buy anything he had given in charity without making it charity [again].
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,

that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory the zakāh of Fiṭr at the end of Ramaḍān upon the people: one ṣāʿ of dates or one ṣāʿ of barley, upon every free person or slave, male or female, among the Muslims.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from Sulaymān ibn Yasār,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās,

who said: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a woman from Khathʿam came to ask him for a ruling. Al-Faḍl began looking at her and she at him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began turning Al-Faḍl's face to the other side. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah's obligation of Hajj upon His servants has come upon my father when he is an old man who cannot stay firmly seated on the mount. May I perform Hajj on his behalf?" He said: "Yes."
And that was during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ dictated to me that he heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When two parties make a sale, each of them has the option [to cancel] the sale as long as they have not separated, or if their sale was made with an option. If their sale was made with an option, then it has become binding."
Ibn Abī ʿUmar added in his narration: Nāfiʿ said: When [Ibn ʿUmar] made a sale with a man and wanted it not to be cancelled, he would get up and walk a little, then return to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We flushed out a hare at Marr al-Ẓahrān,
and the people ran after it but grew tired. I caught up with it and seized it,
then I brought it to Abū Ṭalḥah, who slaughtered it,
and he sent its rump, or its two thighs (he said "its two thighs" without doubt), to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he accepted it.
I said: "And did he eat from it?" He said: "And he ate from it."
Then he said afterwards: "He accepted it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who takes back his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit."
Hammām said: Qatādah said: "And we do not know vomit to be anything but unlawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Salamah [narrated] that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day: "O ʿĀʾish,
this is Jibrīl, who greets you with peace."
I said: "And upon him be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings,
you see what I do not see."
She meant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: When I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then to fall from the sky is dearer to me than to attribute to him what he did not say. But when I speak to you about matters between me and you, then war is deception.
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"In the last days there will emerge a people young in age and foolish in thought. They will speak with the best of what people say. They will recite the Qur'an, but it will not go beyond their throats. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target. So when you meet them, kill them, for in killing them there is a reward for whoever kills them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit me. He found that I had lost consciousness. He came with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, both on foot. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution and poured some of his ablution water over me, and I came to. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should I settle my wealth?" or "What should I do with my wealth?" He did not answer me at all. He had nine sisters, until the verse of inheritance was revealed:
"They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the one who leaves no parent or child (kalālah)..." the verse.
Jābir said: It was revealed concerning me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with these words:

"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Fire and the punishment of the Fire, the punishment of the grave and the trial of the grave, from the evil of the trial of wealth, from the evil of the trial of poverty, and from the evil of the trial of the Antichrist (al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl). O Allah, wash my sins away with the water of snow and hail, and cleanse my heart of sins as You have cleansed the white garment of dirt, and put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the east and the west. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness, decrepit old age, sin, and debt."
He said: This is a sound, good hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade striking the face and branding the face.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I have a co-wife. Would I be at fault if I make a show of being given more than my husband has actually given me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who makes a show of what he has not been given is like one who wears two garments of falsehood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Najrān, and they said to me, "Do you not recite:
'O sister of Hārūn' [Qur'an 19:28], when there was between ʿĪsā and Mūsā what there was?" I did not know how to answer them.
So I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said:
"Why did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after their prophets and the righteous people before them?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A daughter of ʿUmar
was called ʿĀṣiyah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named her Jamīlah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab bint Abī Salamah
asked him, "What have you named your daughter?" He said, "I named her Barrah." She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade this name; I had been named Barrah, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
'Do not declare yourselves pure; Allah knows best who among you are the righteous.'"
He said, "Then what shall we name her?" He said, "Name her Zaynab."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I took ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he was born. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a cloak, treating a camel of his with tar, and he said:
"Do you have any dates with you?" I said, "Yes."

I handed him some dates; he put them in his mouth and chewed them, then opened the baby's mouth and put the chewed dates into it. The baby began to smack his lips over it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Anṣār's love is for dates."
And he named him ʿAbdullāh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "As-sāmu ʿalayka [death be upon you], O Abū al-Qāsim." He said, "And upon you."
ʿĀʾishah said, "I said, 'Rather, upon you be death and disgrace.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, do not be coarse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Your permission to come to me is that the curtain be lifted and that you listen to my private words, until I forbid you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She (may Allah be pleased with her) said: An effeminate man used to enter the quarters of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and they considered him one of those without sexual desire. One day the Prophet ﷺ came in while he was with one of his wives, and he was describing a woman, saying, "When she approaches, she approaches with four [folds], and when she turns away, she turns away with eight." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do I not see that this one knows what is here? Do not let him enter upon you." So they kept him out of sight.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The evil eye is real. If anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it. And if you are asked to wash, then wash."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When any of us fell ill, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would wipe him with his right hand and then say:
"Remove the harm, Lord of the people, and heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill and grew heavy, I took his hand to do for him what he used to do, but he pulled his hand away from mine and said:
"O Allah, forgive me and place me with the highest companions."
She said: I went to look, and he had passed away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A family of the Anṣār called the family of ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm used to perform ruqyah for venomous stings, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden ruqyah. They came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have forbidden ruqyah, and we perform ruqyah for venomous stings." He said to them, "Present it to me."
So they presented it to him, and he said:
"There is no harm in this. These are pledges."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to perform ruqyah in the Days of Ignorance, so we said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is your view on that?" He said:
"Present your ruqyahs to me. There is no harm in ruqyah as long as it contains no polytheism."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a pain he had felt in his body since he became Muslim.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Place your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say, 'In the name of Allah,' three times.
And say seven times: 'I seek refuge in Allah and in His power from the evil of what I feel and fear.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
entered the mosque on a Friday through the door facing the Dār al-Qaḍāʾ,
while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing delivering the sermon.
He stood facing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off.
Pray to Allah to send us rain." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said, "O Allah, give us rain! O Allah, give us rain! O Allah, give us rain!"
Anas said: By Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, nor even a wisp of cloud,
and there was no house or building between us and the mountain of Salʿ.
He said: Then a cloud like a shield appeared from behind it,
and when it reached the middle of the sky it spread out and then it rained.
By Allah, we did not see the sun for six days.
Then a man entered through that same door on the next Friday while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing delivering the sermon,
and he stood facing him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off.
Pray to Allah to hold it back from us."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and then said,
"O Allah, around us and not upon us.
O Allah, upon the hills, the mounds, the bottoms of the valleys, and the places where trees grow."
He said: Then it cleared, and we went out walking in the sun.
Sharīk said: I asked Anas ibn Mālik, "Was he the first man?" He said, "I do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the rain, he would say:
"O Allah, make it a beneficial, wholesome downpour."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until knowledge is taken away, earthquakes become frequent, time becomes shorter, and trials appear,
and harj increases—and that is killing, killing—until wealth becomes abundant among you and overflows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray and made the standing very long. Then he bowed and made the bowing very long. Then he raised his head and made the standing very long, though it was shorter than the first standing. Then he bowed and made the bowing very long, though it was shorter than the first bowing. Then he prostrated. Then he stood and made the standing long, though it was shorter than the first standing. Then he bowed and made the bowing long, though it was shorter than the first bowing. Then he raised his head and stood and made the standing long, though it was shorter than the first standing. Then he bowed and made the bowing long, though it was shorter than the first bowing. Then he prostrated. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said:

"The sun and the moon are among the signs of Allah, and they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life. So when you see them, say takbīr, call upon Allah, pray, and give charity. O community of Muḥammad, there is no one more jealous than Allah that His servant should commit adultery or His maidservant should commit adultery. O community of Muḥammad, by Allah, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. Have I not conveyed [the message]?"
In the narration of Mālik:
"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish woman
came asking her [ʿĀʾishah] for something and said, "May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave."
So ʿĀʾishah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Are people punished in their graves?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "I seek refuge in Allah from that."
Then one morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode out on a mount,
and the sun was eclipsed, so he returned in the forenoon.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed between the rooms,
then stood and prayed,
and the people stood behind him.
He stood for a long time,
then bowed for a long time,
then rose and stood for a long time,
though it was shorter than the first standing.
Then he bowed for a long time,
though it was shorter than the first bowing.
Then he rose and prostrated for a long time. Then he stood and stood for a long time,
though it was shorter than the first standing.
Then he bowed for a long time,
though it was shorter than the first bowing.
Then he stood for a long time,
though it was shorter than the first standing.
Then he bowed for a long time,
though it was shorter than the first bowing.
Then he prostrated, though it was shorter than the first prostration.
Then he finished, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said what Allah willed him to say,
and then he commanded them to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the call was made: "The prayer is being gathered!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed twice in one rakʿah, then stood and bowed twice in another rakʿah, and then the sun cleared. ʿĀʾishah said: I never bowed a bowing nor prostrated a prostration that was longer than it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, pronouncing the talbiyah for Hajj alone, and ʿĀʾishah came pronouncing it for ʿUmrah. When she reached Sarif, she began her menses. When we arrived [in Makkah], we circled the Kaʿbah and [walked between] Ṣafā and Marwah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded those of us who had not brought a sacrificial animal to come out of ihrām. He said: We said, "Release from what exactly?" He said, "Complete release."

So we approached our wives, applied perfume, and put on our [ordinary] clothes, when there were only four nights between us and ʿArafah. Then on the Day of Tarwiyah we pronounced the talbiyah [for Hajj]. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went in to ʿĀʾishah and found her weeping. He said, "What is the matter with you?"
She said, "My situation is that I have started my menses, the people have come out of ihrām while I have not, I have not circled the House, and the people are now going to Hajj." He said,
"This is a matter which Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. So bathe, then pronounce the talbiyah for Hajj." And she did so.
She stood at the standing places, and when she became pure she circled the House and [walked between] Ṣafā and Marwah. Then he said,
"You are now released from both your Hajj and your ʿUmrah."
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I feel in myself that I did not circle the House when I performed Hajj." He said,
"Take her, O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and let her perform ʿUmrah from Tanʿīm."
And that was the night of al-Ḥaṣbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to give rulings in favor of the temporary combination [of ʿUmrah and Hajj] (mutʿah), so a man said to him, "Go easy with some of your rulings, for you do not know what the Commander of the Faithful has since introduced regarding the rites," until he met him afterward and asked him. ʿUmar said, "I know that the Prophet ﷺ did it, and his Companions [too], but I disliked that they would spend the night with their wives under the arāk trees and then go out for Hajj with their heads dripping."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pronouncing the talbiyah for Hajj. When we drew near to Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever has no sacrificial animal with him should come out of ihrām, and whoever has a sacrificial animal with him should remain in his ihrām."

She said: Al-Zubayr had a sacrificial animal with him, so he remained in ihrām. I had no sacrificial animal, so I came out of ihrām, put on my clothes, applied my perfume, and then sat beside al-Zubayr. He said, "Move away from me."
I said, "Do you fear that I will pounce on you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he marked the sacrificial animal on the right side of its hump, then wiped the blood from it, then hung two sandals on it as a garland. Then he mounted his she-camel, and when it stood upright with him on al-Baydāʾ, he entered ihrām for Hajj. He entered ihrām at noon and pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Muʿāwiyah said to me, "Did you know that I trimmed the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Marwah with a broad arrowhead?" I said to him, "I only know this as a proof against you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walk briskly from the [Black] Stone to the [Black] Stone until he reached it, for three circuits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet ﷺ circled the House, and [walked between] Ṣafā and Marwah, on his mount so that the people could see him, so that he would be visible, and so that they could ask him, for the people crowded around him.
Ibn Khashram did not mention "and so that they could ask him" only.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was settled in Makkah in the year of the Conquest, he circled [the House] on a camel, touching the corner with a curved staff in his hand.
She said: And I was watching him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off from ʿArafāt, and when he reached the mountain pass he dismounted and urinated. Usāmah did not say "he released water." He said: Then he called for water and performed a light ablution. He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, the prayer?" He said, "The prayer is ahead of you."
He said: Then he went on until he reached Jamʿ, and he prayed the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked Usāmah ibn Zayd: "Tell me how

you did"—or "how you acted"—"on the evening when you rode behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: We came to the pass where people make their camels kneel for the night halt, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made his she-camel kneel, then urinated. Zuhayr did not say "he released water." Then he called for ablution water and performed an ablution that was not very thorough. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, the prayer?" He said, "The prayer is ahead of you."

He said: Then he mounted and rode until we reached Muzdalifah. He called the iqāmah for Maghrib, then the people made their camels kneel at their stopping places, and they did not unload until the iqāmah was called for ʿIshāʾ and he prayed; then the people unloaded.
Muḥammad added in his narration: I said, "What did you do when morning came?" He said, "Al-Faḍl rode behind him, and I set off on foot with the Quraysh runners."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Thābit came out from Marwān's presence at midday, and I said, "He did not send for him at this hour except about something he asked him."
So I asked him, and he said, "He asked us about things we had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Whoever makes this world his main concern, Allah will scatter his affairs for him and place his poverty before his eyes, and nothing of this world will come to him except what has been decreed for him. And whoever makes the Hereafter his intention, Allah will gather his affairs for him, place his richness in his heart, and the world will come to him humbled.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship and I will fill your chest with richness and remedy your poverty. If you do not, I will fill your hands with preoccupation and will not remedy your poverty.'"
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
And Abū Khālid al-Wālibī's name is Hurmuz.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We, the family of Muhammad ﷺ, would stay a month without lighting a fire; it was only dates and water.
Except that Ibn Numayr said, "We would remain a month."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I was made to fear in the cause of Allah as no one else is made to fear, and I was harmed in the cause of Allah as no one else is harmed. Thirty days and nights have passed me by when neither I nor Bilāl had any food that a living creature could eat, except a little that Bilāl's armpit could hide."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were struck by hunger, and they were seven. He said: The Prophet ﷺ gave me seven dates, one date for each person.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man belched in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Hold back your belching from us, for the one who will be hungriest on the Day of Resurrection is the one among you who was fullest in the life of this world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, the people rushed toward him, and it was said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has arrived! The Messenger of Allah has arrived! The Messenger of Allah has arrived!"
Three times. So I came among the people to see, and when I looked closely at his face, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing I heard him say was:
"O people, spread the greeting of peace, feed food, maintain family ties, and pray at night while people sleep; you will enter Paradise in peace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man met the Prophet ﷺ and shook his hand, he would not withdraw his hand from the man's hand until the man was the one to withdraw it, and he would not turn his face away from the man's face until the man was the one to turn away. And he was never seen putting his knees forward in front of a companion sitting with him.
He said: This is a gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O My servants, all of you are astray except those I have guided, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you. All of you are poor except those I have enriched, so ask Me and I will provide for you. All of you are sinners except those I have pardoned; so whoever among you knows that I have power to forgive and seeks My forgiveness, I will forgive him, and I do not mind. Even if the first of you and the last of you, the living and the dead, the fresh and the dry, were to gather upon the most God-fearing heart of any of My servants, that would not increase My dominion by the wing of a mosquito. And if the first of you and the last of you, the living and the dead, the fresh and the dry, were to gather upon the most wretched heart of any of My servants, that would not decrease My dominion by the wing of a mosquito. And if the first of you and the last of you, the living and the dead, the fresh and the dry, were to gather on one plain, and every one of you asked for whatever his wish reached, and I gave every asker what he asked, that would not diminish My dominion except as if one of you passed by the sea and dipped a needle in it and then lifted it out. That is because I am Generous and Glorious; I do what I will. My gift is speech and My punishment is speech. My command, when I will a thing, is only to say to it "Be," and it is.'"
He said: This is a ḥasan hadith.
And some of them narrated this hadith from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Maʿdīkarib, from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Every son of Adam is prone to error, and the best of those who err are those who repent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The Muslim who mixes with people and is patient with their harm is better than the Muslim who does not mix with people and is not patient with their harm."
Abū Mūsā said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī said, "Shuʿbah held that he was Ibn ʿUmar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent a night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and I said to her, "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gets up, wake me."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up, and I stood at his left side. He took my hand and placed me on his right side. Whenever I dozed off, he would take hold of my earlobe. He said: Then he prayed eleven units (rakʿahs), then sat wrapping his arms around his knees, until I could hear his breathing as he rested. Then, when dawn became clear to him, he prayed two brief units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salamah said: I met Kurayb, and he said that Ibn ʿAbbās said, "I was at my maternal aunt Maymūnah's house, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came."
Then he mentioned it like the hadith of Ghundar. And he said, "and make me a light," without expressing any doubt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and we came to a watering place. He said:
"Will you not go down to the water, Jābir?"

I said, "Yes." He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted and I went down to the water. He said: Then he went to relieve himself, and I set out water for his ablution. He said: He came and performed ablution, then stood and prayed in a single garment, crossing its two ends over each other. I stood behind him, and he took hold of my ear and placed me on his right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.

As for the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, its wording agrees with the hadith of Mālik; they differ only in two words: in place of "qiyām," Ibn Jurayj said "qayyim," and he said "and what I concealed." As for the hadith of Ibn ʿUyaynah, it contains some additions and differs from Mālik and Ibn Jurayj in several words.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The likeness of a house in which Allah is remembered and a house in which Allah is not remembered is like that of the living and the dead."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
Like the hadith of Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, except that Ibn Ayyūb said in his narration, "like his ear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Recite the Qur'an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who recite it. Recite the two bright ones, al-Baqarah and Sūrah Āl ʿImrān, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as if they were two clouds, or two shades, or two flocks of birds in formation, pleading on behalf of those who recite them. Recite Sūrah al-Baqarah, for taking hold of it is a blessing and abandoning it is a cause of regret, and the falsifiers cannot [overcome] it."
Muʿāwiyah said: It has reached me that the falsifiers are the magicians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Nāfiʿ ibn
ʿAbd al-Ḥārith al-Khuzāʿī met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at ʿUsfān.
Like the hadith of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd from al-Zuhrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the mosque when a man came in and prayed, and he recited in a manner that I disapproved of. Then another came in and recited in a manner different from his companion's. When we finished the prayer, we all went in to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I said, "This man recited in a manner that I disapproved of, and another came in and recited differently from his companion." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them, and they recited, and the Prophet ﷺ approved of them both. Then I was seized by a denial in myself such as I had not felt even in the Days of Ignorance. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw what had overcome me, he struck my chest, and I broke out in sweat, and it was as if I were looking at Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in fear. He said to me:
"O Ubayy, it was sent to me to recite the Qur'an in one mode, and I replied to him, 'Make it easy for my nation.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he was sitting in the mosque when a man came in and prayed and recited a recitation; and he related the hadith like the hadith of Ibn Numayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlqamah came to Syria and entered a mosque and prayed in it. Then he stood and went to a circle and sat in it. He said: Then a man came, and I recognized in him the manner and appearance of the people.
He said: He sat beside me and then said, "Do you remember how ʿAbdullāh used to recite?" Then he mentioned it similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the prayer ground on the day of Adhā or Fiṭr,
and passed by the women and said:
"O company of women, give charity,
