for I have been shown that you are the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire."
They said, "And why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands.
I have not seen anyone more deficient in intellect and religion who can overcome the mind of a sensible man than one of you."
They said, "And what is the deficiency in our religion and intellect, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Is the testimony of a woman not equal to half the testimony of a man?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"That is from the deficiency of her intellect.
And is it not the case that when she menstruates she neither prays nor fasts?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"That is from the deficiency of her religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman asked the Prophet ﷺ how she should wash after her menstrual period. He mentioned that he taught her how to wash, then [said] she should take a piece of cotton scented with musk and purify herself with it.
She said, "How should I purify myself with it?" He said, "Purify yourself with it. Glory be to Allah!"

And he covered himself—Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah showed us by gesturing with his hand over his face. ʿĀʾishah said: I pulled her toward me and understood what the Prophet ﷺ meant, so I said, "Trace the marks of blood with it."
Ibn Abī ʿUmar said in his narration: So I said, "Trace the marks of the blood with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to forbid our young women from going out [to the prayer ground].
Then a woman came and stayed at the palace of Banū Khalaf,
and she related that her sister was married to one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who had fought twelve campaigns with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and that her sister had been with him in six of them.
She said: "We used to treat the wounded and look after the sick.
My sister asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Is there any harm for one of us who has no outer garment if she does not go out?" He said:
"Let her companion lend her some of her own garment, and let her witness the good and the supplication of the believers."

When Umm ʿAṭiyyah  may Allah be pleased with her  came, we asked her, or she said: we asked her. She was a woman who never mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without saying, "May my father be ransom for him."
We said, "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say such and such?" She said, "Yes, may my father be his ransom." He said:

"Let the young women who stay in seclusion go out, or the young women and those who stay in seclusion, and the menstruating women, so that they may witness the good and the supplication of the Muslims,
and let the menstruating women keep away from the prayer place." I said, "The menstruating woman?"
She said, "Does she not attend ʿArafah,
and attend such and such, and attend such and such?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [said] that she used to be menstruating and would not pray,
while she lay on a mat beside the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was praying on his small prayer mat,
and when he prostrated, part of his garment would touch me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yasār, the freed slave of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and I came forward

until we entered upon Abū al-Jahm ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṣimmah al-Anṣārī. Abū al-Jahm said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was coming from the direction of Bi'r Jamal when a man met him and greeted him with salām, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not return the greeting until he faced a wall, wiped his face and hands, and then returned the greeting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked al-Zuhrī about the prayer

of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Makkah before the migration to Madinah. He said: ʿUrwah informed me from ʿĀʾishah, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made prayer obligatory upon His Messenger ﷺ, at first, as two rakʿahs each; then it was completed to four for those resident, and the prayer of travel was left upon the first obligation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw men tying their waist wrappers around their necks, because of the scantiness of the wrappers, behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer, like children. Then someone said, "O company of women, do not raise your heads until the men raise theirs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two ways of dressing: that a man sit wrapped in one garment with his private part exposed to the sky, and that he wear his garment with one side hanging out and throw it over his shoulder.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in intense heat, and when one of us was unable to press his forehead to the ground, he would spread out his garment and prostrate on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A trustworthy man said: I asked Anas ibn Mālik, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in his sandals?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he came to a refuse dump of some people and urinated standing. I moved away from him, but he called me, and I stood right behind his heels until he finished. Then he performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Eat the pre-dawn meal, for in the pre-dawn meal there is blessing."
ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd reported it as a statement of the Companion (mawqūf).
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, a man came to him
and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined!" He said, "What is the matter with you?"
He said, "I had intercourse with my wife while I was fasting."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Can you find a slave to set free?" He said, "No." He said: "
Are you able to fast two consecutive months?" He said, "No." He said: "
Can you find [the means] to feed sixty poor people?" He said, "No."
He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ waited.
While we were in that state, a large basket containing dates was brought to the Prophet ﷺ (the ʿaraq is the basket). He said, "Where is the questioner?" The man said, "I am here." He said: "
Take this and give it in charity."
The man said, "To someone poorer than I, O Messenger of Allah? By Allah, there is no household between its two lava plains (he meant the two tracts of volcanic rock) poorer than my household."
The Prophet ﷺ laughed until his eyeteeth showed, and then said, "Feed it to your family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped between Makkah and Madinah while he was in a state of iḥrām and fasting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ad-Dardāʾ said: I remember us being with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his journeys on an extremely hot day, so hot that a man would put his hand on his head because of the intensity of the heat. None of us was fasting except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out from Madinah to Makkah,
and he fasted until he reached ʿUsfān.
Then he called for water and raised it in his hands so that the people could see him, and he broke his fast,
until he arrived in Makkah.
That was in Ramadan. Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted and he also broke his fast,
so whoever wishes may fast,
and whoever wishes may break the fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Do not fast continuously without breaking the fast at night.
If any of you wants to do so, let him continue only until the pre-dawn meal."
They said, "But you fast continuously, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "
I am not like you.
I spend the night with One who feeds me and gives me drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was told that he had said, "I will surely pray at night and fast by day for as long as I live."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Are you the one who says that?"
I said to him, "I did say it, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
You are not able to do that. So fast and break your fast, sleep and rise to pray, and fast three days of each month, for a good deed is rewarded tenfold, and that is like fasting all of time."
He said: I said, "But I am able to do more than that." He said: "
Fast one day and break your fast for two days."
He said: I said, "But I am able to do more than that, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "
Fast one day and break your fast one day. That is the fast of Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and it is the most balanced fasting."
He said: I said, "But I am able to do more than that."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is nothing better than that."
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: To have accepted the three days which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned would be dearer to me than my family and my wealth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The day of ʿĀshūrāʾ was a day which Quraysh used to fast in the Pre-Islamic Period of Ignorance, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also used to fast it in that period. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, he fasted it and commanded that it be fasted. When Ramadan was made obligatory, that became the obligatory fast and ʿĀshūrāʾ was left; so whoever wished fasted it, and whoever wished left it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me one time and said, "Do you have anything?"
She said, "I have nothing." He said, "Then I am fasting."

She said: Then he came to me a second time, after we had been given a gift of ḥays. I brought it to him and he ate, and I was surprised at that. So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you came to me while fasting, and then you ate ḥays?" He said,

"Yes, O ʿĀʾishah. The one who fasts outside Ramadan, or outside making up Ramadan, or in voluntary fasting, is in the position of a man who takes out the charity from his wealth: he is generous with whatever he wishes and gives it away, and is stingy with what remains and holds it back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us one day and we said, "We have been given a gift of ḥays, and we have set aside a share of it for you." He said, "I am fasting." Then he broke his fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon ʿĀʾishah and said,
"Do you have any food?" The rest is similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day and said,
"Do you have any food?" I said, "No." He said, "Then I am fasting."
She said: He entered upon me another time and I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have been given a gift of ḥays." He said,
"Then I will break my fast today, though I had intended to fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not omit fasting the White Days, whether at home or while traveling.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have not seen you fast in any month as you fast in Shaʿbān." He said,
"That is a month which people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan. It is a month in which deeds are raised to the Lord of the worlds, and I love that my deeds be raised while I am fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lay down to sleep, he would place his right palm under his right cheek, and he used to fast on Mondays and Thursdays.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man who fasts all the time. He said,
"I wish he had not eaten at all for all time."
They said, "What about two-thirds of it?" He said, "More."
They said, "Then half of it?" He said, "More." Then he said,
"Shall I not tell you of what removes the rancor of the heart? Fasting three days of every month."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father married me to a woman, and he came to visit her and said, "How do you find your husband?" She said, "An excellent man, who does not sleep at night and does not break his fast by day."
So he rebuked me and said, "I married you to a woman from among the Muslims and you have neglected her."
He said: I paid no attention to his words because of the strength and diligence I saw in myself. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said,
"But I pray at night and I sleep, I fast and I break my fast. So pray and sleep, and fast and break your fast." He said,
"Fast three days of every month."
I said, "I am stronger than that." He said,
"Fast the fast of Dāwūd, peace be upon him: fast one day and break the fast the next."
I said, "I am stronger than that." He said,
"Recite the Qurʾān once every month."
Then he came down to fifteen days, while I kept saying, "I am stronger than that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr and said, "Uncle, tell me what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to you." He said: Nephew, I had resolved to exert myself intensely, so much that I said, "I will surely fast all the time and surely recite the Qurʾān every day and night." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of that and came to me, entering my house, and said,
"It has reached me that you said, 'I will surely fast all the time and surely recite the Qurʾān.'"
I said, "I did say that, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Do not do so. Fast three days of every month."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said,
"Then fast two days of the week, Monday and Thursday."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said,

"Then fast the fast of Dāwūd, peace be upon him, for it is the most balanced fasting in the sight of Allah: a day fasting and a day not fasting. And when he made a promise he did not break it, and when he met the enemy he did not flee."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Negus died, we used to say that a light could still be seen over his grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Cities will be opened up for you,

and there will be mobilized armies, and expeditions will be assigned to you among them. A man among you will dislike being sent on an expedition, so he will free himself from his people, then go around the tribes offering himself to them, saying:
'Who will take my place in the expedition of such-and-such?
Who will take my place in the expedition of such-and-such?' Such a man is a hired hand, down to the last drop of his blood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who fights has his reward,
and the one who equips him has his own reward and the reward of the fighter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave permission for the expedition while I was an old man with no servant,
so I looked for a hired man who would suffice me, and I would give him his share. I found a man,
and when the departure drew near, he came to me and said:
"I do not know what the shares are or how much my share would amount to, so fix something for me, whether there turns out to be a share or not."
So I fixed three dinars for him.
When his spoils came to hand, I wanted to give him his share, but I remembered the dinars,
so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about his case. He said: "
I do not find for him in this expedition of his, in this world and the Hereafter, anything except his dinars that he specified."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
migrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Yemen, and he said: "
Do you have anyone in Yemen?" He said: "My parents." He said: "Did they permit you?" He said: "No." He said: "
Go back to them and ask their permission.
If they permit you, then fight; otherwise, be dutiful to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Three things are among the foundations of faith:
to hold back from whoever says 'There is no god but Allah': do not declare him a disbeliever because of a sin, and do not put him outside Islam because of a deed;

and jihad continues from the time Allah sent me until the last of my nation fights the Dajjāl; it is not nullified by the injustice of an unjust ruler or the justice of a just one; and belief in the divine decrees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he wanted to go on an expedition, and he said: "
O company of the Emigrants and the Helpers,

among your brothers are people who have no wealth and no kinsfolk, so let each of you take two or three men along with him. None of us has a mount to carry him except by turns, like their turns." Meaning one of them.
So I took two or three with me. He said:
I had nothing but a turn on my camel, like the turn of one of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥawālah al-Azdī stayed with me and said to me:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us to gain spoils on foot, but we returned without gaining anything, and the hardship was visible on our faces. He stood among us and said: "
O Allah, do not leave them to me, for I would be too weak for them,
and do not leave them to themselves, for they would be unable,
and do not leave them to the people, for they would prefer themselves over them."
Then he placed his hand on my head, or he said:
on my crown, and then said: "
O Ibn Ḥawālah, when you see the caliphate has settled in the Holy Land, then earthquakes, tribulations and momentous events have drawn near,
and on that day the Hour will be closer to people than this hand of mine is to your head."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Our Lord marvels at a man who fought in the cause of Allah and his companions were routed," meaning his companions: "
and he knew what was upon him, so he went back until his blood was shed.
Then Allah, the Exalted, says to His angels:
Look at My servant: he returned out of desire for what is with Me and fear of what is with Me, until his blood was shed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn Uqaysh
had some usurious dealings from the pre-Islamic period, and he disliked becoming Muslim until he had collected it. Then the day of Uḥud came. He said:
"Where are my cousins?" They said: "At Uḥud." He said:
"Where is so-and-so?" They said: "At Uḥud." He said:
"Where is so-and-so?" They said: "At Uḥud."
So he put on his armor, mounted his horse, and headed toward them.
When the Muslims saw him, they said:
"Keep away from us, O ʿAmr." He said:
"I have believed."
Then he fought until he was wounded,
and he was carried to his family wounded.
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh came to him and said to his sister:
"Ask him: was it out of tribal zeal for your people, or anger on their behalf, or anger for the sake of Allah?" He said:
"Rather, anger for the sake of Allah and His Messenger." Then he died.
He entered Paradise, though he had never prayed a single prayer to Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray Friday prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the sun had passed its zenith, then we would go back, looking for shade.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sermon of the Prophet ﷺ on Friday: he would praise Allah and extol Him, then after that he would speak, with his voice raised.
Then he related the hadith like it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḍimād
came to Makkah. He was from the Azd of Shanūʾah and used to perform ruqyah for this affliction of madness. He heard some foolish people of Makkah saying, "Muḥammad is mad."

He said, "If only I could see this man, perhaps Allah would cure him at my hands." He said: So he met him and said, "O Muḥammad, I perform ruqyah for this affliction, and Allah cures at my hands whomever He wills. Would you like that?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, all praise is for Allah; we praise Him and seek His help. Whoever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whoever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger. To proceed:"
He said: He said, "Repeat these words of yours to me."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated them to him three times. He said: He said, "I have heard the speech of soothsayers, the speech of sorcerers, and the speech of poets, and I have never heard anything like these words of yours. They have reached the depths of the sea." He said: He said, "Give me your hand, that I may pledge allegiance to you upon Islam." He said: So he pledged allegiance to him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "And on behalf of your people."

He said, "And on behalf of my people." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a military detachment, and they passed by his people. The commander of the detachment said to the army, "Did you take anything from these people?" A man from the group said, "I took a water vessel from them."
He said, "Return it, for these are the people of Ḍimād."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Wāʾil said: ʿAmmār gave us a sermon, brief and eloquent. When he came down, we said, "O Abū al-Yaqẓān, you spoke eloquently and briefly. If only you had extended it a little."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, as Ḥammād said, but he did not mention the two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: No adhān was called on the day of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr or the day of ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā.
Then after a while I asked him about that, and he informed me. He said: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī informed me
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās

sent word to Ibn al-Zubayr when allegiance was first pledged to him: "The adhān was not called for the prayer on the day of al-Fiṭr, so do not call it for it." He said: So Ibn al-Zubayr did not call the adhān for it that day. And he also sent word to him: "The sermon is only after the prayer, and that is what used to be done." He said: So Ibn al-Zubayr prayed before the sermon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr

entered upon her while two girls were with her during the days of Minā, singing and beating the tambourine, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was covered with his garment. Abū Bakr rebuked them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ uncovered his face and said:
"Leave them, O Abū Bakr, for these are days of festival."

And she said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shielding me with his cloak while I watched the Abyssinians playing, and I was a young girl. So estimate how long a young girl, eager and of tender age, would remain watching.
label: machine translation

segments_en: the players. I wished that I could see them. She said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and I stood at the door, looking between his ears and his shoulder, while they were playing in the mosque.
ʿAṭāʾ said: Persians or Abyssinians.
He said: And Ibn ʿAtīq said to me, "Rather, Abyssinians."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain and pointed with the backs of his palms toward the sky.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ would not raise his hands in any of his supplications except in the prayer for rain, until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.
Except that ʿAbd al-Aʿlā said: "the whiteness of his armpit was seen," or "the whiteness of his armpits."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was giving the sermon on Friday when the people stood up to him and cried out, saying, "O Prophet of Allah, the rain has failed, the trees have turned red, and the animals have perished."
And he related the hadith, in which, in the narration of ʿAbd al-Aʿlā: "it cleared away from Madinah." Then it began
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Anas ibn Mālik narrated to him that he
heard Anas ibn Mālik
say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Friday while he was on the pulpit.
And he related the hadith and added: I saw the clouds tearing apart like a cloak when it is folded.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar as he was circumambulating the House, a man came up to him and said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, what did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say about the private conversation [between Allah and the believer]?" He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

The believer will be brought close to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, until He places His covering over him. Then He will make him confess his sins, saying: 'Do you recognize [this]?' He will say: 'My Lord, I recognize it.'
Until, when he has reached the point that Allah willed him to reach, He will say: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you.'
Then he will be given the record of his good deeds, or his book, in his right hand.
As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, he will be called out before the witnesses."
Khālid said regarding "the witnesses":
There is some break in the chain here.
{These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers}
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two boys fought each other, a boy from the Muhājirīn and a boy from the Anṣār. The Muhājir called out: "O Muhājirīn!"
And the Anṣārī called out: "O Anṣār!"
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and said: "
What is this? The call of the people of the Jāhiliyyah?"
They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah, except that two boys fought and one of them struck the other on the backside." He said: "

Then there is no harm. A man should help his brother, whether he is the wrongdoer or the wronged. If he is the wrongdoer, let him stop him, for that is his help; and if he is wronged, let him help him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Muʿādh ibn Jabal to Yemen and said: "
Beware of the supplication of the wronged, for there is no veil between it and Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Beware of sitting in the roads."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have no alternative to our gatherings, where we talk." He said: "
If you insist on gathering, then give the road its due."
They said: "And what is the due of the road, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning the greeting,
and enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Ten things are part of the natural disposition (fiṭrah): trimming the moustache, letting the beard grow, using the siwāk, sniffing water into the nose, clipping the nails, washing the knuckles, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and reducing the water [i.e., washing with water after relieving oneself]."
Zakariyyā said: Muṣʿab said: I forgot the tenth, unless it was rinsing the mouth.
Qutaybah added: Wakīʿ said: "Reducing the water" means istinjāʾ [cleaning oneself after relieving oneself].
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to him: "Your Prophet ﷺ has taught you everything, even how to relieve yourselves."

He said: "Yes. He forbade us from facing the qiblah when relieving ourselves, whether for stool or urine, or from cleaning ourselves with the right hand, or with fewer than three stones, or with dung or bone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to perform ablution for every prayer. On the year of the Conquest [of Makkah], he prayed all the prayers with a single ablution and wiped over his leather socks.
ʿUmar said: "You have done something you had not done before." He said: "I did it deliberately."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:]

"When any of you wakes up from his sleep, he should not put his hand into the vessel until he has washed it three times, for none of you knows where his hand spent the night, or where his hand had been roaming."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the mosque, he said:
"ʿĀʾishah, pass me the garment."
She said: "I am not praying [I am menstruating]." He said:
"It is not in your hand." So she passed it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ — and ʿAmr said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — wished to eat or sleep while in a state of major impurity, he would perform ablution — ʿAmr added in his narration — like his ablution for prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"Whoever says, when he hears the muʾadhdhin: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger; I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Muhammad as Messenger, and with Islam as religion,'
his sins will be forgiven."
Ibn Rumḥ said in his narration:
"Whoever says, when he hears the muʾadhdhin: 'And I bear witness...'"
Qutaybah did not mention the words "and I."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs a prayer in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qurʾān, it is deficient, it is deficient, it is deficient, incomplete."
I said: "Abū Hurayrah, sometimes I am behind the imam."
He pressed my arm and said: "Recite it to yourself, O Persian, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Allah the Almighty said: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves, so half of it is for Me and half is for My servant, and My servant will have what he asks.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

'Recite! When the servant says: {All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds}, Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: My servant has praised Me. When the servant says: {The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate}, Allah says: My servant has extolled Me. When the servant says: {Master of the Day of Judgment}, Allah says: My servant has glorified Me. When the servant says: {You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help}, Allah says: This is between Me and My servant, and My servant will have what he asks. When the servant says: {Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have favoured, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who have gone astray}, Allah says: These are for My servant, and My servant will have what he asks.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best rows for men are the first, and the worst are the last; the best rows for women are the last, and the worst are the first."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head from bowing, he would say:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens, filling the earth, filling what is between them, and filling whatever else You will."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sleeping beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I missed him during the night. I felt for him and my hand fell on his feet while he was prostrating, and he was saying:
"I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment. I cannot count Your praises; You are as You have praised Yourself."
He said: This is a ḥasan ḥadīth, and it has been narrated through more than one route from ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:]
"When a servant prostrates, seven limbs prostrate with him: his face, his two palms, his two knees, and his two feet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished [the prayer], and the sun had cleared, and he delivered a sermon,
praising Allah as He deserves, and then he said: "To proceed:"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr [said]: Rabīʿah was one of the best of people. [He reported] what Rabīʿah witnessed of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him: on Friday he recited Sūrat al-Naḥl from the pulpit, and when he came to the verse of prostration, he came down and prostrated, and the people prostrated.
Then on the following Friday he recited it, and when he came to the verse of prostration, he said: "O people, we pass by prostration; whoever prostrates has done right,
and whoever does not prostrate, there is no sin upon him."
And ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, did not prostrate.
And Nāfiʿ added, from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: Allah has not made prostration obligatory, except if we wish.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We stayed with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey for nineteen days, shortening the prayer.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: We shorten [the prayer] for what is between us and nineteen days,
and if we stay longer, we pray in full.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when travel pressed him in haste on a journey, delay the Maghrib prayer until he combined it with the ʿIshāʾ prayer.
Sālim said: ʿAbdullāh used to do the same when travel pressed him in haste.
And al-Layth added: Yūnus narrated to me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Sālim said: Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to combine Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at Muzdalifah.
Sālim said: Ibn ʿUmar delayed the Maghrib prayer,
when he was called urgently regarding his wife Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd. I said to him: "The prayer!" He said: "Keep going." I said: "The prayer!" He said: "Keep going."
until he had travelled two or three miles. Then he dismounted and prayed, and then said: "This is how I saw the Prophet ﷺ pray when travel pressed him in haste."
And ʿAbdullāh said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, when travel pressed him in haste, delay the Maghrib prayer,
and pray it as three [rakʿahs] and then give the salām,
then he would wait only a short while before the iqāmah was made for ʿIshāʾ, and he would pray it as two rakʿahs and then give the salām,
and he would not offer any voluntary prayer after ʿIshāʾ until he rose in the middle of the night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray voluntary prayers while riding, facing a direction other than the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would not pray more than two rakʿahs on a journey,
and [it was] likewise with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, about the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: "Seven, nine, and eleven [rakʿahs], besides the two rakʿahs of Fajr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, regarding the dream, he said:
"As for the one whose head is being crushed with a rock, he is one who takes the Qurʾān and then rejects it, and sleeps through the obligatory prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In his stories, he mentioned the Prophet ﷺ saying:
"Indeed a brother of yours does not speak obscenity."

He meant by that Ibn Rawāḥah, who said: "Among us is the Messenger of Allah, reciting His Book, when a clear streak of dawn breaks forth and shines. He has shown us guidance after blindness, so our hearts are certain that what he says will come to pass. He spends the night keeping his side away from his bed, when the beds weigh heavily upon the disbelievers." ʿUqayl followed him, from al-Zuhrī.
And al-Zubaydī said, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd and al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah:
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with them both, said: In the time of the Prophet ﷺ I saw [in a dream] that I had in my hand a piece of brocade,
and it was as though I did not wish for any place in Paradise except that it flew me to it,
and I saw as though two men came to me wanting to take me to the Fire, but an angel met them and said: "Do not be afraid." So they let me go.
Ḥafṣah related one of my dreams to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What an excellent man ʿAbdullāh is, if only he would pray at night."
And ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, used to pray at night.
And they continued to relate dreams to the Prophet ﷺ [indicating] that it was on the seventh night of the last ten. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I see that your dreams have agreed upon the last ten [nights],
so whoever is seeking it, let him seek it in the last ten."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Do you pray Ḍuḥā?" He said: "No." I said: "What about ʿUmar?" He said: "No."
I said: "What about Abū Bakr?" He said: "No."
I said: "What about the Prophet ﷺ?" He said: "I do not think so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A time will come upon the people when a man will call his paternal cousin and his relative, saying, 'Come to ease and plenty! Come to ease and plenty!' Yet Medina is better for them, if only they knew. By the One in whose hand is my soul, no one will leave it out of dislike for it except that Allah will replace him in it with someone better. Indeed, Medina is like a bellows: it expels the impure.
The Hour will not come until Medina expels its wicked ones, just as the bellows expels the impurity of iron."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is Ṭayyibah"—meaning Medina—"and it expels impurity just as fire expels the impurity of silver."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Exalted, named Medina Ṭābah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever intends evil for its people"—meaning Medina—"Allah will make him dissolve as salt dissolves in water."

"Indeed, it is forbidden from this day of yours until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever has given anything, let him not take it back."

segments_en: He stood up in Mecca and said: Some people—Allah has blinded their hearts just as He has blinded their eyes—give rulings permitting temporary marriage (mutʿah)—alluding to a man. The man called out to him and said: You are a coarse, harsh man! By my life, temporary marriage was practiced in the time of the leader of the righteous—meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ibn al-Zubayr said to him: Then try it yourself! By Allah, if you do it, I will stone you with your own stones.

segments_en: He was
a judge in Medina. He said: We came to Abū Hurayrah about a companion of ours who had gone bankrupt, and he said: This is the one concerning whom the Prophet ﷺ gave a ruling:

segments_en: I read to Mālik ibn Anas, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"None of you should milk another person's livestock without his permission. Would any of you like for his storeroom to be entered, his chest broken open, and his food taken away? Their animals' udders store their people's food for them. So none of you should milk another person's livestock without his permission."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān
and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah
on a military expedition, and I found a whip and took it. They said to me: Leave it.
I said: No, but I will announce it; if its owner comes, [I will return it], and if not, I will make use of it.

He said: I refused their advice. When we returned from our expedition, it was decreed that I perform Hajj. I came to Medina and met Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and I told him about the whip and what they had said. He said: I found a purse containing one hundred dinars during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Announce it for a year."
He said: So I announced it but found no one who recognized it. Then I came to him, and he said: "Announce it for a year."
I announced it but found no one who recognized it. Then I came to him, and he said: "Announce it for a year."
I announced it but found no one who recognized it. Then he said:
"Remember its number, its container, and its binding. If its owner comes, [give it to him]; otherwise, make use of it." So I made use of it.
He said: I met him afterwards in Mecca, and he said: I do not know whether it was three years or one year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him and does not abandon him. Whoever is engaged in meeting the need of his brother, Allah will be engaged in meeting his need. Whoever relieves a Muslim of a distress, Allah will relieve him of a distress from the distresses of the Day of Resurrection. And whoever conceals [the faults of] a Muslim, Allah will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ, saying:
"The most hated of men to Allah is the most quarrelsome, argumentative one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: You send us out, and we stop with a people who do not host us. What do you think about that?
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us:
"If you stop with a people and they order for you what is fitting for a guest, accept it. But if they do not, then take from them the due of the guest that is proper for them [to give]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with one of his wives, and one of the Mothers of the Believers sent a bowl of food with her servant. She struck [the servant's hand] with her own hand and the bowl broke. Ibn al-Muthannā said: The Prophet ﷺ took the two pieces and joined one to the other, and began gathering the food in it, saying: "Your mother was jealous."
Ibn al-Muthannā added: "Eat."
So they ate until her bowl from her house arrived. Then we return to the wording of Musaddad's report, who said: "Eat."
He kept the messenger and the bowl until they had finished, then handed the intact bowl to the messenger and kept the broken one in his house.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, we will meet the enemy tomorrow and we have no knives. May we slaughter with sharp stones and split pieces of cane? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Let the blood flow, or hurry it, as long as it is made to flow and Allah's name is mentioned over it, then eat, as long as it is not a tooth or a nail. I will tell you about that: as for the tooth, it is a bone; and as for the nail, it is the knife of the Abyssinians."

Some hasty people went ahead and hurried, and they took some of the spoils while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at the rear of the people. They set up cooking pots. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by the pots and ordered them to be overturned, and he distributed [the spoils] among them, counting one camel as equal to ten sheep. A camel from the people's camels ran off, and they had no horses, so a man shot it with an arrow and Allah stopped it. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"These animals have wild ways like the wild ways of untamed beasts. So if any of them does this, treat it likewise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade a man to join two dates together [when eating],

label: machine translation

segments_en: Shaddād ibn Aws was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Baqīʿ.
He passed by a man who was being cupped, after eighteen nights of the month had passed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who cups and the one who is cupped have both broken their fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Hamdānī al-Kūfī, and Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr. Abū ʿUbaydah said: He narrated to us; and he said,
Isḥāq: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith informed us: My father narrated to me,
from Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim,
from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr,
who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Awzāʿī narrated to me,
from Yaʿīsh ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī, from his father,
from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah,
from Abū al-Dardāʾ,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ vomited and broke his fast, and then performed ablution.
Then I met Thawbān in the mosque of Damascus and mentioned that to him, and he said: "He spoke the truth. I poured out his ablution water for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And I recited it,
to Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih al-Jurjusī; both said: al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us,
from Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith,
from al-Qāsim Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Abū Umāmah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Whoever does not go out to fight, or equip a fighter, or take good care of a fighter's family in his absence, Allah will afflict him with a calamity."
Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih said in his narration:
"before the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Name yourselves with the names of the prophets. The names most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are ʿAbdullāh and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Keep horses tied up [for the cause of Allah], wipe their forelocks and their hindquarters, and put garlands on them, but do not put bowstrings on them as garlands. And choose every dark bay with a white blaze and white-marked legs, or a chestnut with a white blaze and white-marked legs, or a black horse with a white blaze and white-marked legs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he is given the kunyah Abū ʿAbdullāh, the righteous man; he is Ibn Abī ʿUmar. Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Nawfal ibn Musāḥiq, from Ibn ʿIṣām al-Muzanī, from his father, who was a Companion. He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out an army or a detachment, he would say to them:

segments_en: that he

was in one of the detachments of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The people fled in retreat, and I was among those who fled. He said: When we came out [into the open], we said: "What shall we do, having fled from the advancing battle and incurred [Allah's] anger?" We said: "Let us enter Madinah and stay there, and then leave without anyone seeing us." He said: So we entered, and we said: "If we presented ourselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then if there is repentance for us, we will stay, and if it is otherwise, we will go." He said: So we sat waiting for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before the Fajr prayer. When he came out, we stood up to him and said: "We are the ones who fled." He turned to us and said:
"No, rather you are those who return to the fight."
He said: Then we approached and kissed his hand, and he said:
"I am the group [to whom] the Muslims [may return]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear carefully, and not to sacrifice an animal that is blind in one eye, or muqābalah, or mudābarah, or kharqāʾ, or sharqāʾ.
Zuhayr said: I said to Abū Isḥāq: "Did he mention ʿaḍbāʾ?" He said: "No."
I said: "What is muqābalah?" He said: "One whose ear is cut at the tip."
I said: "What is mudābarah?" He said: "One whose ear is cut from the back."
I said: "What is sharqāʾ?" He said: "One whose ear is split."
I said: "What is kharqāʾ?" He said: "One whose ear is pierced for branding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in three white Saḥūlī cotton garments, among which there was no shirt and no turban. As for the cloak, people were only confused about it, thinking that it had been bought for him to be shrouded in; but the cloak was left aside and he was shrouded in three white Saḥūlī garments. Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr took it and said: I will keep it until I am shrouded in it myself. Then he said: If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had approved it for His Prophet, he would have shrouded him in it.

segments_en: He stood among us to deliver a sermon and said: "I tell you only what I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the day of Ḥunayn. He said:
'It is not lawful for a man who believes in Allah and the Last Day to water the crop of another with his water,'
meaning, to have intercourse with pregnant women.

'And it is not lawful for a man who believes in Allah and the Last Day to have intercourse with a woman from the captives until he has ascertained that she is not pregnant. And it is not lawful for a man who believes in Allah and the Last Day to sell war booty until it has been divided.'"

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah forgive him, was mistaken. This tribe of the Anṣār, who were idol-worshippers, lived alongside this tribe of the Jews, who were People of the Book, and they regarded the Jews as superior to them in knowledge, so they imitated many of their practices. It was the custom of the People of the Book not to approach women except on one side, which is the most concealing way for a woman. This tribe of the Anṣār had adopted that from them. But this tribe of Quraysh used to uncover women in an objectionable manner and enjoy them from the front, from behind, and lying on their backs. When the Emigrants came to Madinah, one of them married a woman of the Anṣār and began to do that with her. She objected to it and said: "We were approached only on one side, so do that or else keep away from me." Their dispute grew serious, and news of it reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish}, meaning from the front, from behind, and lying on their backs, meaning in the place of childbearing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a slave woman and I practice withdrawal with her, as I do not want her to conceive, while I desire what men desire. The Jews say that withdrawal is the lesser burying alive." He said:
"The Jews have lied. If Allah wanted to create it, you would not be able to turn it away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Ṭufāwah said: I stayed with Abū Hurayrah in Madinah, and I saw no Companion of the Prophet ﷺ more diligent in exertion, nor more attentive to a guest, than he. One day while I was with him, he was on a couch of his with a bag containing pebbles or date stones, and below him was a black slave girl of his. He was glorifying Allah with them, and when the bag was empty he threw it to her, and she gathered them, put them back in the bag, and handed it to him. He said: "Shall I not tell you about myself and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" I said: "Yes."
He said: While I was suffering from fever in the mosque, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered the mosque. He said:
"Who has seen the young man from Daws?" three times.

A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, there he is, suffering from fever at the side of the mosque." He came walking until he reached me, put his hand on me, and spoke kindly to me, so I got up. He walked on until he reached his place where he prayed, and he turned to them, with two rows of men and a row of women, or two rows of women and a row of men. He said:
"If Satan makes me forget something of my prayer, let the men say 'Subḥān Allāh' and the women clap."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then prayed and did not forget anything of his prayer. He said: "Stay in your places, stay in your places." Mūsā added: "Right here."
Then he praised Allah, the Exalted, and extolled Him, and then said: "To proceed."
Then the narrators agreed on the wording. He turned to the men and said:
"Is there among you a man who, when he goes to his wife, closes his door, lets his curtain down, and covers himself with the covering of Allah?" They said: "Yes." He said:
"Then afterwards he sits and says: I did such and such, I did such and such."
He said: They fell silent. Then he turned to the women and said:
"Is there any among you who talks about it?"

They remained silent, then a young woman knelt on one knee, Muʾammal said in his narration: a young woman in her prime, and she stretched up toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he might see her and hear her words. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, they certainly talk about it, and the women certainly talk about it too." He said:
"Do you know what that is like?" Then he said:

"That is like a female devil who met a male devil in the street and he satisfied his need with her while people looked on. Indeed, the perfume of men is that whose scent is apparent and whose color is not apparent. And indeed, the perfume of women is that whose color is apparent and whose scent is not apparent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A servant from among Allah's servants, whom Allah had given wealth, was brought to Allah. Allah said to him, 'What did you do in the world?' — and they will not conceal any statement from Allah — He said, 'My Lord, You gave me Your wealth, and I used to deal with people. It was part of my character to be lenient, so I would make things easy for the well-off and give time to the one in difficulty.'
Allah said, 'I am more deserving of this than you. Overlook the faults of My servant.'"
ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī and Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī said, "This is how we heard it from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Qatādah
sought a debtor of his, but the man hid from him. Then he found him, and the man said, "I am in hardship."
He said, "By Allah?" He said, "By Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was cupped by a slave belonging to Banū Bayāḍah. The Prophet ﷺ gave him his payment and spoke to his master, who reduced the daily amount he required from him. Had it been unlawful earnings, the Prophet ﷺ would not have given it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ giving a sermon in Medina. He said,
"O people, Allah the Exalted is hinting at wine, and perhaps Allah will send down a ruling about it. So whoever has any of it, let him sell it and benefit from it."
He said: We had waited only a short while when the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Allah the Exalted has forbidden wine. So whoever hears this verse while he has any of it, let him neither drink nor sell it."
He said: Then the people took whatever they had of it out to the roads of Medina and poured it out.
label: machine translation

label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Conquest. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us: aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk, meaning Abū ʿĀṣim, narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, who said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to me, saying: ʿAṭāʾ wrote to me that he heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of the Conquest, similar to the hadith of al-Layth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in Syria in a circle in which was Muslim ibn Yasār. Then Abū al-Ashʿath came. They said, "Abū al-Ashʿath, Abū al-Ashʿath!"
So he sat down, and I said to him, "Tell our brother the hadith of ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit."

He said, "Yes. We went on a military expedition, with Muʿāwiyah in command of the people, and we took much war booty. Among what we took was a silver vessel. Muʿāwiyah ordered a man to sell it for the people's allowances, and the people hurried to do so. This reached ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit, so he stood up and said, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid the sale of gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, except like for like, equal for equal, hand to hand. Whoever gives more or takes more has engaged in usury.'

So the people returned what they had taken. This reached Muʿāwiyah, and he stood up to give a speech and said, 'What is the matter with men who relate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reports which we, who were present with him and kept his company, never heard from him?'

Then ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit stood up and repeated the story, then said, 'We will certainly relate what we heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even if Muʿāwiyah dislikes it' — or he said, 'even if it is against his wishes' — 'I do not care if I do not accompany him in his army on a dark night.'"
Ḥammād said: This, or something like it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr an-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
— the wording is Ibn Abī Shaybah's; Isḥāq said "akhbaranā" while the other two said "ḥaddathanā" — Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Khālid
al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Abū Qilābah,
from Abū al-Ashʿath,
from ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, salt for salt: like for like, equal for equal, hand to hand. If these kinds differ, then sell as you wish, provided it is hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A necklace containing beads and gold, from the war booty and being offered for sale, was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Khaybar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that the gold in the necklace be removed by itself. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
"Gold for gold, weight for weight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd on a military expedition. A necklace containing gold, silver, and jewels came to me and my companions in the booty, and I wanted to buy it. I asked Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, and he said, "Remove its gold and put it in one pan of the scale, and put your gold in the other pan, and then take only like for like. For I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him take only like for like.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was the expedition of Tabūk, the people were afflicted by hunger.
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you would permit us, we would slaughter our water-carrying camels, eat [their meat], and use their fat."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do so."

He said: Then ʿUmar came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you do that, the riding animals will become few. Rather, call them to bring the remainder of their provisions, then pray to Allah for blessing upon them, perhaps Allah will place [sufficiency] in that."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes."

He said: So he called for a leather mat and spread it out, then called for the remainder of their provisions. He said: A man would come with a handful of corn, another would come with a handful of dates, and another with a piece of bread, until a small amount of that had gathered on the mat. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for blessing upon it, then said,
"Take it in your containers."

He said: So they took it in their containers until there was not a single container in the army camp that they did not fill. He said: They ate until they were full, and there was still some left over. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. No servant meets Allah with these two [testimonies], having no doubt about them, and is then kept from Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray the ʿAṣr prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then a camel would be slaughtered and divided into ten portions, then it would be cooked, and we would eat fully cooked meat before the sun set.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When the Ashʿarīs run low on provisions during a military expedition,
or the food of their families in Medina becomes scarce,
they gather whatever they have in a single cloth, then divide it among themselves equally in a single vessel.
So they are from me, and I am from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The likeness of the one who observes the limits of Allah and the one who transgresses them is that of a people who cast lots for a ship,
so some of them ended up on its lower deck and some on its upper deck.
Those on the lower deck would pass by those on the upper deck to get water, and this bothered them, so one of them took an axe
and began to strike at the bottom of the ship.
They came to him and said, 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'You were bothered by me,
and I must have water.'
If they take hold of his hands, they will save him and save themselves,
but if they leave him, they will destroy him and destroy themselves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, bought Barīrah in order to free her,
but her owners stipulated that her walāʾ [right of patronage] be theirs. So she said, "O Messenger of Allah, I bought Barīrah to free her,
but her owners stipulate that her walāʾ be theirs." He said,
"Free her, for walāʾ belongs only to the one who frees." Or he said, "Pay the price."
He said: So she bought her and freed her.
He said: Barīrah was given the choice [regarding her marriage], and she chose herself, and said, "Even if I were given such and such, I would not stay with him."
Al-Aswad said: Her husband was a free man.
The statement of al-Aswad is disconnected [in its chain],
and the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās, "I saw him as a slave," is more authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: I will not cease to love Banū Tamīm because of three things I heard from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"They are the strongest of my nation against the Dajjāl."
He said: Their charity (ṣadaqāt) came, and the Prophet ﷺ said,
"These are the charities of our people."
He said: A captive woman of theirs was with ʿĀʾishah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Free her, for she is a descendant of Ismāʿīl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The righteous slave has a double reward."
By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Abū Hurayrah, were it not for jihad in the cause of Allah, Hajj, and dutifulness to my mother, I would love to die while a slave.
He said: It has reached us that Abū Hurayrah did not perform Hajj until his mother died, because of his companionship with her.
Abū aṭ-Ṭāhir said in his narration: "for the righteous slave,"
and he did not mention "owned [slave]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them, and he said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"How excellent it is for a slave to die having worshipped Allah well and having served his master well. How excellent for him!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should say, 'Give your lord a drink, feed your lord, help your lord perform ablution.'
And none of you should say, 'my lord' (rabbī).
Rather let him say, 'my master' (sayyidī) or 'my patron' (mawlāya). And none of you should say, 'my slave' (ʿabdī) or 'my slave girl' (amatī).
Rather let him say, 'my young man' (fatāya), 'my young woman' (fatātī), or 'my boy' (ghulāmī)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Give gifts to one another, for a gift removes the rancor of the heart. And let no woman look down on a gift from her neighbor, even if it is only the trotter of a sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If I were invited to a foreleg or a lower leg [of an animal], I would respond,
and if a foreleg or a lower leg were given to me as a gift, I would accept it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Busaysah as a scout to see what the caravan of Abū Sufyān was doing. He came back when there was no one in the house except me and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [Anas] said: I do not know what he excepted, [perhaps] some of his wives. He said: So he told him the news. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and spoke, saying:
"We are seeking [the caravan], so whoever has his mount ready, let him ride out with us."
Some men began asking his permission regarding their mounts, which were in the upper part of Medina. He said:
"No, only the one whose mount is ready."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions set out until they reached Badr before the polytheists. Then the polytheists arrived, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you is to advance toward anything until I am ahead of him."
Then the polytheists drew near, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Rise up to a Paradise whose width is [like] the heavens and the earth."
He said: ʿUmayr ibn al-Humām al-Anṣārī said, "O Messenger of Allah, a Paradise whose width is [like] the heavens and the earth?" He said, "Yes."
He said: "Wow! Wow!"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What makes you say, 'Wow! Wow!'?"
He said: "Nothing, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, except the hope that I may be among its people." He said:
"You are among its people."

Then he took some dates out of his quiver and began eating them. Then he said, "If I live until I have eaten these dates of mine, that would be a long life indeed." He said: So he threw away the dates he had with him.
Then he fought them until he was killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Send men with us who will teach us the Qur'an and the Sunnah."

So he sent to them seventy men from the Anṣār, who were called the reciters, among them my maternal uncle Ḥarām. They would recite the Qur'an and study it together at night, learning it, and by day they would bring water and place it in the mosque, and gather firewood and sell it and buy food with it for the people of the Ṣuffah and for the poor. The Prophet ﷺ sent them to those people, but they intercepted them and killed them before they reached their destination.

They said: "O Allah, convey from us to our Prophet that we have met You, and we are pleased with You and You are pleased with us." He said: A man came to Ḥarām, the maternal uncle of Anas, from behind him and stabbed him with a spear until it went through him.
Ḥarām said: "I have succeeded, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah!" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Your brothers have been killed, and they said: 'O Allah, convey from us to our Prophet that we have met You, and we are pleased with You and You are pleased with us.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people dispersed from around Abū Hurayrah,
and Nātil of Syria said to him... and he related the hadith like the hadith of Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the daughter of Milḥān, the maternal aunt of Anas, and laid his head down by her.
And he related the hadith with the same meaning as the hadith of Isḥāq ibn Abī Ṭalḥah and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he added in it: "And the one who drowns is a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Lands will soon be opened to you, and Allah will suffice you, so let none of you fail to amuse himself with his arrows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fuqaym al-Lakhmī
said to ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, "You go back and forth between these two targets while you are an old man; it is hard on you."
ʿUqbah said, "Were it not for something I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would not undergo this hardship."
Al-Ḥārith said: I asked Ibn Shimāsah, "What is that?" He said: He said:
"Whoever learned archery and then abandoned it is not one of us," or, "has disobeyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"This religion will never cease to stand, with a group of Muslims fighting for it, until the Hour is established."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned a hadith that he narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, saying he had not heard him narrate from the Prophet ﷺ on his pulpit any hadith other than it. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whomever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion. And a group of Muslims will not cease fighting for the truth, prevailing over those who oppose them, until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with us? When we are with you, our hearts soften, we become detached from this world, and we feel as though we are among the people of the Hereafter. But when we leave you and are at ease with our families and smell our children, we no longer recognize ourselves."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If you were to remain, after leaving me, in that same state, the angels would visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, Allah would bring a new creation so that they would sin and He would forgive them."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, from what was creation created?" He said, "From water."
We said, "As for Paradise, what is its construction?" He said:

"One brick of silver and one brick of gold; its mortar is fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will enjoy bliss and never suffer misery, will live forever and never die; their garments will not wear out and their youth will not fade." Then he said:

"Three whose supplication is not rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person when he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the oppressed. Allah raises it above the clouds, the gates of heaven are opened for it, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: By My might, I will certainly help you, even if after a while."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Medina came to Abū al-Dardāʾ, who was in Damascus, and he said, "What brought you, my brother?" He said, "A hadith that has reached me, which you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said, "Did you not come for some need?" He said, "No."
He said, "Did you not come for trade?" He said, "No."
He said, "You came only to seek this hadith?" He said yes. [Abū al-Dardāʾ] said, "Then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah will make him travel a path to Paradise. The angels lower their wings in approval of the seeker of knowledge. Everyone in the heavens and on the earth seeks forgiveness for the scholar, even the fish in the water. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon over all the other stars. Scholars are the heirs of the prophets; the prophets did not leave behind a dinar or a dirham, they left behind only knowledge. So whoever takes it has taken an abundant share.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
"The best perfume for a man is that whose scent is apparent and whose color is faint, and the best perfume for women is that whose color is apparent and whose scent is faint."
And he forbade the crimson saddle-cover.
This is a good (ḥasan) hadith, gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a expedition of a considerable number of men, and he asked them to recite, asking each man how much of the Qur'an he knew. He came to one of the youngest of them in age and said:
"What do you have, so-and-so?"
He said, "I know such-and-such, and Sūrat al-Baqarah." He said:
"You know Sūrat al-Baqarah?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Go, then, you are their commander."
One of their nobles said, "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, the only thing that kept me from learning Sūrat al-Baqarah was the fear that I would not be able to stand in prayer with it."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Learn the Qur'an, recite it, and teach it to others. The example of the Qur'an for one who learns it, recites it, and stands in prayer with it is like a bag filled with musk, its fragrance spreading everywhere. And the example of one who learns it and then sleeps while it is in his chest is like a bag of musk that has been tied shut."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning His statement:
"You are the best nation brought out for mankind," he said:
"You complete seventy nations; you are the best of them and the most honored by Allah."
This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
More than one narrator has reported this hadith from Bahz ibn Ḥakīm in similar wording, but they did not mention in it, "You are the best nation brought out for mankind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Banū Ḥanẓalah, he said: I accompanied Shaddād ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, on a journey, and he said, "Shall I not teach you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us to say? 'O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in all matters, and I ask You for determination to follow the right course. I ask You to be grateful for Your blessings and to worship You well. I ask You for a truthful tongue and a sound heart. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, I ask You for the good of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.'"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"There is no Muslim who takes to his bed and recites a sūrah from the Book of Allah, except that Allah appoints an angel over him, so nothing that could harm him comes near him until he wakes, whenever he wakes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that a man
said, "O Messenger of Allah, I wish to travel, so advise me." He said:
"Hold fast to fear of Allah, and say Allahu Akbar upon every elevated place."
When the man turned to leave, he said:
"O Allah, fold the earth up for him and make the journey easy for him."
He said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The most hateful of people to Allah are three: one who commits deviation (impiety) in the Sacred Precinct,
one who seeks in Islam the practices of the Days of Ignorance,
and one who seeks to shed the blood of a person without right, in order to spill his blood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ to Khaybar, and a man among them said, "O ʿĀmir, let us hear some of your verses." So he chanted for them, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Who is the driver?" They said, "ʿĀmir." He said, "May Allah have mercy on him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, would that you had let us enjoy his company longer!"
Then he was killed the morning after that night, and the people said, "His deeds have come to nothing; he killed himself."
When I returned, they were saying that ʿĀmir's deeds had come to nothing,
so I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom,
they claim that ʿĀmir's deeds have come to nothing." He said:
"Whoever said that has lied.
He will have a double reward,
for he strove and struggled in the cause of Allah,
and what death could add anything to that for him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The daughter of an-Naḍr slapped a girl and broke her front tooth,
so they came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered retaliation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy
was killed by treachery, and ʿUmar said, "Even if all the people of Ṣanʿāʾ had taken part in it, I would have killed them."
Mughīrah ibn Ḥakīm reported from his father that four men killed a boy, and ʿUmar said the same.
Abū Bakr, Ibn az-Zubayr, ʿAlī, and Suwayd ibn Muqarrin allowed retaliation for a slap.
ʿUmar allowed retaliation for a blow with the whip.
ʿAlī allowed retaliation for three lashes.
Shurayḥ applied retaliation for a lash and for scratches.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
stretched out her hand to the Prophet ﷺ holding a letter, but he withdrew his hand. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I stretched out my hand to you with a letter and you did not take it." He said,
"I did not know whether it was the hand of a woman or of a man."
She said, "It is the hand of a woman." He said,
"If you were a woman, you would change your nails with henna."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman met him, and he detected the scent of perfume wafting from her, and the hem of her garment was stirring up dust. He said, "O servant of the Almighty, have you come from the mosque?" She said, "Yes."
He said, "And did you perfume yourself for it?" She said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was above the earlobes and below the shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: When I wanted to part the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would make the parting from the crown of his head, and let his forelock fall between his eyes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Hāniʾ said: The Prophet ﷺ came to Makkah with four braids, meaning plaits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the family of Jaʿfar three days' respite before coming to them. Then he came to them and said,
"Do not weep for my brother after today." Then he said,
"Call my brother's sons to me."
So we were brought, as though we were little chicks. He said,
"Call the barber for me."
Then he ordered that our heads be shaved. [Abridged]
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a boy who had had part of his hair shaved and part of it left, so he forbade them from that and said,
"Shave it all, or leave it all."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to wear sandals of tanned leather and to dye his beard yellow with wars and saffron.
And Ibn ʿUmar used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a man who had dyed his hair with henna, and he said,
"How good this is!"
Then he passed by another who had dyed with henna and katam, and he said,
"This is better than that."
Then he passed by another who had dyed with yellow, and he said,
"This is better than all of that."
He said: And Ṭāwūs used to dye yellow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"There will be people at the end of time who dye [their hair] black, like the crops of pigeons. They will not smell the fragrance of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ disliked ten things: yellow [dye], meaning khalūq perfume; changing grey hair; dragging the lower garment; wearing gold rings; displaying adornment in the wrong place; playing with dice; using spells except with the two protective surahs; tying amulets; withdrawing [during intercourse] in an improper manner or place; and corrupting a child, not [that of] his unlawful partner.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he,

saw his grandfather, who said: His nose was injured on the day of al-Kulāb in the Pre-Islamic Era. So he made a nose of silver, but it began to rot on him, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to make one of gold.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her. She said: Some jewelry arrived for the Prophet ﷺ from the Negus, who had sent it to him as a gift. In it was a gold ring with an Abyssinian stone. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it with a stick, or with some of his fingers, turning away from it. Then he called Umāmah, the daughter of Abū al-ʿĀṣ, the daughter of his daughter Zaynab, and said,
"Adorn yourself with this, little girl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To Ḥudhayfah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"O company of women, do you not have silver with which to adorn yourselves? There is no woman among you who adorns herself with gold and displays it, except that she will be punished with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Any woman who adorns herself, meaning with a necklace of gold, will have a like [necklace] of fire placed around her neck. And any woman who puts a gold earring in her ear, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will put a like earring of fire in her ear on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade riding on leopard skins and wearing gold, except in small pieces.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Between the great battle and the conquest of the city there will be six years, and the False Messiah, the Dajjāl, will emerge in the seventh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no man among a people who commits acts of disobedience among them, while they are able to change it [or stop him] but do not change it, except that Allah will strike them with punishment before they die."
label: machine translation
