segments_en: My father was one of the Companions of the Tree. Whenever a people brought their charity to the Prophet ﷺ, he would say: "
O Allah, send blessings upon the family of so-and-so."
He said: My father came to him with his charity, and he said: "
O Allah, send blessings upon the family of Abū Awfā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people from among the Arabs came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and accepted Islam, then they fell ill. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them to a herd of milch camels so that they could drink their milk, and they stayed there. Then they went for the herdsman, a servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, killed him, and drove off the camels. They claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O Allah, make thirsty tonight whoever has made the family of Muhammad thirsty."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent [men] in pursuit of them, and they were captured. He had their hands and feet cut off and their eyes blinded.
Some of the narrators add more than others, except that Muʿāwiyah said in this hadith: "They drove [the camels] off to the land of polytheism."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: The Prophet ﷺ made obligatory the charity of Ramadan upon the free person and the slave, the male and the female: one ṣāʿ of dates or one ṣāʿ of barley.
He said: Then the people made equivalent to it half a ṣāʿ of wheat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever performs Hajj to this House,
and does not engage in obscenity or commit sin,
will return as his mother bore him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, that Ḥafṣah,

may Allah be pleased with them, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the people that they have come out of their state of iḥrām while you have not come out of yours after your ʿUmrah? He said: "
I have matted my hair and garlanded my sacrificial animal, so I will not come out of iḥrām until I have slaughtered."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Makkah while he was ailing, and he circumambulated on his mount. Whenever he came to the corner, he touched it with a curved staff. When he finished his circumambulation, he made his camel kneel and prayed two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked Ibn ʿUmar about a man

who came for ʿUmrah and circumambulated the House but did not walk between Ṣafā and Marwah: may he go to his wife? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and circumambulated the House seven times, prayed two rakʿahs behind the Station, and walked between Ṣafā and Marwah seven times. And indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik, saying: Tell me something
you retained from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: where did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the noon prayer on the Day of Tarwiyah? He said: At Minā.
I said: And where did he pray the afternoon prayer on the Day of Departure? He said: At al-Abṭaḥ. Then he said: Do as your leaders do.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usāmah was asked while I was present,

or he said: I asked Usāmah ibn Zayd, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made to ride behind him from ʿArafāt, I said: How did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travel when he departed from ʿArafah? He said: He would travel at a steady pace, and when he found an open space, he would go faster.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Sālim ibn
ʿAbdullāh, from Ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers together at Muzdalifah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was among those
whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ahead on the night of Muzdalifah, among the weak of his family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We performed Hajj with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and when we wanted to depart
from Muzdalifah, he said: The polytheists used to say: "Shine, O Thabīr, so that we may hasten on."
And they would not depart until the sun had risen. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted contrary to them and departed before sunrise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAṭāʾ,
and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, that al-Faḍl informed him that he
rode behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he did not cease reciting the talbiyah until he threw the pebbles at the Jamrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to send sacrificial animals from Madīnah, and I would twist the garlands for his sacrificial animals; then he would not avoid anything that one in iḥrām avoids.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O Allah, have mercy on those who shave their heads."
They said: And those who shorten, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "
O Allah, have mercy on those who shave their heads."
They said: And those who shorten, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "And those who shorten."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said to ʿĀʾishah: "Have you not seen so-and-so, the daughter of al-Ḥakam? Her husband divorced her irrevocably, and she left [her house]."
She said: "What she did is evil."
He said: "Have you not heard what Fāṭimah said?" She said: "There is no good for her in mentioning this report."
Ibn Abī al-Zinād added, from Hishām, from his father:
ʿĀʾishah criticized it most severely, and said: "Fāṭimah was in a desolate place, and there was fear for her safety.
For that reason the Prophet ﷺ gave her a concession."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my daughter's husband has died, and her eye is sore. May I apply kohl to it?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No." Then he said:
"It is only four months and ten days. In the days of ignorance, one of you would throw a piece of dung at the end of the year."

Ḥumayd said: I asked Zaynab, "What is throwing dung at the end of the year?" Zaynab said: "When a woman's husband died, she would enter a small hut, wear her worst clothes, and touch no perfume or anything else until a year had passed. Then an animal would be brought to her, a donkey, a sheep, or a bird, and she would rub herself with it. Seldom did she rub herself with anything but that it died. Then she would come out and be given a piece of dung, which she would throw, and after that she would return to perfume or other things as she wished."
Mālik said: "Taftaḍḍu means she wipes herself with it," in the report of Muḥammad.
Mālik said: "The ḥifsh is a hut made of reeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to visit Anas ibn Mālik. Isḥāq said: while his baker was standing there; and al-Dārimī said: while his table was set out. One day he said: "Eat. I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ever saw a thin, fine loaf with his own eyes until he met Allah, nor a roasted sheep with its skin removed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he

entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who was his maternal aunt and the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās. There he found a roasted lizard that her sister Ḥufaydah bint al-Ḥārith had brought from Najd. She presented the lizard to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and seldom was food presented to him until he was told about it and its name was mentioned to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stretched out his hand toward the lizard, and one of the women present said: "Tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what you have presented to him."
They said: "It is the lizard, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted his hand. Khālid ibn al-Walīd said: "Is the lizard forbidden, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"No, but it was not found in the land of my people, so I find myself disliking it."
Khālid said: "So I pulled it toward me and ate it while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was looking on, and he did not forbid me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ: that when one of her family died, the women would gather for that, then disperse,
except her family and her close ones.
She would order a pot of talbīnah, and it would be cooked.
Then tharīd would be made and the talbīnah poured over it. Then she would say: "Eat of it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Talbīnah gives rest to the heart of the sick person,
and removes some of the grief.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were with Ḥudhayfah, and he asked for a drink, and a Magian gave him a drink.
When he placed the cup in his hand, he threw it at him and said: "Had I not forbidden him more than once or twice..."
as if he were saying, "I would not have done this,"
"but I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'Do not wear silk or brocade, and do not drink from vessels of gold and silver,
and do not eat from their plates,
for they are for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and said: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid [eating] the meat of sacrificial animals after three days?" She said: "Yes. The people were struck by hardship, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted the wealthy to feed the poor." Then she said: "I have seen the family of Muḥammad ﷺ eating trotters after fifteen days." I said: "Why was that?" She laughed and said: "The family of Muḥammad ﷺ never had their fill of bread with seasoning for three days [in a row] until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar was told: "We go in to see our rulers and say one thing to them, and when we leave we say something else."
He said: "We used to count that as hypocrisy in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There will be trials, at whose gates will be callers to the Fire. For you to die while biting on the trunk of a tree is better for you than to follow any one of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day he went out to the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found Muʿādh ibn Jabal sitting by the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, weeping. He asked, "What makes you weep?" He said, "Something I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ makes me weep. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'Even a little showing off is shirk, and whoever shows enmity to a friend of Allah has openly declared war on Allah. Indeed Allah loves the righteous, the God-fearing, the hidden ones, who when they are absent are not missed, and when they are present are not called upon or recognized. Their hearts are lamps of guidance; they emerge from every dark and dusty place.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, and my Ummah will split into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire except one, and that is the main body (al-jamāʿah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no morning but two angels call out: Woe to men from women, and woe to women from men."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the mosque, a woman from Muzaynah entered the mosque, trailing along in her finery. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O people, forbid your women from wearing finery and from strutting in the mosque, for the Children of Israel were not cursed until their women wore finery and strutted in the mosques."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, before you call upon Allah and are not answered."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should belittle himself."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how does one of us belittle himself?" He said:

"He sees a matter in which he has something to say for Allah, then does not speak about it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: 'What prevented you from speaking about such and such?' He will say: 'Fear of people.'
Then Allah will say: 'It was I whom you had more right to fear.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When I returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the migration across the sea, he said:
"Will you not tell me about the most amazing things you saw in the land of Abyssinia?"

Some young men among them said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. While we were sitting, an old woman from among their elderly nuns passed by us carrying a jug of water on her head. She passed by a young man of theirs, who put one hand between her shoulders and then pushed her, so she fell on her knees and her jug broke. When she got up, she turned to him and said: 'You will come to know, O traitor, when Allah sets up the Throne, gathers the first and the last, and the hands and feet speak of what they used to earn, you will come to know how it stands between you and me with Him tomorrow.'"
He said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"She spoke the truth, she spoke the truth. How can Allah sanctify a people from whose strong the right of their weak is not taken?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, when may we abandon enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong?" He said:
"When there appears among you what appeared among the nations before you."
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what appeared among the nations before us?" He said:
"Kingship in your young ones, immorality in your elders, and knowledge in your worst ones."
Zayd said: The explanation of the meaning of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ:
"and knowledge in your worst ones"
is when knowledge is among the wicked.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will question a servant until He says: 'What prevented you, when you saw wrongdoing, from denouncing it?' Then, when Allah teaches the servant his plea, he will say: 'My Lord, I hoped in You and I was afraid of people.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in Madinah among some people, among them some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, when a man came in whose face bore a trace of humility. Some of the people said, "This is a man of Paradise, this is a man of Paradise."

He prayed two brief rak'ahs, then went out, and I followed him. He entered his house and I entered, and we talked. When he had become at ease, I said to him, "When you entered earlier, a man said such and such." He said, "Glory be to Allah! It is not right for anyone to say what he does not know. I will tell you why: I saw a vision during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I related it to him. I saw myself in a garden" (he described its spaciousness, its grass and its greenery) "and in the middle of the garden was a pillar of iron, its base on the ground and its top in the sky, and at its top was a handhold.
I was told, 'Climb it.'
I said to him, 'I cannot.'

Then an attendant came to me" (Ibn ʿAwn said: the munsif is the servant) "and he lifted my clothes from behind me" (he described how he raised him from behind with his hand) "and I climbed until I was at the top of the pillar, and I took hold of the handhold. I was told, 'Hold fast.'
I then woke up, and it was still in my hand. I related it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
'That garden is Islam, that pillar is the pillar of Islam, and that handhold is the firmest handhold. And you will remain upon Islam until you die.'"
He said: The man was ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was never jealous of any of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ as I was jealous of Khadījah, though I never saw her,
but the Prophet ﷺ used to mention her often,
and sometimes he would slaughter a sheep,
then cut it into pieces,
then send them to Khadījah's close friends.
Sometimes I said to him, "It is as if there were no woman in the world except Khadījah."
He would say, "She was such and such,
and I had children from her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, here is Khadījah, who has come to you with a vessel containing seasoning, or food, or drink. When she comes to you, convey to her greetings of peace from her Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and from me, and give her glad tidings of a house in Paradise made of hollow pearl, in which there is no noise and no toil."
Abū Bakr said in his narration, from Abū Hurayrah, and he did not say, "I heard."
And he did not say in the hadith, "and from me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hālah bint Khuwaylid, the sister of Khadījah, asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and he recognised the way Khadījah used to ask permission, and was startled by it. He said, "O Allah, Hālah!"
She said: I became jealous and said, "Why do you remember an old woman of the old women of Quraysh, with red gums,
who died long ago, when
Allah has given you someone better than her in exchange?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of ignorance there was a house called Dhū al-Khalaṣah,
and it was also called the Yemeni Kaʿbah,
or the Syrian Kaʿbah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Will you relieve me of Dhū al-Khalaṣah?"
He said: So I set out to it with a hundred and fifty horsemen from Aḥmas. He said: We destroyed it,
and killed whoever we found there. Then we came to him and informed him,
and he made supplication for us and for Aḥmas.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said that Hind bint ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah said, "O Messenger of Allah, there was no household on the face of the earth that I wished more to see humbled than your household,
[Yaḥyā was unsure whether she said 'ahl akhbiyah' or 'ahl khibāʾ'] and today there is no household that I wish more to see honoured than your household."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And by the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, [you will increase] still more."
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Sufyān is a miserly man.
Is there any blame on me if I feed [my family] from what belongs to him?" He said:
"No, except in a reasonable manner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah gave in marriage a girl who was a relative of hers from among the Anṣār. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said, "Have you sent the girl off?" They said, "Yes." He said,
"Did you send someone with her to sing?" She said, "No."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The Anṣār are a people who love song and poetry. If only you had sent with her someone who would say: 'We have come to you, we have come to you, so greetings to us and to you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when he heard the sound of
a drum. He put his two fingers into his ears, then moved away, and he did that three times.
Then he said, "This is what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended a wedding feast with the Prophet ﷺ in which there was neither meat nor bread.
Ibn Mājah said: No one narrated it except Ibn ʿUyaynah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said:] We were to prepare Fāṭimah so as to bring her to ʿAlī. So we set about the house and spread it with soft sand from the open areas of al-Baṭḥāʾ. Then we stuffed two cushions with palm fiber, which we fluffed with our hands. Then we fed [the guests] dates and raisins and gave them sweet water to drink. We took a wooden pole and set it across a corner of the house so that clothing could be thrown over it and the water-skin hung on it. We never saw a wedding better than the wedding of Fāṭimah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"For a previously married woman [the husband stays] three [nights], and for a virgin, seven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:]

"When any of you acquires a wife, a servant, or an animal, let him take hold of her forelock and say: 'O Allah, I ask You for the good in her and the good that she was created with, and I seek refuge in You from the evil in her and the evil that she was created with.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When any of you comes to his wife, let him cover himself and not strip bare like two donkeys."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:]
"Allah will not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her rear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth."
[He said it] three times: "Do not approach women in their rears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Muṣʿab told me that Mishraḥ ibn Hāʿān said: ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Shall I not tell you about the borrowed billy goat?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"He is the muḥallil [one who marries a divorced woman so she becomes lawful to her former husband]. Allah has cursed the muḥallil and the one for whom it is done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among what Allah revealed of the Qurʾān, and which was then dropped, was: "Only ten known nursings, or five known nursings, make [a marriage] unlawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The verse of stoning and the verse on suckling an adult ten times were revealed, and they were on a sheet under my bed. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and we were preoccupied with his death, a domestic animal came in and ate it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I had two sisters whom I had married in the Jāhiliyyah [pre-Islamic period]. He said,
"When you return, divorce one of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb took charge, he addressed the people and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted us temporary marriage (mutʿah) for three [days], then he prohibited it. By Allah, I do not know of anyone who contracted it while married but that I will stone him with stones, unless he brings me four witnesses that the Messenger of Allah permitted it after having prohibited it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ married while in the state of iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Choose carefully for your offspring, marry those who are compatible, and give [your daughters] in marriage to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled, he would draw lots among his wives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was displeased with Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy over something.
Ṣafiyyah said, "O ʿĀʾishah, would you be willing to reconcile the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with me, and in return you may have my day?" She said, "Yes."
So she took a headscarf of hers dyed with saffron and sprinkled it with water so that its scent would spread. Then she sat beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said,
"O ʿĀʾishah, keep away from me; it is not your day."
She said, "That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills."
Then she told him the matter, and he was reconciled with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She said: This verse, {and reconciliation is better}, was revealed about a man who had a wife who had been with him a long time and had borne him children, and he wanted to replace her. So she came to an agreement with him that she would stay with him and he would not divide his time equally for her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Among the best intercession is to intercede between two people in marriage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was the first of the Arabs to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah,
and we used to fight alongside the Prophet ﷺ with no food for us except the leaves of trees,
so that one of us would relieve himself as a camel or a sheep does,
with no mixture in it.
Then the Banū Asad began to rebuke me over Islam.
Then I would have failed and my deeds would have gone astray.
They had slandered him to ʿUmar,
saying, "He does not know how to pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: Ismāʿīl informed us; and the others said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us
— meaning Ibn Jaʿfar — from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard Ibn ʿUmar
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out an expedition and appointed Usāmah ibn Zayd as commander over them. People criticized his appointment, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and said:

"If you criticize his appointment, you used to criticize the appointment of his father before him. By Allah, he was truly fit for command, and he was among the dearest of people to me, and this one [Usāmah] is among the dearest of people to me after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of ours, O nation, is Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī on his shoulder, and he was saying:
"O Allah, I love him, so love him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My brother and I came from Yemen,
and we stayed for a while thinking only that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd was a man from the household of the Prophet ﷺ,
because of how often we saw him and his mother enter upon the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ — or he said: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ —: "
If the Anṣār were to take a valley or a mountain pass,
I would take the valley of the Anṣār,
and were it not for the Hijrah, I would be a man from the Anṣār."
Abū Hurayrah said: "He was not wronged, by my father and mother! They gave him refuge and they supported him."
Or another statement.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was digging the trench and we were carrying the earth. He passed by us and said:
"O Allah, there is no life but the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Anṣār and the Muhājirūn."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route.
And Abū Ḥāzim's name is Salamah ibn Dīnār al-Aʿraj, the ascetic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "I am exhausted [with hunger]."
So he sent word to one of his wives, and she said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, I have nothing but water."
Then he sent to another, and she said the same, until all of them said the same: "No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I have nothing but water." Then he said:
"Who will host this man tonight? May Allah have mercy on him."
A man from the Anṣār stood up and said, "I will, O Messenger of Allah."
He took him to his home and said to his wife, "Do you have anything?"
She said, "No, only the children's food."
He said, "Distract them with something, and when our guest comes in, put out the lamp and make him think that we are eating. When he reaches out to eat, get up to the lamp and put it out."
He said: So they sat, and the guest ate.
In the morning, he went to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Allah was amazed at what you two did for your guest last night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ubayy:
"Allah has commanded me to recite the Qur'an to you."
Ubayy said, "Did Allah name me to you?" He said:
"Allah named you to me."
So Ubayy began to weep.
Qatādah said: I was told that he recited to him, {Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture were not...}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Qur'an was collected during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by four, all of them from the Anṣār: Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Abū Zayd.
Qatādah said: I asked Anas, "Who is Abū Zayd?" He said, "One of my paternal uncles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was never jealous of any woman as I was jealous of Khadījah,
though she had died three years before he married me,
because I used to hear him mention her.
And his Lord had commanded him to give her glad tidings of a house in Paradise made of hollow pearl,
and he would slaughter a sheep and then send gifts from it to her close friends.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he was forty years old,
and he stayed thirteen years,
then he was commanded to emigrate,
so he emigrated to Medina,
and he stayed there ten years, then he ﷺ passed away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet ﷺ when the sun had passed its zenith and said, "Get up, O Muḥammad, and pray Ẓuhr when the sun has declined." Then he waited until a man's shadow was equal to his height, and came to him for ʿAṣr and said, "Get up, O Muḥammad, and pray ʿAṣr."

Then he waited until the sun had set, and came to him and said, "Get up and pray Maghrib." So he got up and prayed it exactly when the sun had set. Then he waited until the twilight had gone, and came to him and said, "Get up and pray ʿIshāʾ."
So he got up and prayed it. Then he came to him for the morning prayer when the dawn had spread, and said, "Get up, O Muḥammad, and pray."
So he got up and prayed the morning prayer. Then he came to him the next day when a man's shadow was equal to his height and said, "Get up, O Muḥammad, and pray."
So he prayed Ẓuhr. Then Jibrīl (peace be upon him) came to him when a man's shadow was twice his height and said, "Get up, O Muḥammad, and pray."
So he prayed ʿAṣr. Then he came to him for Maghrib when the sun had set, at the same time as before, without any difference, and said, "Get up and pray."
So he prayed Maghrib. Then he came to him for ʿIshāʾ when the first third of the night had passed and said, "Get up and pray."
So he prayed ʿIshāʾ. Then he came to him for the morning prayer when it had become very bright and said, "Get up and pray."
So he prayed the morning prayer. Then he said,
"The time is anywhere between these two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the morning prayer when the dawn had become clear to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about the time of the morning prayer. The next morning, when dawn broke, he ordered that the prayer be called, and he led us in prayer. The following day, when it had become bright, he ordered that the prayer be called, and he led us in prayer. Then he said,
"Where is the one who asked about the time of prayer? The time is between these two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the morning prayer at Khaybar in the darkness before dawn, while he was close to them, and he attacked them. He said,
"Allahu Akbar! Khaybar is ruined" (twice). "When we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Pray the dawn prayer when it is bright."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From his people among the Anṣār, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The more you delay the dawn prayer until it is bright, the greater the reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I later asked about the two rakʿahs

before sunset. He said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr used to pray them, so Muʿāwiyah sent to him asking, 'What are these two rakʿahs at sunset?'" The report was referred to Umm Salamah, and Umm Salamah said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs before ʿAṣr, but he was kept busy from them, so he prayed them when the sun had set. I never saw him pray them before or after."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī stood up to pray two rakʿahs before Maghrib. I said to ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, "Look at this one, what prayer is he praying?" He turned to him, saw him, and said, "This is a prayer we used to pray in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh about prayer

while traveling. We said, "Did ʿAbdullāh combine any of the prayers while traveling?" He said, "No, except at Jamʿ." Then I came to him and he said, "Ṣafiyyah was with him, and she sent word to him: 'I am in the last day of this world and the first day of the Hereafter.'
So he rode, and I was with him, and he hurried along until the time of prayer came. The muʾadhdhin said to him, 'The prayer, O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.'
He kept going until, when he was between the two prayers, he dismounted and said to the muʾadhdhin, 'Call the iqāmah, and when I finish Ẓuhr, call the iqāmah again right where you are.'

So he called the iqāmah and prayed Ẓuhr, two rakʿahs, then gave the salām. Then he called the iqāmah in his place and prayed ʿAṣr, two rakʿahs. Then he rode and hurried along until the sun set. The muʾadhdhin said to him, 'The prayer, O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.'
He said, 'Do as you did before.'
He went on until the stars had become thick, then he dismounted and said, 'Call the iqāmah, and when I finish, call it again.'
So he prayed Maghrib, three rakʿahs, then called the iqāmah in his place and prayed the last ʿIshāʾ. Then he gave one salām, to the front. Then he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'When any of you faces a matter whose passing he fears, let him pray this prayer [in this way].'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He prayed in Basra Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr with nothing between them, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ with nothing between them. He did that because of being occupied. Ibn ʿAbbās claimed that he prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, eight prostrations, with nothing between them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with a man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Mujāshiʿ, of Banū Sulaym. The sheep became scarce, so he ordered a caller to announce that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"The jadhaʿ suffices for what the thaniyyah suffices for."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Eid al-Adha prayer at the prayer ground. When he finished his sermon, he came down from his pulpit and a ram was brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered it with his own hand and said:
"In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. This is on behalf of me and of those of my Ummah who have not sacrificed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we eat what we kill, but we do not eat what Allah kills?" So Allah revealed: "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses," up to His saying:
"and if you obey them, indeed you would be polytheists."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what if one of us catches game and has no knife with him? May he slaughter with a sharp stone or a split piece of a stick?" He said:
"Let the blood flow with whatever you wish, and mention the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the ʿaqīqah for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, with two rams for each.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whatever is cut off from an animal while it is alive, what is cut off from it is carrion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man or a woman may act in obedience to Allah for sixty years, then death comes to them and they cause harm in the bequest, so the Fire becomes due for them."
Then Abū Hurayrah recited to me:
"after any bequest by which he bequeaths or any debt, without causing harm, a bequest from Allah," up to His saying:
"that is the great success." Abū ʿĪsā said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith.
And Naṣr ibn ʿAlī who narrated from al-Ashʿath ibn Jābir is the grandfather of Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed, "And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best," and "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly," the verse, whoever had an orphan went and separated his food from the orphan's food and his drink from the orphan's drink. Some of his food would be left over and be kept for the orphan until he ate it or it spoiled. This was difficult for them, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And they ask you about orphans. Say: Improving their condition is best; and if you mix with them, they are your brothers." So they mixed their food with his food and their drink with his drink.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Knowledge is three things, and whatever is besides that is surplus: a firmly established verse, an established Sunnah, or a just obligation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, they seek a ruling from you regarding kalālah. What is kalālah?" He said:
"The verse of the summer will suffice you."
I said to Abū Isḥāq, "Is it the one who dies and leaves behind neither a child nor a parent?" He said, "Yes, that is what they thought it to be."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "My grandson has died; what is my share of his inheritance?" He said, "You have a sixth."
When the man turned away, he called him back and said:
"You have another sixth."
When he turned away, he called him back and said:
"The other sixth is a food allotment."
Qatādah said: They do not know with what he inherited it.
Qatādah said: The least that a grandfather inherits is a sixth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever leaves behind a dependent, then to me." And sometimes he said:
"To Allah and to His Messenger."

"And whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs. I am the heir of one who has no heir; I pay the blood-money for him and inherit from him. And the maternal uncle is the heir of one who has no heir; he pays the blood-money on his behalf and inherits from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A freed slave
of the Prophet ﷺ fell from a date palm and died, leaving behind wealth but neither a child nor a close relative. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Give his inheritance to a man from the people of his village."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any inheritance that was divided in the Jāhiliyyah remains according to the division of the Jāhiliyyah, and any inheritance that Islam reached is according to the division of Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ [spoke of] four things which pleased me and impressed me: he forbade a woman to travel a distance of two days unless her husband or a mahram is with her.
And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, where will you stay tomorrow?" This was during his Hajj, when we drew near to Makkah. He said:
"Has ʿAqīl left us any dwelling?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is not permissible for any of you to carry weapons in Makkah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam

addressed the people and mentioned Makkah, its people and its sanctity, but did not mention Madinah, its people and its sanctity. So Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj called out to him and said: "Why do I hear you mention Makkah, its people and its sanctity, but not mention Madinah, its people and its sanctity, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared sacred what lies between its two lava plains? That is with us written on a Khawlānī parchment, if you wish I will recite it to you."
He said: Marwān fell silent, then said: "I have heard some of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
both from Abū Aḥmad,
Abū Bakr said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Asadī narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred, and I have made Madinah sacred, what lies between its two lava plains: its thorny trees are not to be cut and its game is not to be hunted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd, that Saʿd

rode to his palace at al-ʿAqīq and found a slave cutting down trees or beating them down for leaves, so he took his belongings. When Saʿd returned, the slave's people came to him and spoke to him, asking him to return to their servant, or to them, what he had taken from their servant. He said: "Allah forbid that I return something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me as spoils."
And he refused to return it to them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That hardship and severe difficulty had struck them in Madinah, and that he came to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and said to him: "I have a large family and hardship has struck us, so I wanted to move my family to some rural area."

Abū Saʿīd said: "Do not do so. Stay in Madinah, for we went out with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ—I think he said—until we reached ʿUsfān. He stayed there for some nights, and the people said: 'By Allah, we are doing nothing here, while our families are left behind and we do not feel secure about them.'
That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

'What is this that has reached me of your talk?'—I do not know how he phrased it—'By the One by whom I swear,' or 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, I was resolved'—or 'if you wish,' I do not know which he said—'to order my she-camel to be saddled and then not undo a knot of hers until I reach Madinah.' And he said: 'O Allah, Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred and made it a sanctuary, and I have made Madinah sacred, a sanctuary between its two mountain passes: that no blood be shed in it, no weapon be carried in it for fighting, and no tree be beaten down in it except for fodder. O Allah, bless us in our city. O Allah, bless us in our ṣāʿ. O Allah, bless us in our mudd. O Allah, bless us in our ṣāʿ. O Allah, bless us in our mudd. O Allah, bless us in our city. O Allah, place two blessings with the blessing. By the One in whose hand is my soul, there is no mountain pass or road in Madinah except that two angels are guarding it, until you come to it.' Then he said to the people: 'Set out.'"

So we set out and headed toward Madinah. And by the One by whom we swear, or by whom [one] swears—the doubt is from Ḥammād—we had not yet put down our saddles when we entered Madinah, until the Banū ʿAbdullāh ibn Ghaṭafān raided us, and nothing had provoked them before that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I have made sacred what lies between the two lava plains of Madinah, just as Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred."
He said: Then Abū Saʿīd would take—and Abū Bakr said: would find—one of us with a bird in his hand, and he would free it from his hand and then release it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pointed with his hand toward Madinah and said:
"It is a sanctuary of safety."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr, all from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar,
from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of my nation will be patient through the hardship and severity of Madinah except that I will be an intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection, or a witness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr, all from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar: al-ʿAlāʾ informed me, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Messiah will come from the direction of the east, intending Madinah, until he halts behind Uḥud. Then the angels will turn his face toward Syria, and there he will perish."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he sent his servant with a ṣāʿ of wheat and said, "Sell it, then buy barley with it."

The servant went and took a ṣāʿ and a little more than a ṣāʿ. When he came to Maʿmar he told him about that, and Maʿmar said to him, "Why did you do that? Go and return it, and do not take anything except like for like, for I used to hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Food for food, like for like."
He said: Our food in those days was barley.
It was said to him, "But it is not the same [as wheat]." He said, "I fear that it may resemble it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dates were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"What are these dates? They are not from our dates."
The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, we sold two ṣāʿs of our dates for one ṣāʿ of these."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This is usury (ribā). Return it, then sell our dates and buy for us some of these."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās about currency exchange,
and they saw no harm in it. Then I was sitting with Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, so I asked him about currency exchange, and he said, "Whatever is in excess is usury (ribā)."

I objected to that because of what the two of them had said. He said, "I will only tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: The owner of a date grove came to him with a ṣāʿ of fine dates, and the dates of the Prophet ﷺ were of this kind. The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Where did you get this?"
He said, "I went with two ṣāʿs [of inferior dates] and bought this ṣāʿ with them, for the price of this one in the market is such-and-such and the price of that one is such-and-such."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Woe to you! You have engaged in usury (ribā). If you want to do that, sell your dates for some goods, then buy with your goods whichever dates you wish."

Abū Saʿīd said, "Is it not more fitting that dates for dates would be usury than silver for silver?" He said: Afterwards I came to Ibn ʿUmar and he forbade me, but I did not go to Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: Abū al-Ṣahbāʾ told me that he asked Ibn ʿAbbās about it in Makkah and he disliked it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
the wording being ʿAmr's. Isḥāq said, "He informed us," while the others said,
"Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿUbayd
Allah ibn Abī Yazīd, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās
say: Usāmah ibn Zayd informed me
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Usury (ribā) is only in deferred transactions."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no usury (ribā) in what is exchanged hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was addressing the people in Ḥimṣ, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear."
Then he mentioned [a narration] like the hadith of Zakariyyāʾ from al-Shaʿbī, up to his words:
"he is about to fall into it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and my water-carrying camel lagged behind.
And he related the hadith, and he said in it: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prodded it, then said to me:
"Ride, in the name of Allah."
He also added: He kept on giving me more [of his favor] and saying:
"And may Allah forgive you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this story, except that he said: Then he bought it from me for a price that he named.
And he did not mention the two ūqiyahs, the dirham, or the two dirhams.
And he said: He ordered that a cow be slaughtered, and then its meat was distributed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived [in Madīnah] while the people were paying in advance for goods, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"Whoever pays in advance, let him pay in advance only for a known measure and a known weight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman in Madīnah granted a garden of hers as a lifetime grant to a son of hers. Then he died, and she died after him, leaving a son, and he [the deceased] had brothers, sons of the woman who had made the grant. The son of the woman who made the grant said, "The garden has returned to us," and the sons of the one who received the grant said, "Rather, it belonged to our father in his life and in his death."

They brought their dispute to Ṭāriq, the freed slave of ʿUthmān, and he called Jābir, who testified from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the lifetime grant belongs to the one who received it. So Ṭāriq ruled accordingly, then wrote to ʿAbd al-Malik and informed him of that and of Jābir's testimony, and ʿAbd al-Malik said, "Jābir has spoken the truth."
So Ṭāriq enforced that.
And that garden remains with the sons of the one who received the grant to this day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The lifetime grant (ʿumrā) is a permitted gift."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"The lifetime grant (ʿumrā) is an inheritance for its people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The lifetime grant (ʿumrā) is a permitted gift."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not right for a Muslim who has something he wishes to bequeath to spend two nights without having his will written down with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...to her, while he was asking her about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {until, when the messengers despaired}. He said: I said, "Were they denied or did they [themselves] lie?" ʿĀʾishah said, "They were denied."
I said, "But they were certain that their people had denied them, so what is [meant by] 'thinking'?" She said, "Yes, by my life, they were certain of that."
I said to her, "{and they thought that they had been lied to}?" She said, "Allah forbid! The messengers did not think that of their Lord."
I said, "Then what is this verse?"
She said, "They are the followers of the messengers who believed in their Lord and believed them."
Their trial was prolonged for them,

and help was delayed from them, until the messengers despaired of those among their people who had denied them, and the messengers thought that their followers had denied them; then the help of Allah came to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Prophet ﷺ returned to Khadījah with his heart trembling,
and she took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal,
who was a man who had become a Christian and used to read the Gospel in Arabic.
Waraqah said, "What do you see?" So he told him.
Waraqah said, "This is the Nāmūs that Allah sent down upon Moses,
and if I live to see your day, I will support you with strong support."
The Nāmūs is the keeper of the secret, who informs [another] of what he conceals from others.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey, until he reached the fifth heaven,
and there was Aaron. He said, "This is Aaron; greet him." So I greeted him,
and he returned the greeting, then said, "Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ [said]:
"People will be struck unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and there I will find Moses holding one of the legs of the Throne."
And al-Mājishūn said, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Faḍl,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"I will be the first to be raised, and there will be Moses holding the Throne."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came out to us one day and said:
"The nations were presented to me,
and I saw a great multitude that blocked the horizon. It was said, 'This is Moses with his people.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Mujāhid about the prostration in Sūrah Ṣād,

and he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, "From where do you derive the prostration?" He said, "Do you not recite: {and from his descendants, David and Solomon} ... {Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance}? David was one of those whom your Prophet ﷺ was commanded to follow,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated at it." {ʿUjāb} means amazing.
{Al-Qiṭṭ} means the record; here it is the record of good deeds.
Mujāhid said: {fī ʿizzah} means being contentious.
{The last religion} is the religion of Quraysh. Ikhtilāq means lying.
Al-Asbāb are the paths of the heaven in its gates. {A defeated army, there} means Quraysh. {Those are the factions} are the past generations. {Fawāq} means returning.
{Qiṭṭanā} means our punishment. {We took them in mockery}; we encompassed them. Atrāb means peers.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Al-Ayd means strength in worship; al-Abṣār means insight in the matter of Allah.
{the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord} means from the remembrance.
{He began to stroke} means he stroked the manes of the horses and their hocks. {Al-Aṣfād} means shackles.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey:
"Then he ascended until he came to the second heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Gabriel.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Has he been sent for?' He said, 'Yes.' When I passed through,
there were John and Jesus, who were cousins through their mothers.
He said, 'This is John and Jesus; greet them.'
I greeted them and they returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I saw Jesus, Moses, and Abraham.
As for Jesus, he was reddish, with curly hair and a broad chest,
and as for Moses, he was brown, heavily built, with straight hair, as if he were one of the men of the Zuṭṭ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not exalt me excessively as the Christians exalted the son of Mary,
for I am only His servant,
so say: 'the servant of Allah and His Messenger.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul,
the son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just ruler; he will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizyah,
and wealth will overflow until no one will accept it,
until a single prostration will be better than the world and all that is in it."

Then Abū Hurayrah would say, "Recite, if you wish: {There is none from the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the one praying places his hand on his waist, and she said, "The Jews do this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Wakīʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said—and Ibn Numayr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Whoever dies associating anything with Allah will enter the Fire."
And I said: And whoever dies not associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Maʿmar and Yūnus said: Az-Zuhrī said: Abū Salamah informed me that ʿĀʾishah told him that Abū Bakr came on a horse from his dwelling at as-Sunḥ until he dismounted and entered the mosque. He did not speak to the people until he entered upon ʿĀʾishah, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was covered with a Yemeni striped cloak. He uncovered his face, then bent over him and kissed him and wept. Then he said: "May my father be your ransom! By Allah, Allah will never bring two deaths upon you. As for the death that Allah decreed for you, you have [now] died it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon and said: "
Zayd took the banner and was struck down;
then Jaʿfar took it and was struck down;
then ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah took it and was struck down;
then Khālid ibn al-Walīd took it without having been appointed commander, and victory was granted to him." And he said: "It would not please us that they were with us."
Ayyūb said, or he said: "
It would not please them that they were with us." And his eyes were shedding tears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit when he was ill died during the night, and they buried him at night.
When morning came, they informed him, and he said: "
What prevented you from letting me know?"
They said: It was night, and it was dark, and we disliked to trouble you.
So he came to his grave and prayed over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā fell ill with a severe pain and fainted, with his head in the lap of one of the women of his family. One of the women of his family cried out, and he was unable to respond to her at all. When he recovered, he said: I disown what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disowned, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disowned the woman who raises her voice [in wailing], the one who shaves her head, and the one who tears her clothes [in mourning].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent out a detachment of men called the Qurrāʾ (Qur'an reciters), and they were killed.
I never saw the Prophet ﷺ grieve over anything as he grieved over them,
so he made qunūt for a month in the dawn prayer, saying: "
A tribe has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah fell ill, so the Prophet ﷺ came to visit him, together with ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them. When he entered, he found him surrounded by his family and said: "Has he passed away?"
They said: No, O Messenger of Allah.
The Prophet ﷺ wept, and when the people saw the weeping of the Prophet ﷺ, they wept. He said: "
Do you not hear? Allah does not punish for the tears of the eye,
nor for the grief of the heart,
but He punishes for this"—and he pointed to his tongue—"or shows mercy. And the dead is punished for the weeping of his family over him."
And ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to strike with a stick because of this,
throw stones, and throw dust [at those who wailed].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you sees a funeral procession, then if he is not walking with it, let him stand until it has passed him,
or he has passed it, or it is set down before it passes him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to say: "
When the funeral bier is set down and the men carry it on their shoulders,
if the deceased was righteous, it says: 'Take me forward.'
And if he was not righteous, it says to its family: 'Woe to it! Where are they taking it?' Everything hears its voice except man,
and if man were to hear it, he would fall unconscious."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Today a righteous man from Abyssinia has died, so come and pray over him."
He said: So we formed rows, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed over him while we stood in rows.
Abū az-Zubayr said from Jābir: I was in the second row.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to Ibn ʿUmar: Abū Hurayrah says: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Whoever follows a funeral procession will have a qīrāṭ of reward."
Ibn ʿUmar said: Abū Hurayrah has said too much to us.
So he sent to ʿĀʾishah and asked her, and she confirmed Abū Hurayrah. Then Ibn ʿUmar said: We have indeed neglected many qīrāṭs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the illness from which he did not recover: "
May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians;
they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship."
Had it not been for that, his grave would have been made prominent,
except that he feared, or it was feared, that it would be taken as a place of worship.
And from Hilāl, who said: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr gave me a kunyah, though no child had been born to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man was buried with my father, but I was not at ease until I took him out and placed him in a separate grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this report, and without mentioning the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"And let him say, 'My master and my protector.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not call a hypocrite 'master,' for if he is a master, you have angered your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not say, 'What Allah wills and so-and-so wills,' but say, 'What Allah wills, and then what so-and-so wills.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ when his mount stumbled, so I said, "May Satan perish!" He said:

"Do not say, 'May Satan perish,' for when you say that, he swells until he becomes like a house and says, 'By my power.' But say, 'In the name of Allah,' for when you say that, he shrinks until he becomes like a fly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, and Misʿar said, "I think he was from Khuzāʿah," "If only I had prayed and found rest." It seemed that they disapproved of that, so he said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'O Bilāl, call the iqāmah for the prayer, give us rest through it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father and I went out

to visit a relative by marriage of ours from the Anṣār. The time for prayer came, and he said to one of his household, "O girl, bring me water for ablution, perhaps I will pray and find rest." He said: We disapproved of that, so he said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Get up, Bilāl, call the iqāmah and give us rest through the prayer.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ attribute no one to anything except to the religion.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from among the freed slaves of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah al-ʿAdawī narrated to him from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir that he said: One day my mother called me while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in our house, and she said, "Come here, I will give you something."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"What did you want to give him?"
She said, "I would give him dates."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Indeed, had you not given him anything, a lie would have been recorded against you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"It is enough sin for a person that he narrates everything he hears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I made a transaction with the Prophet ﷺ before he was sent as a prophet, and a remainder was still due to him. I promised him that I would bring it to him at his place, but I forgot. Then I remembered after three days, so I came, and there he was in his place. He said:
"Young man, you have put me to hardship. I have been here for three days waiting for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ and heard ʿĀʾishah's voice raised. When he entered, he reached for her to slap her and said, "I will not see you raise your voice against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" The Prophet ﷺ began to hold him back, and Abū Bakr went out angry. When Abū Bakr had left, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"How did you see me rescue you from the man?"

He said: Abū Bakr stayed away for some days, then asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that the two had reconciled. He said to them, "Admit me into your peace as you admitted me into your quarrel." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"We have done so, we have done so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the expedition of Tabūk while he was in a tent of leather. I greeted him with salām, he returned it and said, "Come in."
I said, "All of me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "All of you." So I entered.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He only said, "Come in, all of you,"
because of the smallness of the tent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ﷺ: that they were traveling with the Prophet ﷺ, and a man among them fell asleep. One of them went to a rope he had and took it, and the man was startled. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not permissible for a Muslim to frighten a Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever learns the artifices of speech in order to captivate the hearts of men, or people, Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any obligatory or voluntary act."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He read in the original manuscript of Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, and his son Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated it to him, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Ḍamḍam narrated to me from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, who said: Abū Ẓabyah narrated to us that ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said one day, when a man stood up and spoke at great length, ʿAmr said, "Had he been moderate in his speech, it would have been better for him. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'I have been shown, or commanded, to be concise in speech, for conciseness is best.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king, 'I have grown old, so send me a boy to whom I can teach sorcery.'

So the king sent him a boy to teach. On the boy's way [to the sorcerer] there was a monk, so he sat with him and listened to his words, and it pleased him. Whenever he went to the sorcerer, he would pass by the monk and sit with him, and when he reached the sorcerer, the sorcerer would beat him. He complained of that to the monk, who said, 'If you fear the sorcerer, say, "My family kept me back."
And if you fear your family, say, "The sorcerer kept me back."'

While he was in that state, he came upon a huge beast that had stopped the people [from passing]. He said, 'Today I will know whether the sorcerer is better or the monk is better.' So he took a stone and said, 'O Allah, if the way of the monk is more beloved to You than the way of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so that the people may pass.'
He threw it and killed it, and the people passed on. Then he went to the monk and told him, and the monk said to him, 'My son, today you are better than I.
Your affair has reached what I see, and you will be tested; if you are tested, do not point to me.'

The boy used to heal the born-blind and the leper, and to cure people of all [kinds of] illnesses. A companion of the king, who had gone blind, heard of him and came to him with many gifts. He said, 'All that is here is yours if you cure me.' The boy said, 'I cure no one; only Allah cures. If you believe in Allah, I will supplicate to Allah and He will cure you.'
So he believed in Allah, and Allah cured him. Then he came to the king and sat with him as he used to sit. The king said to him, 'Who restored your sight to you?' He said, 'My Lord.'
The king said, 'Do you have a lord other than me?' He said, 'My Lord and your Lord is Allah.'

So the king seized him and kept torturing him until he pointed to the boy. The boy was brought, and the king said to him, 'My son, your sorcery has reached the point that you heal the born-blind and the leper, and you do this and that.'
He said, 'I cure no one; only Allah cures.'
So the king seized him and kept torturing him until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him, 'Turn back from your religion.'

He refused, so [the king] called for a saw, placed the saw in the middle of his head and split him until his two halves fell. Then the king's companion was brought, and it was said to him, 'Turn back from your religion.'
He refused, so the saw was placed in the middle of his head and he was split with it until his two halves fell. Then the boy was brought, and it was said to him, 'Turn back from your religion.'

He refused, so [the king] handed him over to a group of his men and said, 'Take him to such-and-such mountain and climb the mountain with him. When you reach its summit, if he turns back from his religion [let him go], otherwise throw him down.' They took him and climbed the mountain with him, and he said, 'O Allah, suffice me against them in whatever way You will.'
The mountain shook with them and they fell, and he came walking to the king. The king said to him, 'What happened to your companions?' He said, 'Allah sufficed me against them.'

So [the king] handed him over to another group of his men and said, 'Take him and carry him in a small boat, and when you reach the middle of the sea, if he turns back from his religion [let him go], otherwise throw him in.'
They took him, and he said, 'O Allah, suffice me against them in whatever way You will.'
The boat capsized with them and they drowned, and he came walking to the king. The king said to him, 'What happened to your companions?' He said, 'Allah sufficed me against them.'
Then he said to the king, 'You will not be able to kill me until you do what I command you.'

The king said, 'What is it?' He said, 'Gather the people on one plain and crucify me on a palm trunk. Then take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the bow, and say, "In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy."
Then shoot me; if you do that, you will kill me.'
So [the king] gathered the people on one plain and crucified him on a trunk. Then he took an arrow from his quiver, placed the arrow in the bow, and said, 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.'

Then he shot him, and the arrow struck his temple. The boy placed his hand on his temple where the arrow had hit, and died. The people said, 'We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy! We believe in the Lord of the boy!'
Then the king was told, 'Do you see what you were afraid of? By Allah, what you feared has befallen you: the people have believed.'
So he ordered trenches to be dug at the entrances of the roads. They were dug and fires were kindled, and he said, 'Whoever does not turn back from his religion, throw him into it.'
Or it was said to him, 'Plunge in.'
They did so, until a woman came with her child, and she hesitated to fall into it. The boy [the child] said to her, 'O Mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed: "And warn your closest kinsmen" — and your tribe, the sincere ones among them —
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he climbed Mount Ṣafā and cried out, "O morning danger!"
They said, "Who is this calling out?" They said, "Muhammad."
So they gathered around him, and he said,
"O Banū so-and-so, O Banū so-and-so, O Banū so-and-so, O Banū ʿAbd Manāf, O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib!"
They gathered around him, and he said,
"Tell me, if I were to inform you that cavalry was coming out from the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?"
They said, "We have never found you to lie." He said,
"Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment."
He said: Abū Lahab said, "May you perish! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he got up, and this chapter was revealed: "Perished are the hands of Abū Lahab, and he has perished."
Thus al-Aʿmash recited it, to the end of the chapter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with ʿAbdullāh, who was reclining among us, when a man came to him and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, there is a storyteller at the gates of Kindah who tells people that the sign of the Smoke will come and seize the breaths of the disbelievers, while the believers will suffer from it something like a cold." ʿAbdullāh sat up, angry, and said, "O people, fear Allah! Whoever among you knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say, 'Allah knows best,' for it is part of knowledge that one says 'Allah knows best' about what he does not know. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet ﷺ: 'Say: I do not ask you for any payment for this, and I am not among those who pretend.' When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the people turning away, he said,
"O Allah, seven years like the seven years of Yūsuf."

He said: So a drought seized them that destroyed everything, until they ate hides and carrion because of hunger, and one of them would look at the sky and see something like smoke. Abū Sufyān came to him and said, "O Muhammad, you have come commanding obedience to Allah and the maintenance of family ties, yet your people have perished, so pray to Allah for them." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "So watch for the day when the sky brings a clear smoke, covering the people; this is a painful punishment," up to His words: "you will surely return [to disbelief]."

He said: "Will the punishment of the Hereafter be removed?" "On the day We seize with the greatest seizure, We will surely take retribution." So the seizure was the day of Badr. The sign of the Smoke, the Seizure, the Inevitable Punishment, and the sign of the Romans have already passed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask permission on the day of one of us [wives] after this verse was revealed: "You may postpone whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will, and there is no blame on you if you seek one whom you had set aside."
I said to her, "What did you used to say?" She said, "I used to say to him, 'If the matter were up to me, O Messenger of Allah, I would not prefer anyone over you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: Aflaḥ, the brother of Abū al-Quʿays, asked permission to see me after the observance of hijāb had been revealed.
I said, "I will not permit him until I ask the Prophet ﷺ about it, for his brother Abū al-Quʿays did not nurse me,
but the wife of Abū al-Quʿays nursed me."
Then the Prophet ﷺ came in to me, and I said to him, "O Messenger of Allah,
Aflaḥ, the brother of Abū al-Quʿays, asked permission,
and I refused to admit him until I asked you." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"What prevented you from permitting your paternal uncle?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, the man did not nurse me,
but the wife of Abū al-Quʿays nursed me." He said,
"Permit him, for he is your paternal uncle. May your right hand be covered in dust."
ʿUrwah said: For that reason ʿĀʾishah used to say, "Treat as forbidden through nursing what you treat as forbidden through lineage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish rabbi came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Muhammad," or "O Abū al-Qāsim, Allah the Exalted will hold the heavens on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains and trees on one finger, water and moist earth on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger. Then He will shake them and say, 'I am the King, I am the King.'"

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, in amazement at what the rabbi said and in confirmation of it. Then he recited: "They did not esteem Allah with true esteem. The whole earth will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate [with Him]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection,
and He will roll up the heavens in His right hand, then say, 'I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?'"
Shuʿayb, al-Zubaydī, Ibn Musāfir, and Isḥāq ibn Yaḥyā said, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salamah:
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and a neighbor of mine from the Ansar, from Banū Umayyah ibn Zayd,
which is among the upper districts of Madinah,
used to take turns visiting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He would go down one day and I would go down the next day.
When I went down, I would bring him the news of that day, of revelation and other matters,
and when he went down, he would do the same.
Then my Ansari companion went down on his day,
and he knocked on my door very hard.
He said, "Is he there?" I was alarmed and came out to him, and he said, "A great event has occurred."
He said: I went in to Ḥafṣah and found her weeping. I said, "Has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced you all?" She said, "I do not know."
Then I went in to the Prophet ﷺ and said, while standing, "Have you divorced your wives?" He said, "No."
So I said, "Allahu akbar!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out,
and ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥudhāfah stood up and said, "Who is my father?" He said, "Your father is Ḥudhāfah."
Then he repeatedly said, "Ask me."
So ʿUmar knelt on his knees and said, "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet." Then he fell silent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah,
who will be the most fortunate of people with your intercession on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I thought, O Abū Hurayrah, that no one would ask me about this hadith before you,
because of what I have seen of your eagerness for hadith.
The most fortunate of people with my intercession on the Day of Resurrection is the one who says, 'There is no god but Allah,'
sincerely from his heart or his soul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with this [report].
And from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aṣbahānī,
who said: I heard Abū Ḥāzim,
from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
"Three who have not reached the age of sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, would not hear anything she did not know without going back to it until she understood it,
and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever is brought to account will be punished."
ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "Does Allah, the Exalted, not say, {Then he will be judged with an easy reckoning}?" She said that he said:
"That is only the presentation [of deeds],
but whoever is examined thoroughly in the reckoning will be destroyed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy was born to a man among us, and he named him al-Qāsim. The Ansar said, "We will not call you Abū al-Qāsim, and we will not give you the comfort of your eye."
So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, a boy was born to me,
and I named him al-Qāsim, and the Ansar said, 'We will not call you Abū al-Qāsim, and we will not give you the comfort of your eye.'" The Prophet ﷺ said, "The Ansar have done well. Use my name,
but do not use my kunyah,
for I am only a Qāsim [distributor]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I memorized two vessels [of knowledge] from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
As for one of them, I have spread it,
and as for the other, if I were to spread it, this throat would be cut.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was mentioned to me that the Prophet ﷺ said to Muʿādh:
"Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him will enter Paradise."
He said, "Shall I not give the people the good news?" He said, "No,
I fear that they will rely on it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that he used to carry with the Prophet ﷺ a water container for his ablution and his need.
While he was following him with it, he said, "Who is this?"
I said, "I am Abū Hurayrah." He said:
"Find me some stones to clean myself with,
and do not bring me a bone or dung."
So I brought him stones, carrying them in the fold of my garment, until I put them beside him, then I left,
and when he had finished, I walked [with him].
I said, "What is the matter with bones and dung?" He said:
"They are the food of the jinn,
and the delegation of the jinn of Naṣībīn came to me, and what excellent jinn they were, and they asked me for provisions,
so I prayed to Allah for them that they would not pass by a bone or dung without finding food on it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed ablution washing each part twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
