"When one of you performs ablution, let him put water in his nose and then blow it out,
and whoever cleans himself with stones, let him use an odd number.
When one of you wakes from his sleep, let him wash his hand before putting it into his ablution water,
for none of you knows where his hand spent the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbīdah, "We have some of the hair of the Prophet ﷺ that we obtained from Anas,
or from the family of Anas." He said, "For me to have a single hair of his is dearer to me than the world and everything in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shaved his head, Abū Ṭalḥah was the first to take some of his hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from the Ansār came to the Prophet ﷺ asking [for help], and he said:
"Do you have nothing in your house?"
He said: "Yes, a coarse cloth, part of which we wear and part of which we spread out, and a wooden bowl from which we drink water." He said: "Bring them to me."
So he brought them to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took them in his hand and said:
"Who will buy these two?"
A man said: "I will take them for one dirham." He said:
"Who will offer more than a dirham?"
[He said it] two or three times. A man said: "I will take them for two dirhams."
So he gave them to him, took the two dirhams, gave them to the Ansārī, and said:
"Buy food with one of them and leave it with your family, and buy an axe with the other and bring it to me."
He brought it to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fixed a wooden handle into it with his own hand, then said to him:
"Go, gather firewood and sell it, and do not let me see you for fifteen days."
So the man went off gathering firewood and selling it. He came back having earned ten dirhams, and he bought a garment with some of it and food with some of it.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"This is better for you than that begging should come as a blemish on your face on the Day of Resurrection. Begging is not appropriate except for three: one in severe poverty, one in crushing debt, or one with a painful blood-debt [to pay]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever is struck by want and brings it before people, his want will not be relieved. But whoever is struck by want and brings it before Allah, Allah will soon grant him provision, either sooner or later."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man said] to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Shall I ask, Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No. But if you must ask, then ask the righteous."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever seeks refuge with you by Allah, give him refuge; and whoever asks you by Allah, give to him."
Sahl and ʿUthmān said:
"And whoever invites you, accept his invitation." Then they agreed:
"And whoever does you a kindness, repay him."
Musaddad and ʿUthmān said:
"If you cannot find [the means], then pray to Allah for him until you know that you have repaid him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to give charity, and that coincided with my having some wealth. I said: "Today I will outdo Abū Bakr, if I am ever to outdo him." He said: I came with half of my wealth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What have you left for your family?"
I said: "The same amount." Then Abū Bakr came with everything he had, and [the Prophet ﷺ] said:
"Abū Bakr, what have you left for your family?"
He said: "I have left for them Allah and His Messenger." I said: "By Allah, I will never outdo him in anything."
This is a hasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She died. He said: "Messenger of Allah, my mother has died. Shall I give charity on her behalf?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Which charity is best?" He said: "Providing water to drink."
So that is the water-station of Saʿd in Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and his name is
Ziyād ibn al-Mundhir al-Hamdānī, from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī,
from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Any believer who feeds a hungry believer, Allah will feed him on the Day of Resurrection from the fruits of Paradise. Any believer who gives a thirsty believer something to drink, Allah will give him to drink on the Day of Resurrection from the sealed nectar. And any believer who clothes a believer who is naked, Allah will clothe him from the green garments of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded giving charity, and a man said: "Messenger of Allah, I have a dinar." He said:
"Spend it on yourself."
He said: "I have another." He said:
"Spend it on your children."
He said: "I have another." He said:
"Spend it on your wife." Or he said: "your husband."
He said: "I have another." He said:
"Spend it on your servant."
He said: "I have another." He said: "You know best."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever finds a lost item should have one or two just witnesses attest to it, then he must not alter it or conceal it. If its owner comes, he has the greater right to it; otherwise it is the property of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Messenger of Allah, is Hajj every year or only once?" He said:
"Rather, once only. Whoever does more, it is voluntary."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed al-ʿAqīq as the station [for entering ihrām] for the people of the East.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A wife] of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed one cow on behalf of the family of Muhammad during the Farewell Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever anticipates [Allah's reward for the loss of] three from his own loins will enter Paradise."
A woman stood up and said, "Or two?" He said, "Or two."
The woman said, "If only I had said one!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: My son died and I was distraught over him, so I said to the one who was washing him, "Do not wash my son with cold water, for you will kill him."
So ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what she had said, and he smiled, then said:
"May her life be long!"
And we do not know of any woman who lived as long as she lived.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAbbās was in Madinah, so the Anṣār looked for a garment to clothe him in, but they could not find a shirt that fit him except the shirt of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, so they clothed him with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of perfumes is musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed of her illness, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit the poor and ask about them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When she dies, let me know."

But her funeral procession was taken out at night, and they disliked to wake the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the morning, he was told what had happened to her, and he said:
"Did I not command you to inform me of her?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, we disliked to wake you at night."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he lined up the people at her grave and said the takbīr four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a righteous man is placed on his bier, he says, 'Take me forward, take me forward!' And when a man—meaning an evil one—is placed on his bier, he says, 'Woe to me! Where are you taking me?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the funeral of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah, and Ziyād went out walking in front of the bier. Some men from the family of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and their freed slaves began to face the bier and walk backwards, saying, "Slowly, slowly, may Allah bless you."

So they were creeping along slowly, until, when we were on a part of the road at al-Mirbad, Abū Bakrah caught up with us on a mule. When he saw what they were doing, he drove his mule at them and reached toward them with his whip and said, "Make way! By the One who honored the face of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ, I have seen us with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we would almost run at a trot with it." So the people moved on briskly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿīd [and another] said: We never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ attend a funeral and then sit down until it was set down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd said: And ʾIbrāhīm ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq informed us,
he said: Abū Zayd narrated to us,
Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ, who said: Shuʿbah narrated to us,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī al-Safar,
who said: I heard al-Shaʿbī
narrating from Abū Saʿīd,
that a funeral passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he stood up.
And ʿAmr said: A funeral passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he stood up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a funeral appeared, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and those with him stood, and they kept standing until it had passed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿAlī when a funeral passed, and they stood up for it. ʿAlī said, "What is this?" They said, "It is the command of Abū Mūsā."
He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only stood for the funeral of a Jew, and he did not do so again afterward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A funeral passed by al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Ḥasan stood up but Ibn ʿAbbās did not. Al-Ḥasan said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not stand for it?" Ibn ʿAbbās said, "He stood for it, then he sat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A funeral passed by the two of them; one stood and the other sat. The one who stood said, "By Allah, you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood." The one who sat said to him, "You know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [also] sat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī

was sitting when a funeral passed by him, and the people stood until the funeral had gone past. Al-Ḥasan said, "It was only the funeral of a Jew that passed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting on its path, and he disliked that the funeral of a Jew should rise above his head, so he stood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A funeral
passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he stood up. It was said, "It is the funeral of a Jew." He said:
"We only stood for the angels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A deceased person was mentioned badly in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, so he said:
"Do not mention your dead except with good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ri'āb ibn Ḥudhayfah ibn Saʿīd ibn Sahm married Umm Wāʾil bint Maʿmar al-Jumaḥiyyah, and she bore him three children. Their mother then died, and her sons inherited from her her property and the right of patronage over her freed slaves. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ took them out with him to Syria, and they died in the plague of ʿAmwās. ʿAmr inherited from them, as he was their agnate heir. When ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ returned, the sons of Maʿmar came to dispute with him before ʿUmar over the right of patronage of their sister's freed slaves. ʿUmar said, "I will judge between you by what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I heard him say:
'Whatever the child or the father has secured belongs to his agnate heirs, whoever they may be.'"

He said: So he ruled in our favour on that basis and wrote for us a document to that effect, containing the testimony of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Zayd ibn Thābit, and another man. Then, when ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān became caliph, a freed slave of hers died and left two thousand dinars. It reached me that this ruling had been changed, so they took their dispute to Hishām ibn Ismāʿīl, who referred us to ʿAbd al-Malik. We brought him the document of ʿUmar, and he said, "I used to think this was among the rulings about which there is no doubt, and I never thought the matter of the people of Madinah had reached the point that they would doubt this ruling."
So he ruled in our favour on that basis, and we have held to it ever since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the infant cries out at birth, the funeral prayer is offered for him and he inherits."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When Allah intends good for a ruler, He gives him a truthful minister: if he forgets, the minister reminds him, and if he remembers, the minister helps him. And when Allah intends other than that for him, He gives him an evil minister: if he forgets, he does not remind him, and if he remembers, he does not help him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, Allah has placed the truth upon the tongue of ʿUmar, and he speaks by it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Najdah al-Ḥarūrī,

when he rose up during the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr, sent to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about the share of the near relatives: to whom did he think it belonged? He replied, "It is ours, for the near kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ apportioned it to them. ʿUmar offered us something that we considered less than our due, so we refused to accept it. What he offered them was to help their unmarried to marry, to pay the debts of their debtors, and to give to their poor, but he refused to give them more than that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A gift, or a she-camel, was presented to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Have you accepted Islam?" He said, "No." He said:
"I have been forbidden [to accept] the gifts of the polytheists."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to grant him the salt [mine]—Ibn al-Mutawakkil said: the one at Maʾrib—so he granted it to him. When he turned to leave, a man from the gathering said, "Do you know what you have granted him? You have only granted him water that never runs dry."
He said: So it was taken back from him. He also asked him about what may be reserved of the arāk trees, and he said:
"What the hooves cannot reach."
And Ibn al-Mutawakkil said, "The hooves of camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever revives dead land, it belongs to him."

And he mentioned something similar. He said: The one who narrated this hadith to me informed me that two men brought a dispute before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: one of them had planted date palms in the other's land. So he ruled that the land belonged to its owner and ordered the owner of the palms to remove his palms from it.
He said: I saw them, their roots being struck with axes, and they were tall, full-grown palms, until they were removed from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qarībah bint ʿAbd Allāh [reported] that her mother,
Karīmah bint al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr, informed her from Ḍubāʿah bint al-Zubayr,
from al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr,

that he went out one day to al-Baqīʿ, which is the graveyard, to relieve himself. People in those days would not go out to relieve themselves except once every two or three days, and they would pass dung like camels do. Then he entered a ruined place, and while he was sitting there for his need, he saw a rat bring a dinar out of a hole, then go in and bring out another, until it had brought out seventeen dinars. Then it brought out the edge of a red piece of cloth.

Al-Miqdād said: I pulled out the cloth and found a dinar in it, making eighteen dinars. I went out with them until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him about it. I said, "Take the charity due on it, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Take it back; there is no charity due on it. May Allah bless you in it." Then he said:
"Perhaps you put your hand into the hole?"
I said, "No, by the One who honoured you with the truth."
He said: Its last part was not exhausted before he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has people among mankind."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said:
"They are the people of the Qur'an; they are the people of Allah and His chosen ones."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"O Abū Dharr, that you go out in the morning and learn a verse from the Book of Allah is better for you than praying a hundred units of prayer, and that you go out in the morning and learn a chapter of knowledge, whether it is acted upon or not, is better for you than praying a thousand units of prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim, and the one who places knowledge with those who are not worthy of it is like one who puts jewels, pearls and gold on pigs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Whoever comes to this mosque of mine, not coming except for good that he learns or teaches, is in the position of a fighter in the cause of Allah; and whoever comes for anything other than that is in the position of a man looking at the belongings of others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Hold fast to this knowledge before it is taken away, and its being taken away is its being lifted."
He joined his two fingers, the middle finger and the one next to the thumb, like this, and then said:
"The scholar and the learner are partners in reward, and there is no good in the rest of the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out from one of his rooms and entered the mosque, and there were two circles: one reciting the Qur'an and supplicating to Allah, and the other learning and teaching. The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Both are upon good. These are reciting the Qur'an and supplicating to Allah; if He wills He will give them, and if He wills He will withhold. And these are learning and teaching, and I was only sent as a teacher." Then he sat with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Another [narration], which is better in my view than that of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon on the Day of Sacrifice and said:
"Let the one who is present convey to the one who is absent, for perhaps one to whom it is conveyed will retain it better than the one who heard it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah al-Qushayrī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let the one who is present convey to the one who is absent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let those of you who are present convey to those of you who are absent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among the people are some who are keys to good and locks against evil, and among the people are some who are keys to evil and locks against good. So glad tidings to the one at whose hands Allah has placed the keys of good, and woe to the one at whose hands Allah has placed the keys of evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever teaches knowledge will have the reward of the one who acts upon it, without diminishing the reward of the one who acts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best things a man leaves behind after him are three: a righteous child who prays for him, ongoing charity whose reward reaches him, and knowledge that is acted upon after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among the deeds and good works that reach a believer after his death are: knowledge that he taught and spread, a righteous child he left behind, a copy of the Qur'an he left as inheritance, a mosque he built, a house he built for the wayfarer, a river he caused to flow, or charity he gave from his wealth while he was healthy and alive; these reach him after his death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The best charity is that a Muslim man learns knowledge and then teaches it to his Muslim brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On an extremely hot day the Prophet ﷺ passed toward Baqīʿ al-Gharqad, and the people were walking behind him. When he heard the sound of sandals, it weighed upon his heart, so he sat down until he let them go ahead of him, so that nothing of pride would enter his heart.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ walked, his Companions walked in front of him and left his back to the angels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"People will come to you seeking knowledge. When you see them, say to them: 'Welcome, welcome, in accordance with the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,' and teach them."
I said to al-Ḥakam, "What does 'aqnūhum' mean?" He said, "Teach them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥārith [reported] that Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl,
and Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj,
narrated to him from Abū Bakr ibn al-Munkadir, from ʿAmr,
ibn Sulaym, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from his father,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Bathing on Friday is obligatory for every person who has reached puberty, as well as using the siwāk and applying perfume as far as one is able."
except that Bukayr did not mention ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and regarding perfume he said, "even if it is the perfume of a woman."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik; (another chain:) and Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us,
from Mālik ibn Anas,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Friday and said:
"On it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant happens to be standing in prayer, asking Allah for something, except that He gives it to him."
In his narration Qutaybah added: and he gestured with his hand to indicate how short it is.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar, saying: "What do you think about the two rakʿahs before the morning prayer; should I lengthen the recitation in them?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at night two [rakʿahs] at a time, and then pray witr with one rakʿah." He [the narrator] said: I said: "I am not asking you about this."

He said: "You are really stubborn! Will you not let me recount the hadith to you? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray at night two [rakʿahs] at a time and pray witr with one rakʿah, and he would pray two rakʿahs before the morning prayer as if the call to prayer were in his ears."
Khalaf said: "What do you think about the two rakʿahs before the morning," and he did not mention "prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,
from Saʿīd ibn Yasār,

that he said: I was traveling with Ibn ʿUmar on the road to Makkah. Saʿīd said: When I feared the dawn, I dismounted and prayed witr, then caught up with him. Ibn ʿUmar said to me, "Where were you?" I said to him, "I feared the dawn, so I dismounted and prayed witr."
ʿAbdullāh said, "Do you not have an excellent example in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" I said, "Yes, by Allah."
He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr on his camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zughbah, Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ and al-Ḥārith ibn Miskīn, [it being] read to him while I listened,
the wording being his, from Ibn Wahb, from Yūnus,
from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim, from his father,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray voluntary prayers on his mount, in whatever direction it faced, and he would pray witr on it, except that he did not pray the obligatory prayer on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād, Abū
ʿAwānah and Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to them from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd,
from Ibn Masʿūd,

who said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray a prayer except at its proper time, except at Jamʿ [Muzdalifah], where he combined the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers, and prayed the dawn prayer the next morning before its usual time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We mentioned pledging collateral in a salam sale in the presence of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and he said: Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd narrated to us from ʿĀʾishah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought food from a Jew for a fixed term and pledged his iron coat of armor to him as collateral.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Swearing oaths makes goods sell, but wipes out blessing."
Ibn al-Sarḥ said: "[wipes out] earnings."
And he said, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted on the day of Khaybar two shares for the horse and one share for the foot soldier.
He said: Nāfiʿ explained it, saying: If a man has a horse, he gets three shares,
and if he has no horse, he gets one share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed the first prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he went out to his family and I went out with him. Some children met him, and he began to stroke the cheeks of each of them, one by one. As for me, he stroked my cheek too. I found his hand to be cool and fragrant, as though he had just taken it out of a perfumer's container.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to enter the house of Umm Sulaym and sleep on her bed while she was not there. One day he came and slept on her bed. I came, and she was told, "The Prophet ﷺ is sleeping in your house, on your bed." She came, and he had sweated, and his sweat had collected on a piece of leather on the bed. She opened her container and began to wipe up that sweat and wring it into her bottles. The Prophet ﷺ was startled and said,
"What are you doing, Umm Sulaym?"
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, we hope for its blessing for our children." He said, "You have done right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Revelation would come down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a cold morning, and then his forehead would stream with sweat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When revelation came down upon the Prophet ﷺ, he would lower his head, and his Companions would lower their heads. When it had passed from him, he would raise his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at a time when there was no man on the face of the earth who had seen him other than me.
I said to him, "How did you see him?" He said, "He was fair, handsome, and of medium build."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Numayr and ʿAmr al-Nāqid, both from Ibn Idrīs,
ʿAmr said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs al-Awdī narrated to us, from Hishām,
from Ibn Sīrīn,

who said: Anas ibn Mālik was asked, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dye his hair?" He said, "He had seen only a little grey hair"—Ibn Idrīs said, "as if he meant that it was little"—"but Abū Bakr and ʿUmar dyed their hair with henna and katam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He disliked that a man should pluck
a white hair from his head or his beard. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not dye his hair. The whiteness was only in his chin-tuft, at the temples, and a few scattered hairs on his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bashshār, Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Dawraqī, and Hārūn ibn ʿAbdillāh, all from Abū Dāwūd,
Ibn al-Muthannā said: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us,
from Khulayd ibn Jaʿfar,
who heard Abū Iyās, from Anas,
that he was asked about the grey hair of the Prophet
ﷺ, and he said, "Allah did not disfigure him with white hair."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this [chain], but they did not say, "white" or "he had turned grey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The front of the head and the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had become streaked with grey. When he oiled his hair it was not noticeable, and when his hair was disheveled it was noticeable. His beard was thick. A man said, "His face was like a sword." He said, "No, rather it was like the sun and the moon, and it was round." And I saw the seal near his shoulder, like a pigeon's egg, resembling his body.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw a seal on the back of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as if it were a pigeon's egg.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ and ate bread and meat with him—or he said, thareed. I said to him, "Did the Prophet ﷺ ask forgiveness for you?" He said, "Yes, and for you," and then he recited this verse: {And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women.} Then I went around behind him and looked at the seal of prophethood between his shoulders, near the soft part of his left shoulder blade, like a closed fist, with moles on it like warts.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Through both chains, like the hadith of ʿAqīl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿUrwah, "How long did the Prophet ﷺ stay in Makkah?" He said, "Ten years."
I said, "But Ibn ʿAbbās says thirteen or so."
He said, "Allah forgive him," and he said, "He only took it from the words of a poet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, "How old was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day he died?" He said, "I did not think that someone like you from his people would be ignorant of that." I said, "I have asked people and they differed with me, and I wanted to know your view on it."
He said, "Do you count?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "Hold on: he was sent [as a Prophet] at forty; fifteen years in Makkah, in safety and in fear, and ten years from his emigration to Madīnah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah for fifteen years. For seven years he heard a voice and saw a light but saw nothing [else], and for eight years revelation came to him. And he stayed in Madīnah for ten years.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to name himself to us with several names, and he said,
"I am Muḥammad, Aḥmad, al-Muqaffī, al-Ḥāshir, the Prophet of repentance, and the Prophet of mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque, and a man entered and prayed. Then he came and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who returned the greeting and said:
"Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."
So the man went back and prayed as he had prayed before, then came to the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "And upon you be peace." Then he said:
"Go back and pray, for you have not prayed."
He did that three times. Then the man said, "By the One who sent you with the truth, I cannot do better than this, so teach me." He said:

"When you stand up for prayer, say the takbīr, then recite what is easy for you of the Qur'an. Then bow until you are at ease in bowing, then rise until you stand upright, then prostrate until you are at ease in prostration, then sit until you are at ease sitting, then do that throughout all of your prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was [a Companion],
he had companionship [with the Prophet ﷺ], as Muhammad ibn ʿAmr claimed. He said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever neglects the Friday prayer three times out of negligence, Allah seals his heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, in how much time should I recite the Qur'an?" He said, "In a month."
He said, "I am able to do more than that" – Abū Mūsā repeated the words – and he kept reducing it until he said:
"Recite it in seven days."
He said, "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"One who recites it in less than three days does not understand it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Supplication is worship." Then he recited:
"And your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation."
He said: This is a good and authentic hadith.
It was also narrated by Manṣūr and al-Aʿmash from Dharr, and we only know it from the narration of Dharr.
He is Dharr ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Hamdānī, trustworthy, the father of ʿUmar ibn Dharr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked permission of the Prophet ﷺ to perform ʿUmrah, and he gave me permission and said:
"Do not forget us, my brother, in your supplication."
He said a word that I would not exchange for the whole world. Shuʿbah said: Then I met ʿĀṣim afterwards in Medina and he narrated it to me, and he said:
"Include us, my brother, in your supplication."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Wakīʿ,
and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī,
said: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Salamah ibn Kuhayl,
from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: When you have thrown the Jamrah, everything becomes lawful for you except women.
A man said to him, "O Ibn ʿAbbās, and perfume?" He said, "As for me, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smearing his head with musk. Is that perfume or not?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ, and from ʿIkrimah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
they both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no marriage without a guardian."
And in the hadith of ʿĀʾishah:
"And the ruler is the guardian of one who has no guardian."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ – and ʿAmr said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – had divorced Ḥafṣah, then took her back. And Allah knows best.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the fetus [found in a slaughtered animal], and he said:
"Eat it if you wish."
Musaddad said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we slaughter the she-camel, the cow and the sheep, and find a fetus in its belly. Should we throw it away or eat it?" He said:
"Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no faraʿ and no ʿatīrah."
Ibn Mājah said: This is among the singular narrations of al-ʿAdanī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Ḥabīb, Yūnus, and Qatādah,
from Muhammad ibn Sīrīn,
from Salmān ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḍabbī,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"For a boy there is the ʿaqīqah, so shed blood [of an animal] for him and remove harm from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a woman was nursing her son, a rider passed by her as she nursed him,
and she said, "O Allah, do not let my son die until he is like this one."
The child said, "O Allah, do not make me like him."
Then he returned to the breast.
Then [the child] passed by a woman who was being dragged along and mocked, and [his mother] said, "O Allah, do not make my son like her."
The child said, "O Allah, make me like her."
He said: As for the rider, he is a disbeliever;
and as for the woman, they say to her, "You commit fornication,"
and she says, "Allah is sufficient for me." And they say, "You steal,"
and she says, "Allah is sufficient for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the plague, and he said:
"It was a punishment that Allah would send upon whomever He willed,
then Allah made it a mercy for the believers.
There is no servant who is in a land where it has broken out, and remains in it,
not leaving that land, patient and seeking reward from Allah,
knowing that nothing will befall him except what Allah has written for him,
except that he will have a reward like that of a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both.
[Regarding the verse] {And We made you into peoples and tribes}, he said: The peoples are the large tribes, and the tribes are the sub-tribes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ Zaynab, the daughter of Abū Salamah. He said: I said to her, "Tell me, was the Prophet ﷺ from Muḍar?" She said, "From whom else would he be, if not from Muḍar? He was from the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Narrated, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"From here came the trials"—pointing toward the east—
"and harshness and hardness of hearts are among the loud-voiced herdsmen, the people of camel-hair tents, at the base of the tails of camels,
and cattle, in Rabīʿah and Muḍar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Boasting and arrogance are among the loud-voiced herdsmen, the people of camel-hair tents,
and tranquility is among the people of sheep and goats. Faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."
Yemen was named so because it lies to the right of the Kaʿbah,
and Syria lies to the left of the Kaʿbah. Al-mashāmah means the left side,
and the left hand is called ash-shuʾmā,
and the left side is called al-ashʾam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim used to relate that word reached Muʿāwiyah, while he was with him among a delegation of Quraysh, that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ was saying that a king would arise from Qaḥṭān, and Muʿāwiyah became angry.
He stood and praised Allah as He deserves,
then said: To proceed: It has reached me that some men among you are relating narrations that are not in the Book of Allah
and are not reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Those are the ignorant among you.
So beware of wishful fancies that lead their people astray,
for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"This matter [of leadership] belongs to Quraysh.
No one opposes them except that Allah throws him down on his face,
as long as they uphold the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr went with some people from Banū Zuhrah to ʿĀʾishah,
and she was the most tender-hearted of people toward them because of their kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said, concerning] a sale or a gift that ʿĀʾishah had given: "By Allah, ʿĀʾishah must stop this,
or I will place a restriction on her."
She said, "Did he say this?" They said, "Yes."
She said, "I vow to Allah
that I will never speak to Ibn al-Zubayr."
Ibn al-Zubayr sought intercession with her
when the estrangement had grown long, but she said, "No, by Allah, I will never accept intercession for him,
and I will not break my vow."
When this became long for Ibn al-Zubayr, he spoke to al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth,
who were from Banū Zuhrah,
and said to them, "I ask you by Allah to bring me in to ʿĀʾishah,
for it is not lawful for her to vow to cut me off."
So al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came with him, wrapped in their cloaks, and asked permission to enter upon ʿĀʾishah. They said, "Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.
May we enter?" ʿĀʾishah said, "Enter."
They said, "All of us?" She said, "Yes, enter, all of you."
She did not know that Ibn al-Zubayr was with them.
When they entered, Ibn al-Zubayr went in behind the screen,
embraced ʿĀʾishah, and began to plead with her and weep,
and al-Miswar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān began to implore her to speak to him and accept his apology,
saying, "The Prophet ﷺ forbade what you know of forsaking one another,
for it is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three nights."
When they had reminded her and pressed her much, she began to remind them of her vow and weep, saying, "I made a vow, and a vow is a serious matter."
They kept at her until she spoke to Ibn al-Zubayr,
and she freed forty slaves in expiation of that vow.
After that she would remember her vow and weep
until her tears wet her head-covering.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the greatest of lies is that a man claims to be the son of someone other than his father,
or claims that his eyes saw what they did not see,
or attributes to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he did not say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that she was pregnant with ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr in Makkah. She said: I set out while I was at full term,
and I came to Madīnah and stayed at Qubāʾ, and I gave birth at Qubāʾ.
Then I brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and placed him in his lap.
Then he called for a date and chewed it,
then he put some of his saliva into the child's mouth, so the first thing to enter his stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he rubbed his palate with the date,
then he made supplication for him and blessed him.
He was the first child born in Islam,
and they rejoiced over him greatly,
because they had been told: The Jews have bewitched you, so no children will be born to you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with Abū Bakr when he first arrived in Madīnah, and there was ʿĀʾishah, his daughter, lying down, struck by a fever. Abū Bakr came to her and said to her, "How are you, my little daughter?" and he kissed her cheek.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If ten of the Jews were to follow me, not a single Jew would remain on the face of the earth except that he would accept Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced the House and invoked [Allah's curse] against six men of Quraysh,
among them Abū Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah, and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. I swear by Allah that I saw them lying slain at Badr,
the sun having changed their appearance, and it was a hot day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Badr:
"Who will look to see what has become of Abū Jahl?"
So Ibn Masʿūd went,
and found that the two sons of ʿAfrāʾ had struck him until he was cold [near death].
He said, "Are you Abū Jahl?" Ibn ʿUlayyah said: Sulaymān said: This is how Anas said it.
He said, "Are you Abū Jahl?" He replied, "Is there anyone above a man you have killed?" Sulaymān said: or he said, "[A man] his own people killed."
He said: And Abū Mijlaz said: Abū Jahl said, "If only it had been someone other than a farmer who killed me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was mentioned in the presence of ʿĀʾishah that Ibn ʿUmar
attributes to the Prophet ﷺ [the saying]:
"The dead person is punished in his grave because of his family's weeping over him."
So she said: He has made a mistake. Rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is being punished for his sin or his wrongdoing, while his family are weeping over him now."
And that is like his report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at the well on the day of Badr, in which were those of the polytheists slain at Badr, and said to them what he said:
"They hear what I say."
But he has erred. Rather, he said:
"They now know that what I used to tell them was the truth."
Then she recited: {Indeed, you do not make the dead hear} and {you cannot make those in the graves hear}, [meaning] when they take their seats in the Fire.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jibrīl came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
"How do you regard those who fought at Badr among you?" He said, "As among the best of the Muslims," or a similar statement. He said, "And likewise those of the angels who witnessed Badr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī
returned from a journey, and his family presented him with meat from the sacrificial animals. He said, "I will not eat it until I ask."

So he went to his maternal brother Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān, who was a Badr veteran, and asked him about that. He said, "A new ruling came after you left, abrogating what they had been forbidden, namely eating the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That is, Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar was widowed from Khunays ibn Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī, who was among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and died in Madīnah. ʿUmar said: I went to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, and proposed Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar to him. I said, "If you wish, I will marry Ḥafṣah to you."
He said, "I will consider my matter." I waited some nights, then he met me and said, "It has become clear to me that I should not marry at this time."
ʿUmar said: Then I met Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, and said, "If you wish, I will marry Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar to you."

Abū Bakr stayed silent and gave me no reply at all, and I was more upset with him than I had been with ʿUthmān. I waited some nights, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her and I married her to him. Then Abū Bakr met me and said, "Perhaps you were upset with me when you proposed Ḥafṣah to me and I gave you no reply."
ʿUmar said: I said, "Yes."

He said, "Nothing prevented me from replying to you about what you offered me except that I knew the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her, and I would not disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left her, I would have accepted her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the governorship of Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr, [I was asked]: Are the two who have exchanged oaths of condemnation to be separated? I did not know what to say, so I got up from where I was and went to the house of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar and asked permission to enter. I was told that he was taking his midday rest.
He heard my voice and said, "Ibn Jubayr, come in. You have only come for some need."
He said: So I entered, and he was reclining on the saddle-cloth of his riding saddle.

I said, "Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, are the two who have exchanged oaths of condemnation to be separated?" He said, "Glory be to Allah! Yes. The first to ask about that was so-and-so, son of so-and-so. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'Messenger of Allah, what do you think if one of us found his wife committing an indecency, what should he do? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter; and if he stays silent, he stays silent over a grave matter.'"
He said: The Prophet ﷺ remained silent and did not answer him. Later, the man came to the Prophet ﷺ again and said, "What I asked you about, I have been tried with it myself."
So Allah revealed these verses in Sūrat al-Nūr:

"And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves..." until he completed the verses. So he called the man, recited the verses to him, admonished him, reminded him, and told him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter.
The man said, "No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I have not lied about her."

Then he turned to the woman, admonished her, reminded her, and told her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said, "No, by the One who sent you with the truth, he has not spoken the truth."
He said: So he began with the man, who testified four times by Allah that he was among the truthful, and a fifth time that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was among the liars.
Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four times by Allah that he was among the liars, and a fifth time that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was among the truthful.
Then he separated them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He went out with the Prophet ﷺ to the place of prayer and saw the people trading with one another. He said:
"O assembly of merchants!"
They responded to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and raised their necks and their eyes toward him. Then he said:
"Merchants will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as wicked sinners, except those who fear Allah, are dutiful, and are truthful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had two Qatarī cloaks, and when he sat and sweated in them they became heavy on him. A Jewish man, so-and-so, had received cloth from Syria. I said, "If only you would send for him and buy two garments from him on credit until a time of ease."
So he sent for him, and the man said, "I know what Muḥammad wants. He only wants to take my wealth, or take the two garments [without paying]."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He has lied. He knows that I am among the most God-fearing of them and the most faithful in fulfilling trusts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAddāʾ ibn Khālid ibn Hawdhah said to me, "Shall I not read to you a document that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote for me?"
I said, "Yes."
So he brought out a document for me, and in it was:

"This is what al-ʿAddāʾ ibn Khālid ibn Hawdhah bought from Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he bought from him a male slave or a female slave, with no defect, no vice, and no immorality—the sale of a Muslim to a Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two animals for one is not valid on credit, but there is no harm in it hand to hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me two young slave boys who were brothers, and I sold one of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"ʿAlī, what has become of your boy?" I told him, and he said, "Take him back! Take him back!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you passes by a garden wall, let him eat, but not carry any away in the fold of his garment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever seeks the office of judge and asks for intercessors for it will be left to himself; and whoever is forced into it, Allah will send down an angel to him who will guide him aright."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah is with the judge so long as he does not act unjustly; when he acts unjustly, He abandons him and Satan attaches himself to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulaymān ibn Hishām asked me about the ʿumrā [a lifetime gift],
so I said: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn narrated from Shurayḥ,
who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ ruled that the ʿumrā is permissible.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of what you eat is from your own earnings, and your children are part of your earnings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever kills intentionally is handed over to the guardians of the slain: if they wish they may kill him, and if they wish they may take the blood-money. That is thirty ḥiqqah camels, thirty jadhaʿah camels, and forty pregnant she-camels; that is the blood-money for intentional killing. Whatever they agree upon by settlement is theirs. And that is the stricter blood-money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was never asked for anything and said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears by a religion other than Islam [falsely] is as he has said.
A son of Adam has no vow [to fulfil] concerning what he does not own.
Whoever kills himself with something in this world will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection.
Whoever curses a believer, it is like killing him,
and whoever accuses a believer of disbelief, it is like killing him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man passed by Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, and it was said to him, "This man reports to the rulers what people say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most untrue of speech. Do not spy, do not search for faults, do not compete with one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn away from one another. Be servants of Allah, brothers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: All of my Ummah will be pardoned except those who publicize [their sins]. Part of such publicizing is that a servant does a deed at night, and in the morning, though his Lord has concealed it, he says, 'O so-and-so, last night I did such and such.' He had spent the night with his Lord concealing it, then he spends the morning uncovering the concealment of Allah." Zuhayr said:
"And part of it is al-hijār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Any slave woman of the people of Madinah would take the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would not withdraw his hand from hers until she had taken him wherever she wished in Madinah for her need.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No one is more patient than Allah, the Exalted, in the face of harmful words he hears. They ascribe to Him a rival and ascribe to Him a child, yet despite that He provides for them, grants them well-being, and gives to them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did something and allowed it as a concession. That reached some of his Companions, and it was as if they disliked it and kept away from it. When this reached him, he stood to give a speech and said:

"What is the matter with men to whom word has reached of something I did as a concession, and they dislike it and keep away from it? By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of them about Allah and the most fearful of Him among them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I had covered [a shelf] with a curtain bearing images. When he saw it, his face changed colour, then he tore it down with his hand and said:
"Indeed, the people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate the creation of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some guests of ours came to us. He said: My father used to talk with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night. He said: So he left and said, "O ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, take care of your guests."

He said: When evening came, we brought their food. He said: But they refused and said, "Not until the master of our house comes and eats with us." He said: I said to them, "He is a man of sharp temper, and if you do not do so I fear I will be harmed by him." He said: But they refused. When he came, he began with nothing before them and said, "Have you finished with your guests?" They said, "No, by Allah, we have not finished."
He said, "Did I not order ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān?" He said: I kept away from him, and he said, "O ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān!"

He said: So I kept away. He said: Then he said, "O worthless one! I adjure you, if you hear my voice, to come!" He said: So I came and said, "By Allah, I am not at fault. These are your guests, so ask them. I brought them their food, but they refused to eat until you came." He said: Then he said, "What is the matter with you, that you do not accept your food from us?" He said: Abū Bakr said, "By Allah, I will not eat it tonight." He said: They said, "By Allah, we will not eat it until you eat it."

He said: I never saw an evil like that night. He said, "Woe to you! What is wrong with you, that you do not accept your food from us?" Then he said, "The first [oath] was from Satan. Bring your food." He said: So the food was brought, he mentioned Allah's name and ate, and they ate. He said: When morning came, he went early to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, they kept their oaths and I broke mine." He said: He informed him, and he said:
"Rather, you are the most dutiful of them and the best of them."
He said: And no expiation has reached me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came upon his wives while a driver named Anjashah was driving them along, and he said:
"Woe to you, Anjashah! Gently! [You are] driving glass vessels."
He said: Abū Qilābah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke a word which, had one of you said it, you would have held it against him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he asked his uncle about prayer,
whether anything interrupts it. He said, "Nothing interrupts it."
ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stand and pray at night,
while I was lying across [the space] between him and the qiblah, on the bed of his family."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAṭāʾ, "Did you hear Ibn ʿAbbās say: 'You were only commanded to circumambulate [the House]; you were not commanded to enter it'?"

He said, "He did not forbid entering it, but I heard him say: Usāmah ibn Zayd informed me that when the Prophet ﷺ entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners and did not pray in it until he came out. When he came out, he prayed two rakʿahs facing the front of the House, and said, 'This is the qiblah.'"
I said to him, "What are its corners? In its angles?" He said, "Rather, in every direction of the House."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved to be directed toward the Kaʿbah,
so Allah revealed: "We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven," and he turned toward the Kaʿbah.

The foolish among the people, meaning the Jews, said, "What has turned them away from the qiblah they were following?" [Allah said:] "Say: To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path." A man prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, then left after he had prayed,
and passed by some people of the Anṣār who were praying the ʿAṣr prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis. He said, bearing witness, that he had prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and that he had turned toward the Kaʿbah.
So the people turned around until they were facing the Kaʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When any of you prays, he is conversing privately with his Lord, so let him not spit to his right,
but beneath his left foot."
Saʿīd said, from Qatādah: "Let him not spit in front of him or before him,
but to his left or beneath his feet."
Shuʿbah said: "Let him not spit in front of him or to his right,
but to his left or beneath his foot."
Ḥumayd said, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"Let him not spit toward the qiblah or to his right,
but to his left or beneath his foot."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a cavalry force toward Najd, and they brought a man from Banū Ḥanīfah called Thumāmah ibn Uthāl, the chief of the people of al-Yamāmah.
They tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to him and said:
"What do you have [to say], Thumāmah?"

He said, "I have good, Muhammad. If you kill, you kill a man of blood [guilt]; if you show favor, you show favor to one who is grateful; and if you want wealth, ask and you will be given as much of it as you wish."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left him until the day after next, then said:
"What do you have, Thumāmah?"

He said, "What I told you: if you show favor, you show favor to one who is grateful; if you kill, you kill a man of blood [guilt]; and if you want wealth, ask and you will be given as much of it as you wish."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left him until the following day, then said:
"What do you have, Thumāmah?"

He said, "What I told you: if you show favor, you show favor to one who is grateful; if you kill, you kill a man of blood [guilt]; and if you want wealth, ask and you will be given as much of it as you wish."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Release Thumāmah."

He went to a palm grove near the mosque and bathed, then entered the mosque and said, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.

O Muhammad, by Allah, there was no face on earth more hateful to me than your face, and now your face has become the most beloved of all faces to me. By Allah, there was no religion more hateful to me than your religion, and now your religion has become the most beloved of all religions to me. By Allah, there was no town more hateful to me than your town, and now your town has become the most beloved of all towns to me. Your cavalry seized me while I was intending ʿUmrah; what do you think?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him glad tidings and commanded him to perform ʿUmrah. When he came to Makkah, someone said to him, "Have you abandoned your religion?" He said, "No, but I have embraced Islam with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And no, by Allah, not a grain of wheat will come to you from al-Yamāmah until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permits it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are no days in which it is more beloved to Allah that He be worshipped than the ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Fasting each day of them equals fasting a year, and standing in prayer on each night of them equals standing in prayer on the Night of Qadr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: At al-Rabadhah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"If you fast any part of the month, then fast the thirteenth, the fourteenth, and the fifteenth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and passed by a man. They said: "O Prophet of Allah, this man has not broken his fast since such and such a time." He said:
"He has neither fasted nor broken his fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She is called Laylā, from Umm ʿUmārah.
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, and we brought food near to him. Some of those with him were fasting, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When food is eaten in the presence of a person who is fasting, the angels send blessings upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever stays with a people should not observe a voluntary fast except with their permission."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever gives a fasting person something with which to break his fast will have a reward like his, without anything being reduced from the reward of the fasting person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stood up before the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what makes Hajj obligatory?" He said: "Provision and a mount."
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the pilgrim?" He said: "The one who is disheveled and unperfumed."
Another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Hajj?" He said: "Raising the voice [in talbiyah] and shedding blood [in sacrifice]."
Wakīʿ said: By "raising the voice" he means raising the voice with the talbiyah, and by "shedding blood" the sacrifice of the camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When [the verse] was revealed: "And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people—whoever is able to find a way to it," they said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He remained silent.
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He said:
"No. Had I said yes, it would have become obligatory." So Allah revealed:
"O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made plain to you, would distress you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ began the talbiyah [for Hajj] right after prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The two of them
were discussing performing ʿUmrah followed by Hajj [tamattuʿ]. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays said: "No one does that except one who is ignorant of the command of Allah."
Saʿd said: "What a terrible thing you have said, O son of my brother."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays said: "But ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb forbade it."
Saʿd said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did it, and we did it with him."
He said: This is a sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no Muslim who recites the talbiyah but that everything to his right or to his left responds with talbiyah, whether stone, tree, or clod of earth, until the earth ends on this side and on that side."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ on a Hajj or an ʿUmrah, and a swarm of locusts, or a kind of locust, came toward us. We began striking them with our whips and sandals. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Eat it, for it is from the game of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Mecca, he entered the Mosque and touched the Black Stone. Then he proceeded to his right, walking briskly for three rounds and walking normally for four. Then he came to the Station [of Ibrāhīm] and said:

"And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer." He prayed two rakʿahs with the Station between him and the House. Then after the two rakʿahs he came to the Stone and touched it. Then he went out to al-Ṣafā. I think he said: "Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to the people of Mecca with [the declaration of] Barāʾah. He said:
"What were you proclaiming?"
He said: We were proclaiming:

"No one will enter Paradise except a believing soul; no one may circumambulate the House naked; whoever has a treaty between himself and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, its term or period is extended to four months; and when the four months have passed, Allah and His Messenger are free of [obligation to] the polytheists; and no polytheist may perform Hajj after this year."
I kept proclaiming until my voice became hoarse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ left me while his eyes were cool [with contentment] and his soul at ease. Then he returned to me sorrowful. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you left me with your eyes content, and you have returned sorrowful." He said:
"I entered the Kaʿbah, and I wish I had not done so. I fear that I have burdened my Ummah after me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a man among the Anṣār called Abū Shuʿayb,
and he had a slave who was a butcher. He said, "Prepare a meal for me, for I want to invite the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the fifth of five."
So he invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the fifth of five,
and a man followed them. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"You invited us as the fifth of five, and this man has followed us.
If you wish, you may permit him [to enter],
and if you wish, I will leave him."
He said, "Rather, I permit him."

Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl say: When people are at a dining spread, they should not pass food from one spread to another; rather, they may pass it to one another at that same spread, or leave it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ. [Another chain:] And Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Hamdānī narrated to us,
and the wording is his, Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from Burayd,
from Abū Burdah,
from Abū Mūsā,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"The likeness of a good companion and a bad companion is only that of a musk-seller and a blacksmith's bellows-blower. As for the musk-seller, either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find a pleasant fragrance from him. As for the one who blows the bellows, either he will burn your clothes, or you will find a foul smell from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Ṭaybah performed cupping on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that he be given a ṣāʿ of dates,
and he ordered his masters to lighten his daily payment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped and gave the cupper his wage; had he known it to be vile, he would not have given it to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar saw ʿUṭārid at-Tamīmī displaying a silk-striped garment for sale in the market—he was a man who frequented kings and received gifts from them—so ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw ʿUṭārid displaying a silk-striped garment in the market. If only you would buy it and wear it for the delegations of the Arabs when they come to you"—and I think he said, "and wear it on Friday." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"Only one who has no share in the Hereafter wears silk in this world."

Then some time later, silk-striped garments were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He sent one garment to ʿUmar, sent one garment to Usāmah ibn Zayd, and gave one garment to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and he said,
"Tear it into head-coverings for the women of your household."
He said: ʿUmar came carrying his garment and said, "O Messenger of Allah, you sent this to me, yet yesterday you said about ʿUṭārid's garment what you said." He said,
"I did not send it to you for you to wear, but I sent it to you so that you might benefit from it."

As for Usāmah, he went out in his garment, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at him in a way that made him realize that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disapproved of what he had done. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do you look at me like that, when you yourself sent it to me?" He said,
"I did not send it to you for you to wear, but I sent it to you so that you might tear it into head-coverings for the women of your household."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah,

that she bought a cushion with pictures on it. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he stood at the door and did not enter. She recognized the dislike in his face and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I repent to Allah and to His Messenger. What sin have I committed?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"What is this cushion?"
She said, "I bought it for you to sit on and to recline on."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The makers of these pictures will be punished, and it will be said to them: 'Bring to life what you have created.'" Then he said,
"Angels do not enter a house in which there are pictures."
label: machine translation
